speaker: The Wanderer
before: Ugh... Where am I? Who am I?
after: Ugh... where am I? And while I'm asking, who am I?

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I search for my name. For how I got here. But I find nothing.
after: I keep reaching for my name, or for how I got here, and there's nothing there at all.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I try to rise, but I am weak. A low groan escapes my mouth.
after: I should get up. My legs have other ideas, and every part of me aches.

speaker: (narration)
before: A cold draft rises from the dark. It smells of old stone and older water. The stranger said the town is on the other side. Go in?
after: A cold draft rises out of the dark, smelling of old stone and older water. The stranger said the town lies on the other side. Go in?

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Easy. Stay down. Gather what strength you have. I can't imagine it's much after what they put you through.
after: Easy. Stay down a moment and get your breath back. After what they put you through, I'm amazed you're breathing at all.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Keep your voice low. We are not the only ones in these woods tonight.
after: And keep your voice low. We're not the only ones in these woods tonight.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I don't know this place. I don't know my own name. ...Who are you?
after: I don't know this place, and I don't know my own name. ...Who are you?

speaker: The Rescuer
before: A friend. That's all I can say. There isn't much time.
after: A friend. That's all I can tell you, and there isn't time for more.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Can you still fight, still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand.
after: Can you still draw on the Paths? Hold out your hand and let me see.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: That will have to do. The Path-ologists are hunting us.
after: Faint will have to do. The Path-ologists are already hunting us.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: That one, then. Cling to it. Hopefully you can walk the others again soon.
after: That one, then. Hold on to it. The others will come back to you, in time.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Behind me is the Forgotten Cave. Follow it all the way through to {town}. Elder Maren will be waiting for you. Find her first.
after: The Forgotten Cave is just behind me, and it comes out at {town}. Elder Maren will be waiting for you on the other side. Find her before you do anything else.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: Hear that? They're close, but they don't know about this place. Few do.
after: Hear that? They're close, but they don't know about the cave. Hardly anyone remembers it now.

speaker: The Rescuer
before: You must escape. I'll draw them off the other way. I'll find you if I make it out.
after: Go, and don't stop for anything. I'll draw them off the other way, and when I'm clear, I'll find you. I always do.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: She's gone, and she's leading them away. By the sound of their shouting, I do not want to be caught by them.
after: She's gone, and she's taking the shouting with her. Whoever they are, I'd rather not meet them.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: The trees are too dense to pass through. To the cave.
after: The trees are packed too tight to get through. The cave it is, then.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: No point getting lost twice in one day. Back up the path to the glowing arch.
after: No point getting lost twice in one day. I'll head back up the path to the glowing arch.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Whoever that was said help would be waiting on the other side. Whatever is inside the cave seems like a better option than those Path-ologists.
after: Whoever she was, she said help would be waiting on the other side. Whatever's in that cave, it has to be better than those Path-ologists.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: ...Hm. Woken from my slumber.
after: ...Footsteps. It has been a long time since anything woke me.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: It has been some time since anyone has walked this path.
after: No one has walked this way since the house fell silent. I have kept the door all the same.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: No matter. Only one may pass, and he is long dead.
after: Turn back. Only one may pass this door, and he is long dead.

speaker: Hollow Warden
before: I shall perform my duty.
after: Then I will do what I was left here to do.

speaker: Hollow Warden
before: What is that I sense in you? NO! You are not HIM!
after: ...That light in your hands. I know it. No. NO. You cannot be him. He is gone.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: Let the Paths guide you.
after: ...The door knows your hand. I do not understand it, but I will not stand against it. Pass, and let the Paths guide you.

speaker: The Hollow Warden
before: The light drains from the Warden's eyes.
after: The light goes out of the Warden's eyes slowly, like a lamp turned down for the night.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Hmph... about time you showed up. {villain}'s soldiers have been out and about today.
after: Hmph. About time. {villain}'s soldiers have been up and down the road all day, and nobody has come out of that cave in ten years, so forgive me for staring.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And look at the state of you! I said I'd help whoever she sends along, not take in a stray.
after: And look at the state of you. I told her I'd help whoever she sent along. I never said I'd take in a half-drowned stray.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I don't love being wrapped up in this. I told her not to go through with whatever she has planned.
after: I didn't want any part of this, and I told her so. She went ahead anyway. She always does.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: But a body in that state needs a bed, and I have far too much pie. I can't just leave you out on your own, now can I?
after: But you need a bed, and I've baked far too much pie, so I can hardly leave you out here on your own, can I?

speaker: The Wanderer
before: ...I don't remember who I am, or where I am. I don't even know who rescued me.
after: I don't know who I am, or where this is. I don't even know the name of the woman who got me out.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Hm. Well if you don't know then I'm not telling. There must be a reason she didn't give you her name. As for here, this is {town}. We solve everything here with cards. It looks like you already have a deck.
after: Hm. If she didn't give you her name, she had a reason, and I won't be the one to spoil it. As for where you are: this is {town}. We settle most things here with cards, and I see you've already got a deck.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: If you really don't remember anything, you might be here awhile. You should get acquainted with the townsfolk. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, and buy a card from Sable. Then come back.
after: If your memory's really gone, you'll be here a while, so you'd best get to know people. Say hello to Sable, Tilly and Pip on the square, buy yourself a card from Sable, then come back to me.

speaker: (narration)
before: Beside you kneels someone hooded. They nudge you gently, then not so gently. You look up but cannot make out their face.
after: Someone in a hood is kneeling beside you, shaking your shoulder gently, then less gently. Their face stays in shadow.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant.
after: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant TO the Regional Merchant. The TO is load-bearing.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Fact: the beets came in early this year. The bear has been informed. We have an understanding. I do not ask why it is here.
after: Fact: the beets came in early this year, and the bear has been informed. We have an understanding. I do not ask why it is here, and it does not ask about the beets.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I don't know who you are, but I can't turn away someone in need. And you are definitely in need.
after: I still don't know what to make of you, dearie. But you need feeding more than you need questioning, so sit down a minute.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You can have as much pie as you like, but don't go stealing my recipe.
after: Have as much pie as you like. Just keep your eyes off the recipe; better people than you have tried.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I sense something within you that wasn't there before. I trust the Paths to guide you.
after: That tune's stayed with you, hasn't it? I can see it on your face. Good. Keep it somewhere safe, dearie, even when it hurts.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Have you found answers to any of your questions? I can't deny, I am intrigued despite my better judgment.
after: Found any more answers out there? I keep telling myself it's none of my business, and I keep asking anyway.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Somebody in the square says you have a look of the old court about you. That is no prince, I told them. That is a damp young man with good posture.
after: Somebody in the square says you've a look of the old court about you. 'That's no prince,' I told them. 'That's a damp young man with good posture.'

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And if you meet Wren in the Capital, tell her my pie is still the best thing in the kingdom. She'll argue. She'll be wrong.
after: When you find Wren in the Capital, tell her my pie is still the best thing in the kingdom. She'll argue, and she'll be wrong.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Go on, dearie, the next zone won't free itself. At my pace, we'd have to outlive the regime.
after: Go on, dearie. The next road won't open itself, and if we left it to me, we'd be at it until the regime died of old age.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Go on, the kingdom is waiting. The pie has less patience.
after: Go on, then. The kingdom has waited ten years for you; the pie won't wait ten minutes.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Sit. When you are ready, the memories will come, and I will be here. With pie. Obviously.
after: Sit down. The rest of your memories will come when they're ready, and I'll be right here when they do. With pie, obviously.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes made the energy, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead, Refusemancers hauled the waste and grew the crops. Everyone complained. Everything worked.
after: Ten years ago {kingdom} was whole. Beefcakes kept the lights on, Gourmands fed us, Necrocrats minded the dead and Refusemancers turned rubbish into harvests. Everyone complained, and everything worked.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Then {villain} took the Paths, one by one, and set his rulers over them. Every road out of town has a gatekeeper now: a bridge, a barrier, a pantry door, a wall of thorns.
after: Then {villain}, the Minister of Improvements, took the Paths one by one and set his own people over them. Now every road out of town has a gatekeeper: a bridge, a barrier, a pantry door, a wall of thorns.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Beat a gatekeeper and its road opens. Buy cards from Sable, fix your deck at the Deck Station, and come back to me for pie. Not answers. Pie.
after: Beat a road's gatekeeper and that road opens. Before you try, buy a few cards from Sable and sort your deck at the Deck Station. Then come back to me for pie. Pie, mind. Not answers.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The roads are waiting, dearie: the Gainlands, the Buffet, the D.N.A. and the Dump. One zone at a time.
after: Four roads out of town, dearie: the Gainlands, the Buffet, the D.N.A. and the Dump. Pick one and see it through before you start the next.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You could still be anyone's spy. I have been wrong about people before. Once. In 1987.
after: For all I know, you're somebody's spy. I've been wrong about people before. Once, in 1987.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Still here, dearie? {villain} would love you to sit by my fire forever. Don't give him the satisfaction. Give me back my chair.
after: Still here, dearie? {villain} would like nothing better than you sitting by my fire forever, so don't give him the satisfaction. And give me back my chair.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The pie on the sill is cooling, dearie. Unlike you, it knows when to wait.
after: The pie on the sill needs another hour, dearie. You don't. Off you go.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Off you go, dearie; I'll be here. I'm dependable at a speed you can barely measure.
after: Off you go, dearie. I'll be here when you get back. Tortoises are very dependable, just not quickly.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Gate stays open. Always is. My girl's still up that road somewhere. In case.
after: Gate stays open. Always has. My girl's still up that road somewhere, and I'd hate for her to come home and find it shut.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Hm. That road. The Capital. You want to know why nobody comes back.
after: Hm. That road goes to the Capital. You'll be wanting to know why nobody comes back from it.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Four Paths kept that city alive. Beefcakes ran the lights, Gourmands the kitchens, Necrocrats the graveyards, Refusemancers the bins. {villain} chained all four.
after: Four Paths kept that city alive. Beefcakes ran the lights, Gourmands the kitchens, Necrocrats the graveyards, Refusemancers the bins. Then {villain} chained all four.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: You could walk in today. You would not walk far. Free the four zones: each one you free turns one service back on.
after: You could walk in today, but you wouldn't get far. Free the four zones first. Each one you free turns one of those services back on.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Hm. Services still broken. Count them on the board by the road.
after: Hm. Services still broken up there. The board by the road keeps count, if you want to check.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Hm, each freed zone restores a service and makes the castle less frightening. My knees remain a local problem.
after: Hm. Each zone you free turns another service back on, and the castle gets a little less frightening. My knees, sadly, are a local problem.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Go on. Knock on that castle door. Hard. And if you see Isla... I'm still watching the road.
after: Go on, knock on that castle door, and knock hard. And if you see Isla up there... tell her I'm still watching the road.

speaker: Sable
before: You start with plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable, dull. The Paths are where the power is. Buy some, then put them to work at the Deck Station.
after: Your deck's all plain neutral cards, darling: honest, dependable and dull. The power is in the Paths. Buy a few, then put them to work at the Deck Station.

speaker: Sable
before: Where do my cards come from? The past. Next question. My prices are fair, mostly. {villain}'s taxes are not.
after: Where do my cards come from? The past, darling. Next question. My prices are fair, more or less; {villain}'s taxes on them are not.

speaker: The Store Room Ghosts
before: Ninety years ago the three of us bought one lantern between us. It never worked. Tilly's great-grandmother said: no receipt, no refund.
after: Ninety years ago the three of us went halves - well, thirds - on one lantern, and it never worked. Tilly's great-grandmother said no receipt, no refund.

speaker: The Store Room Ghosts
before: A FAULTY lantern. Four copper. With ninety years' interest, it is still four copper. We did the maths. We had time.
after: A FAULTY lantern, for four copper. We worked out ninety years' interest and it's still four copper. We had the time.

speaker: The Store Room Ghosts
before: Nobody comes in until it is refunded. Or until somebody beats us at cards. Everyone settles everything with cards round here.
after: Nobody comes in until it's refunded, or until somebody beats us at cards. That's how everything gets settled round here, living or otherwise.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Halt. Equipment is issued on referral only. Security Protocol Two. Elder Maren does the referring.
after: Halt. Security Protocol Two. Equipment is issued on referral only, and Elder Maren does the referring.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Elder Maren sent you. I could tell from your gait. It says 'referred'. Congratulations: your file is now thick enough to be a file.
after: Elder Maren sent you; I could tell from your gait, which now says 'referred'. Congratulations. Your file is finally thick enough to be a file.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Before I issue gear, protocol asks for exactly one thing: win a fight. Any fight. Any win counts. I will know.
after: Before I issue gear, protocol requires exactly one thing: win a fight. Any fight counts, and I will know if you lie.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Fact: things roam the edges of town. The outskirts, round the lanes. They are rude and they are close.
after: Fact: things roam the outskirts, on the lanes round the edge of town. They are rude, they are close, and they are not on my referral list.

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Security Protocol Four: check the outskirts. Enemies roam the edges of town. Any win counts.
after: Security Protocol Four: check the outskirts. Enemies roam the lanes round the edge of town, and any win counts.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Press C. Click the Weapon slot on the figure. Choose the blade. Press Equip. Four steps. I have written them down for you. In my head.
after: Press C, click the Weapon slot on the figure, choose the blade and press Equip. Four steps. I have written them down for you, in my head.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: WELCOME TO THE UNDERCROFT, CHAMPION - ANNOUNCER GRAND BELLOWS, KEEPER OF THE SAND! Mind the third stair; it bites without an introduction.
after: WELCOME TO THE UNDERCROFT, CHAMPION! I AM ANNOUNCER GRAND BELLOWS, KEEPER OF THE SAND! (normal voice) Mind the third stair. It's loose, and it holds a grudge.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Auntie Alembic. Alchemist. Do not touch anything. ...Fine. Touch that one. It likes you.
after: Auntie Alembic, dear: alchemist, and keeper of some very nervous glassware. Don't touch anything. ...Oh, fine, touch that one. It likes you.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Bring me six essence each of two Paths, plus 100 gold, and I will brew you a card of BOTH. Random. Unpredictable. Occasionally on fire. I only take what the brew needs; the rest stays in your jars.
after: Bring me six essence each of two Paths, plus 100 gold, and I'll brew you a card of BOTH. Which card is up to the cauldron, and now and then it's on fire. I only take what the brew needs; the rest stays in your jars.

speaker: Auntie Alembic
before: Six essence of each of two Paths and 100 gold, dear; faith helps with the waiting. Lower your voice around the red flask - it takes things personally.
after: Six essence each of two Paths and 100 gold, dear, and the cauldron does the rest. Lower your voice near the red flask. It takes things personally.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: How it works: whenever a Path's final dungeon falls, that Path sends me its pack. Don't ask how. Lots of foil, no paperwork. The Necrocrats find it upsetting.
after: Here's how it works: whenever a Path's final dungeon falls, that Path sends me its pack. Don't ask how. There's a great deal of foil and no paperwork at all, which the Necrocrats find upsetting.

speaker: Foil Fenwick
before: Free a zone and I stock its pack. Until then it's just a rumour in a wrapper. Browse! Sniff, if you like. I won't judge. I sniff.
after: Free a zone and I'll stock its pack; until then it's just a rumour in a wrapper. Browse, sniff if you like. I won't judge. I sniff.

speaker: Arena challenger (marshal)
before: THE CROWD! GOES! WILD! (normal voice) Please stay behind the rope. There is a rope.
after: THE CROWD! GOES! WILD! (normal voice) Could the crowd please stay behind the rope? I put up a rope.

speaker: Arena challenger (marshal)
before: INTERMISSION! (normal voice) I'm having soup. THE SOUP IS WINNING.
after: INTERMISSION! (normal voice) Everybody sit down a minute. I've brought a flask of soup, and my voice needs it more than I do.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: VICTORY ON THE SAND - THE PRIZE IS YOURS! The echo would like it known that it believed in you first.
after: VICTORY ON THE SAND - THE PRIZE IS YOURS! (normal voice) Mind your head on the way up to collect it. The ceiling doesn't celebrate.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Some coins for you. From the crowd. The crowd is me.
after: ANOTHER WIN FOR THE BOOKS! (normal voice) Here's a few coins from the crowd. The crowd is me, but I mean every one of them.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: PUZZLE SOLVED - THE CROWD GOES WILD! A triumph for thinking, shouted at full volume!
after: PUZZLE SOLVED - THE CROWD GOES WILD! (normal voice) Lovely bit of thinking, that. I could hear the gears turning from the booth.

speaker: Announcer Grand Bellows
before: THE PUZZLE WINS THIS ROUND! (normal voice) Study the board. Try again. It's not going anywhere.
after: THE PUZZLE WINS THIS ROUND! (normal voice) Have a good long look at the board and try again. It's not going anywhere, and neither am I.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: No station yet. Walk into the town there and a cousin will wake up and rip one into the wall.
after: No station yet. Walk into that town yourself and a cousin will turn up and rip one into the nearest wall.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Ripping out of a zone ends your visit: you arrive at full HP, and the roaming enemies there come back. Rips are free. Beefcakes charge for spotting, and spotting is also free.
after: Ripping out of a zone ends your visit: you arrive at full HP, and the roaming enemies there come back. Rips are free, and so is the spotting.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: The elevator lobby. A cousin ripped it into the wall beside the Out-Of-Order sign. It is the only thing in the building that works.
after: The elevator lobby, where a cousin ripped it into the wall beside the Out-Of-Order sign. It's the only thing in the building that works.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: A short walk from the heavy meal table. The cousin ripped it open just by the napkins.
after: A short walk from the heavy meal table. The cousin ripped it open right by the napkins, so you'll never arrive without one.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Right by the harvest table. The Rip is slightly damp. So is everything.
after: Right by the harvest table. The Rip on duty is slightly damp, but then so is everything else out there.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: A rip into the hideout under the Capital. Do not ask how we found it. We followed the smell of Fig Sly's hot sauce through the fabric of space.
after: A rip into the hideout under the Capital. Don't ask how we found it; we followed the smell of Fig Sly's hot sauce straight through the fabric of space.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: The sky is surprisingly heavy. Do NOT skip sky day. And do not look at the seam. It is not a seam. It is a PUMP.
after: The sky is heavier than it looks, buddy, so we never skip sky day. Do not look at the seam. It's working very hard and it's shy about it.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Reach a town and we send a cousin to rip a station there. All named Rip; around cousin four, naming became a cooldown exercise.
after: Reach a new town and we send a cousin to rip a station there. Every one of them is called Rip. Our mother found a name she liked and saw no reason to stop.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Back for another rip, little buddy? Say where, and we will tear it right open. Rips are free.
after: Back for another rip, buddy? Say where and we'll tear it right open. Rips are free, same as always.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Spotting is free, buddy. Hydration is a bring-your-own-water situation.
after: Spotting is free, buddy. Water, sadly, you'll have to bring yourself.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Shhh. Keep it down, there is a Wrinkle sleeping behind the crates. Rip Tearson, Cousin #7, Rift Express. Allegedly.
after: Shhh. Keep it down, buddy, there's a Wrinkle asleep behind the crates. Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Seven, Rift Express. Allegedly.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: I was told this place did not exist, so I ripped a hole to it. Sometimes you just have to want it. And the sauce smell helped.
after: They told me this place didn't exist, so I ripped a hole to it anyway. Sometimes you just have to believe in yourself. The sauce smell helped.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Spot this whole dimension, brother! Lift with your LEGS - lower back does not mean lower universe!
after: Spot this whole dimension, brother! Lift with your LEGS! Nobody ever tore the sky open with their lower back!

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: You check for an approved way to have arrived. The memo offers none.
after: You turn the memo over, looking for an approved way to have arrived. There isn't one.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: You land in the Pantry and receive a napkin before you find your balance. Priorities are immaculate.
after: You land in the Pantry, and someone hands you a napkin before you've found your feet.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: You arrive at the Grange in a whiff of ozone, mulch and gym sock. The Express leaves a personal impression.
after: You arrive at the Grange in a whiff of ozone, mulch and gym sock, and the gym sock is definitely the Express.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: A hasty rip where you first woke up, between the trees. There is a hatch in the clearing now that nobody remembers being there. It smells like a hospital.
after: A hasty rip between the trees where you first woke up. There's a hatch south of the clearing now that nobody remembers being there, and it smells like a hospital.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Eight, rift technician, tree enthusiast. This is the clearing where I found the hatch, buddy. I did not open it.
after: HNNNGH. Rip Tearson, Cousin Number Eight, rift technician and tree enthusiast. This is where I found the hatch, buddy, and no, I didn't open it.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Say the word and I will rip you back to {town}. Or you can go down the hatch. I will hold the sky.
after: Say the word and I'll rip you back to {town}. Or, if you're going down the hatch, I'll hold the sky open till you're back up.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: Need a rip back to {town}, or are you heading down the hatch? Either way, I have been holding this sky since breakfast.
after: Back to {town}, buddy, or down the hatch? Either way, I've been holding this sky since breakfast and it's ready when you are.

speaker: Rip Tearson and cousins
before: I went exploring up there, and I saw some very interesting things. The brambles south of the clearing just... let go. There is a path now, and at the end of it a hatch that was NOT there before. Little glowing roots. A smell like a hospital.
after: I went up there on my day off and saw some very interesting things. The brambles south of the clearing just... let go, and there's a path now, with a hatch at the end that was NOT there before. Glowing roots, and a hospital smell.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Sable, Tilly and Pip, dearie, all on the square. And buy a card from Sable. You are not leaving this town with only what a cave gave you.
after: Sable, Tilly and Pip, dearie, all three on the square. And buy a card from Sable while you're there. I'll not have you facing the roads with nothing but what a cave gave you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Back already. Sable charmed you, Tilly was a colour, Pip measured you. That is {town}, dearie. Try leaving with the same hat.
after: Back already? Let me guess: Sable charmed you, Tilly turned a colour, and Pip measured you before you'd finished saying hello. That's {town}, dearie.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Here: a trophy. Everybody gets one. I made it myself, so participate carefully.
after: Here, have a trophy. Everybody gets one, so don't let it go to your head. I made it myself, and the handle comes off if you wave it about.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: A deck you never chose is a deck you will lose with, says Maren. New cards first, then make the deck your own.
after: Maren says a deck you never chose is a deck you'll lose with. Open a pack for some new cards, then make the deck your own at the Deck Station.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Now that deck of yours. A deck you never chose is a deck you will lose with.
after: Now, about that deck of yours. You didn't choose a single card in it, dearie, and a deck you never chose is a deck you'll lose with.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: New cards first. Open a pack: the Menu, top right, then Packs. Or press P, if you are the sort who presses things.
after: New cards first, so open a pack: the Menu at the top right, then Packs. Or press P, if you're the sort who presses things.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Then the Deck Station, down Champions' Road south of the square. Swap what you like, save it to a slot, and come and tell me.
after: Then take it to the Deck Station, down Champions' Road south of the square. Swap in whatever you like, save it to a slot, and come and tell me how it went.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: No packs at all? Here, dearie. A General Pack. Slightly sat on. Cards are cards.
after: No packs at all? Here, dearie, have a General Pack. It's been sat on a little. Cards are cards, and these ones won't hold it against you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Open the pack first, dearie. Menu, then Packs. It will not open itself. I have asked.
after: Open the pack first, dearie: the Menu, then Packs. It won't open itself. I've asked it nicely.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The Deck Station, dearie. Champions' Road, south of the square. Save it to a slot, or it doesn't count. I check.
after: The Deck Station is down Champions' Road, south of the square, dearie. Save it to a slot when you're done, or it doesn't count. I do check.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Sorted and saved. Your own deck, at last. Now you may take personal offence when it loses.
after: Sorted and saved, and every card in it your own choice. Good. Now when it loses, you've nobody to blame but yourself, which is how it ought to be.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: Tilly Tonic's store room has been rattling, moaning and refusing visitors. Maren would like it to stop. So would Tilly.
after: Tilly Tonic's store room has been rattling and moaning for a week, and nobody can get in. Maren wants it sorted, and so, very much, does Tilly.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Now, a favour. Tilly's store room, the corner house beside her shop, has been moaning for a week. Not Tilly. The room.
after: Now, a favour. Tilly's store room, the corner house beside her shop, has been moaning for a week. I don't mean Tilly, dearie. I mean the room.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Ghosts, I expect. Petty ones: the worst kind. Nobody can get in for so much as a candle. Go and sort them out. Gently, if they let you.
after: Ghosts, I expect, and petty ones, which are the worst kind. Nobody's been able to get in for so much as a candle. Go and sort them out, gently if they'll let you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The store room door, beside Tilly's shop on the north side of the square. Ignore the rattling. That is just them being dramatic.
after: The store room door is beside Tilly's shop, on the north side of the square. Ignore the rattling, dearie; that's just them being dramatic.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: A refund. Ninety years of haunting, over a refund. I have had customers like that. I still have one.
after: A refund? Ninety years of moaning, all over one broken lantern. I've had customers like that. I still have a few.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Well done, dearie. You settled the ghosts. Next, settle yourself somewhere dry.
after: Well done, dearie. You've settled the ghosts, so now go and settle yourself somewhere dry before you catch a chill.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: Maren says it is time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth issues gear, by the book: report to his smithy and win him one fight.
after: Maren says it's time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth issues gear strictly by the book: report to his smithy, then win one fight to earn it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Right. Time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth issues gear, at the smithy on the west side of the square.
after: Right, then. It's time you had something sharper than a deck. Bertram Beetsworth hands out gear from his smithy, on the west side of the square.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Bertram's smithy, west side of the square. Win him a fight, any fight, and he will stamp something. He lives to stamp something.
after: Bertram's smithy is on the west side of the square. Win him one fight, any fight at all, and he'll stamp something for you. He lives to stamp things.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Armed, are we. Good. Now, where to point you. Start with {zone}, dearie. It is {path} country, and so are you.
after: Armed now, are we? Good. Then it's time I pointed you somewhere. Start with {zone}, dearie. It's {path} country, and so, by the look of you, are you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: {vendor} sells more {path} cards there than anyone in this town. Take gold. Take a bag. Take my advice, for once.
after: {vendor} sells more {path} cards out there than anyone in this town does, so take gold and a good big bag. And take my advice, for once.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And inside {zone}, your Path stands taller. {buff}: {buff_text}
after: Inside {zone}, your Path stands a little taller. {buff}: {buff_text}

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The Paths quarrel, dearie. Beefcake against Necrocrat, Gourmand against Refusemancer. Since before the roads. Possibly because of them.
after: The Paths quarrel, dearie: Beefcake against Necrocrat, Gourmand against Refusemancer. They always have. Once, they needed each other too much for it to matter.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: So in {zone} the {rival} side gets the short end. {debuff}: {debuff_text} In {rival_zone}, it is your turn to suffer.
after: So in {zone}, it's the {rival} side that gets the short end. {debuff}: {debuff_text} In {rival_zone}, it's the other way round, and you're the one who suffers.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: {gatekeeper} holds the way in. Win that fight first. Then come back alive. Pie is not cheap.
after: {gatekeeper} holds the way in, and you'll have to win that fight before anything else. Then come back alive. I'll have a pie waiting, and I don't bake for people who don't come back.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Evening! Old Hob. I dig. Not much call for it these ten years. Nobody's been collected, you see. Paperwork. Heh.
after: Evening! Old Hob, at your service. I dig, mostly, though there's not been much call for it these ten years. Nobody's been collected, you see. Paperwork. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Appointments. Let's have a look for you... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Mind the cairn at the end of the row. Something under it is still counting its turns. Rude to keep it waiting. Heh.
after: Mind the cairn at the end of the row. Something under it is still counting its turns, and it's rude to keep a thing like that waiting. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Still digging. Slowly. Two particular graves, these ten years. I like to take my time with the important ones. Heh.
after: Still digging, slowly. Two particular graves, these ten years now. I like to take my time over the important ones. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Appointments. Let's have a look for you... hm. Not for a good long while yet. Lovely! That's what I like to see.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: {villain} is gone, but Rip found something in the forest where you first woke: a hatch that was not there before. Something under it feels like yours. So does someone.
after: {villain} is gone, but Rip found something in the forest where you first woke: a hatch that wasn't there before. Whatever is down there feels like yours, and so does someone.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: Elder Maren wants you fed, kitted out and known in town. Say hello to the shopkeepers on the square and buy yourself a card. There is a trophy in it. Everyone gets the trophy.
after: Elder Maren wants you fed, kitted out and known in town. Say hello to the shopkeepers on the square and buy yourself a card. There's a trophy in it, though everyone gets the trophy.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The kettle's on and the pie is cooling. Neither is for you. Both are for you.
after: Kettle's on and the pie's cooling. Neither's for you, dearie. Well. Both are.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Hm. Wrote you in the book. 'Stranger, damp.' I'll fix it when you know.
after: Hm. Wrote you in the book. 'Stranger, damp.' I'll add a name when you've got one.

speaker: Sable
before: Two typos, darling. One misprint. Such a small card, such a complicated past.
after: Two typos and a misprint, darling. Such a small card, such a complicated past.

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Fresh tonics! Tested them all this morning! I'm teal! Teal means it works!
after: Fresh tonics! I tested every one this morning, and I'm teal, so they work!

speaker: Tilly Tonic
before: Emergency tonic! Works on Tuesdays too! That's when I test the emergency tonic!
after: Emergency tonic! I keep inventing new emergencies just to test it on!

speaker: Bertram Beetsworth, Assistant to the Regional Merchant
before: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Nobody opens the drawer. Protocol Three.
after: Fact: bears cannot open the drawer. Neither can you. Security Protocol Three.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: Hydration. Stretching. Sorry, am I ordering again? I meant we could do them together.
after: Water, then a stretch. Sorry, was that an order? I meant we could do them together.

speaker: Brindle the Baker
before: Fresh bread! Flour in my whiskers again. Occupational dusting. Anyone want a roll?
after: Fresh bread! Flour in my whiskers again, but the rolls came out lovely. Want one?

speaker: Brindle the Baker
before: I knead a holiday. Then I knead the dough. Busy, busy badger.
after: I knead a holiday, but the dough won't hear of it. Busy, busy badger.

speaker: Crosspath townsfolk
before: The old cottage cheers at night now. From the cellar. I'm choosing to love it.
after: The old cottage cheers at night now, from the cellar. I've decided to find it lovely.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: You did it. Grandmaster Flex is out. He made me stretch for forty minutes. I cried twice. Good tears.
after: You actually did it - Grandmaster Flex is out! First thing he did was make me stretch for forty minutes. I cried twice, but they were good tears. Stretchy ones.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: The bridge stays down now, but I still oil the crank every morning. Maintenance is how I say sorry.
after: The bridge stays down now, but I still oil the crank every morning. Maintenance is how I say sorry, and I've got a lot of sorry left to get through.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: Want to spar? Gently. I'll spot you. I'm a spotter. ...I'm SO glad I can say that quietly.
after: Want to spar? Gently, I mean. I'll spot you. I'm still a spotter, I just get to say it at a normal volume now, and honestly, it's a huge relief.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: Brick Bronson cracks his knuckles, grabs the crank, and lowers the bridge with one arm. Show-off.
after: Brick Bronson cracks his knuckles, takes the crank in one hand and lowers the bridge with it, making very sure you're watching.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: The planks thump down across the gorge. The Gainlands are open.
after: The planks thump down across the gorge, and the road into the Gainlands lies open.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: The bridge stays up by order of the regime and Chancellor Clench. Only iron matters! IRON! Also hydration!
after: THE BRIDGE STAYS UP BY ORDER OF CHANCELLOR CLENCH AND THE REGIME! ONLY IRON MATTERS! ...AND HYDRATION! HYDRATION ALSO MATTERS!

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: YOU WANT THE CRANK? TEN REPS! NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING! IT IS GOING GREAT!
after: YOU WANT THE CRANK? EARN IT! TEN REPS, NO REST! I HAVE NOT SAT DOWN SINCE SPRING AND I FEEL FANTASTIC!

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: ...Oh no. Was I yelling? I was yelling. Sorry. That was the pre-workout talking, and it talks a lot.
after: ...Oh no. Was I yelling? I was yelling, wasn't I. I'm so sorry - that was the pre-workout talking, and it doesn't know when to stop.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: Chancellor Clench locked Grandmaster Flex in the House of Gains. People whispered the old man never broke. I didn't whisper. I yelled. Sorry again.
after: Chancellor Clench had Grandmaster Flex locked away under the House of Gains, ten years ago now. Folks still whisper that the old man never broke. I should've whispered with them instead of yelling.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: The bridge is yours, friend. Stretch before you cross. Hamstrings are friends, and friends don't let friends pull one.
after: The bridge is yours, friend. Stretch before you cross, though - a pulled hamstring is a terrible souvenir.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: HA! THE PUMP IS STILL MINE! GO HOME AND HYDRATE! THAT IS AN ORDER, NOT CONCERN!
after: HA! THE PUMP IS STILL MINE! GO HOME AND HYDRATE! THAT IS AN ORDER, NOT CONCERN! ...IT IS A LITTLE BIT CONCERN.

speaker: Brick Bronson
before: COME BACK WHEN YOU CAN LIFT! THE BRIDGE STAYS UP - FINALLY, SOMETHING THAT HOLDS ITS FORM!
after: COME BACK WHEN YOU CAN LIFT! THE BRIDGE STAYS UP, AND SO DO I! NEITHER OF US IS ALLOWED TO SIT DOWN!

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: The Gainlands bridge is drawn up and a very large man is guarding the crank. Get across and find out who is running the Gainlands now.
after: The bridge into the Gainlands is drawn up, and the very large man on the crank answers to the regime. Get across and find out who is running the Beefcakes now.

speaker: (UI)
before: The Gainlands: the Swole Station is safe, mostly because the regime forgets it exists. HP does not come back after battles - soak in the Cooldown Hot Tub or walk down to town. The House of Gains is on Leg Day Ridge.
after: The Gainlands: the Swole Station is safe, mostly because the regime forgets it exists. HP doesn't come back after battles, so soak in the Cooldown Hot Tub or walk down to town. The House of Gains is on Leg Day Ridge.

speaker: (narration)
before: The House of Gains looms over you, all iron-less steel and floodlights. The regime's flag snaps in the wind: a barbell with a red line through it.
after: The House of Gains looms over you, all bare stone and floodlights. Above it the regime's flag snaps in the wind: a barbell with a red line through it.

speaker: (narration)
before: You are already as recovered as a Beefcake gets. Go lift something. Preferably not Gary.
after: You're already as rested as a Beefcake ever gets. The tub has done all it can for you.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: "Passed out mid-rep. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... the spring of... well. Towel's on your tab.
after: "You passed out mid-rep, lad. Happens to the best of us. Happened to me in the spring of... the spring of... well, it was a spring. Towel's on your tab.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Don't tell the regime. They'd only fine you for resting."
after: Just don't tell the regime you had a lie-down. They fine people for resting, and I've only got the one towel."

speaker: (narration)
before: You find a hidden stash. Excellent spotting technique, terrible lifting posture.
after: Behind a rock you find a hidden stash, wrapped in an old gym towel so the regime wouldn't spot it.

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Nailed the landing. Mostly, the ground nailed you.
after: You land. The ground takes most of the credit.

speaker: (narration)
before: You fall off the island and respawn at your last safe spot. Gravity declines your request for a spotter. (-1 HP)
after: You slip off the edge and come round at your last safe spot, bruised. Gravity has never spotted anyone in its life. (-1 HP)

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Terrible landing, though. Hold still; the view is the comfortable part."
after: Landing's a bit rough, mind. Tuck your elbows in and enjoy the view while you've got it."

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Brock is out of stock on locks. This one is always open.
after: Brock is always ready, and so is his throwing arm.

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Rita flexes both hands like she is about to open a very stubborn jar. "Delt Deck? Wild ride. I rip the portal, you walk in.
after: Rita flexes both hands like she's about to open a very stubborn jar. "Delt Deck? Easy. I rip the portal open, you walk through.

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: No tools, no spells. Bare hands. Just lats."
after: No tools and no spells, just bare hands and a lot of back."

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Rita shakes her head. "No juice, no rip. Ripping takes power, and the grid is bone dry.
after: Rita shakes her head. "Can't rip a thing with the grid this dry. Portals run on power, same as everything else up here.

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Somebody needs to run the big hamster wheel up the hill. Do that, then come back."
after: Somebody has to run the big hamster wheel up the hill. Get it spinning, then come back and I'll have you through in no time."

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Tobias hefts you like a sack of oats. "Cross-country to the west meadow. Long way.
after: Tobias hefts you like a sack of oats. "West meadow, cross-country. It's a long way, so I'm putting everything into this one.

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: I'll put everything into the throw. You can tell me what you thought of it when your thoughts catch up."
after: You can tell me how it was once your thoughts catch up with you."

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Tobias squints at you. "Cross-country is for Gainers only. Show me a Gym Rat card and I'll chuck you clear across the map. Coach Brutus Benchley sells them."
after: Tobias squints at you. "Cross-country chucks are for Gainers only. Show me a Gym Rat card and I'll send you clear across the Gainlands. Coach Brutus Benchley sells them."

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Did the old yeti say hello? ...Don't tell me. I don't care. Did he, though?
after: Shredna rolls her shoulders. "Calf Cove. Did the old yeti say hello? ...No, don't tell me, I don't care. Did he, though?

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Old Man Mountain vouches for you, so Calf Cove's open. Mind the edges; the view really drops off."
after: Old Man Mountain vouches for you, so Calf Cove's open. Mind the edges out there; the view drops off very suddenly."

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Dmitri cracks his neck, slowly, both ways. "Glute Garden is a long throw. Very long.
after: Dmitri cracks his neck slowly, one way and then the other. "Glute Garden's a long throw. A very long throw.

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: I need you to be aerodynamic. Try not to think about it. Thinking adds drag."
after: I need you aerodynamic, so try not to think about it. Thinking adds drag."

speaker: Throwers and rippers
before: Raelynn tears a seam in the air with one grunt. "Home? Home is always an option. Mind the gap. It bites."
after: Raelynn tears a seam in the air with one grunt. "Heading home? Home's always open. Mind the gap on your way through; it bites."

speaker: (narration)
before: Results may vary. Please wait for the shake to settle before deciding whether you have.
after: Results may vary. Please let the shake settle before you drink it, and your stomach settle after.

speaker: (narration)
before: Protein, powder and cards. Mostly cards. The protein is optional. The yelling is not.
after: Protein, powder and cards, but mostly cards. The protein is optional; the yelling is not.

speaker: (narration)
before: Professor Pump teaches: 4 questions on Beefcake knowledge. Bring your own notes. Notes are on the signs.
after: Professor Pump asks 4 questions on Beefcake knowledge. Every answer is written on a sign somewhere in the Gainlands, so read as you go.

speaker: (narration)
before: Run it to power the grid. No actual hamsters. The hamsters get breaks.
after: Run it to power the grid. There are no actual hamsters inside; the hamsters get breaks.

speaker: (narration)
before: (Chalk sold at Benchley's. Chalk is a lie.)
after: (Chalk sold at Benchley's, at a price he calls motivational.)

speaker: (narration)
before: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only. Authorization takes thirty seconds, by order of the Minister of Efficiency.
after: The regime's stronghold. Authorized personnel only. Authorization takes exactly thirty seconds, and someone inside is timing you.

speaker: (narration)
before: Ask a Beefcake. They have loads. The regime takes most of it.
after: Ask any Beefcake: they've got loads of it, and the regime takes most of it.

speaker: (narration)
before: You hear confiscated protein powder rattle inside a walking tub. Whey out of line.
after: A walking tub of confiscated protein powder rattles past, and it does not like the look of you.

speaker: (narration)
before: Pure mandatory pre-workout. Zero chill. Vibrates through walls.
after: A sprite of pure mandatory pre-workout buzzes past, vibrating so hard it goes straight through a wall.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Shh. Welcome to the Gainlands. The regime has ears. Big ones. Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its folks moving. Wheels, mills... and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.
after: Shh, keep it down - the regime has big ears up here. Welcome to the Gainlands. They call me Old Man Mountain. We Beefcakes keep the kingdom's lights on and its people moving... and if you're in a hurry, we throw you.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Ten years back, {villain}'s people put Chancellor Clench in charge. Grandmaster Flex's own star pupil. They locked Flex under the House of Gains and took every weight. Every... every plate.
after: Ten years back, {villain}'s people put Chancellor Clench in charge - Grandmaster Flex's own star pupil, if you can believe it. They locked Flex under the House of Gains and took every weight. Every... every last plate.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: We haven't crumbled. Tired, mind. If you fall, I catch you. Rule one: never lift alone. Rule two: never skip leg day. Rule three... I forget. Two is plenty.
after: We're tired, but we haven't crumbled. If you fall, I'll catch you: rule one, never lift alone. Rule two, never skip leg day. Rule three is... I've forgotten rule three. Two's plenty.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: And that gate up on the overlook, past the ridge? Sealed. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely.
after: And that gate up on the overlook, past the ridge, won't budge for anybody. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely. Twice.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Back for more? Good. The only bad rep is the one nobody spotted.
after: Back again? Good. The only bad rep is the one nobody was there to spot.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Beat the regime and I'll buy the first round of shakes. The illegal flavour... ah, that's the one worth remembering.
after: You beat the regime and I'll buy the first round of shakes. Even the illegal flavour. Especially the illegal flavour... ah, I can nearly taste it.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: The old king used to come up for the Lifting Festival every summer, with his boy. Little fella tried my dumbbell and sat down hard on his royal behind.
after: The old king came up for the Lifting Festival every summer, and he brought his boy. The little fella tried my dumbbell once and sat down very hard on his royal behind.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Laughed about it, too. Four colours in his hands, plain as day. You've got a look about you... never mind. Old man talk. Where was I.
after: He laughed about it, too, and his hands lit up four colours, plain as day. You've a look of him, you know... no, never mind me. Old man talk. Where was I?

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: That gate up on the overlook? Sealed. Opens when the kingdom is whole again. Not a day before. I asked it nicely.
after: That gate up on the overlook is still sealed. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I check on it most mornings, just in case.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Foreman Gus: wheels turning, grid humming, hamsters... *volunteers*... fed. Pre-workout's in the water, but so far I'm only feeling the water.
after: Foreman Gus. I keep the wheels turning, the grid humming and the hamsters - sorry, the volunteers - fed. They put pre-workout in the water. So far I'm mostly feeling the water.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The regime wants a hundred and ten percent. The wheels go to a hundred. The extra ten is me, crying quietly.
after: The regime wants a hundred and ten percent. The wheels only go to a hundred. The extra ten comes out of the crew, and nobody writes down where it went.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: They want the same out of the city wheels up in the Capital. Those crews get told it's cardio. It isn't.
after: The crews on the city wheels up in the Capital have it worse. They're told it's cardio, for their own good. It's neither.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Grid still humming? If it goes quiet, somebody's resting, and the regime writes that down as a personal insult.
after: Grid's still humming. If it ever goes quiet, it means somebody sat down, and the regime takes that very personally.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: LET'S GO! NEW RECRUIT! Coach Brutus Benchley! Retired champion, current motivator, part-time merchant! Protein, powder, pasteboard! Supplements for your DECK!
after: LET'S GO! A NEW RECRUIT! Coach Brutus Benchley - retired champion, current motivator, part-time merchant! Protein, powder and pasteboard! SUPPLEMENTS FOR YOUR DECK!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: *whispering* Mind the loose floorboard behind the counter. Nothing under it... just iron, which officially isn't anything.
after: *whispering* Mind the loose floorboard behind the counter. There's nothing under it. Just some iron, which officially doesn't exist.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: LET'S GO, RETURNING CUSTOMER! The cards are pumped and my whistle has been SAVING ITS BREATH!
after: LET'S GO, RETURNING CUSTOMER! The cards are pumped and my whistle's been SAVING ITS BREATH for you!

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Aha, a student! Professor Pump, Beefcake scholar, lecturing from this very log. I have written seventeen books.
after: Aha, a student! I'm Professor Pump, Beefcake scholar, and I lecture from this very log. I've written seventeen books, you know.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Fifteen concern biceps. The other two were a history of the Lifting Festival; the regime burned those, so I rewrote them from memory. You cannot confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.
after: Fifteen of them concern the biceps. The other two were a history of the Lifting Festival, and when the regime burned those, I rewrote them from memory. You can't confiscate a well-trained brain-cep.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Back for another set of questions? Splendid - knowledge gains are retained even when you stop flexing.
after: Back for another set of questions? Splendid! Knowledge gains stay with you, even on your rest days.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Zero, with no reward this time. A clean baseline; research begins somewhere.
after: Zero, I'm afraid, and no reward this time. Still, it's a clean baseline, and all research has to begin somewhere.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Consult the signs before your next attempt. Your eyes may do the heavy reading.
after: Do read the signs before your next attempt. Let your eyes do the heavy lifting for once.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: One. A muscle twitch of knowledge. Take this pat on the back. It's a small one.
after: One. A twitch of knowledge, at least. Take this small pat on the back.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Two. Half-credit, graded on a bicep curve. In the Gainlands half a rep still counts. Just not for much.
after: Two. Half-credit, graded on a bicep curve. In the Gainlands half a rep still counts, just not for very much.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: FOUR! A perfect set! You may now call yourself a Certified Gainer, Class A. The reward is real. The certificate is imaginary.
after: FOUR! A perfect set! You may now call yourself a Certified Gainer, Class A. The reward is real; the certificate, sadly, is imaginary.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a little less for repeat attendance. The regime calls it a "processing fee". A D.N.A. phrase, I suspect.
after: Another lap! The Gainlands pay a little less for repeat attendance. The regime calls it a 'processing fee', which sounds suspiciously like the D.N.A. to me.

speaker: Professor Pump
before: Not a pass yet; read the signs around the Gainlands and return. We are training recall, not regret.
after: Not a pass yet, I'm afraid. Read the signs around the Gainlands and come back. We're training recall here, not regret.

speaker: Chet Thunderabs
before: The regime banned my show for 'unauthorized fun'! These cameras are STILL ROLLING - you can't spell resistance without... well, SPANDEX HELPS!
after: The regime banned my show for 'unauthorized fun'! But these cameras are STILL ROLLING, because you can't confiscate a man's ENTHUSIASM! They tried! It came back!

speaker: Chet Thunderabs
before: REHYDRATE AND TRY AGAIN! The beat and the legwarmers are standing by - only one of those has legs!
after: REHYDRATE AND TRY AGAIN! The beat is standing by! The legwarmers are standing by! I am STANDING BY, and my calves are SO ready!

speaker: Gary
before: Mmmph! Oh good, a spotter! Hi. Gary. Lovely to meet you.
after: Mmmph! Oh, thank goodness, a spotter! Hi, I'm Gary. Lovely to meet you. Sorry I can't shake hands.

speaker: Gary
before: I've been under this barbell since lunch... possibly since the regime took over. No rush, but I would like to become a standing appointment.
after: I've been under this barbell since lunch. Possibly since the regime took over - it's hard to tell from down here. No rush. Bit of a rush.

speaker: Gary
before: It's the last barbell they didn't confiscate. I loaded one more plate than my confidence.
after: It's the last barbell they didn't confiscate, so I got excited and loaded one more plate than my confidence.

speaker: Gary
before: It's fine. It's FINE. Could you give it a little push? Bit of a rush, actually.
after: It's fine. It's FINE. Could you give it a little push? Whenever you're ready. Now would be good.

speaker: Gym attendant
before: Gym's open! The weights are not. The scales stayed, though - standard measures, from the Capital. Say what you like, they never lie.
after: Gym's open! The weights aren't. The scales stayed, though - standard measures, sent up from the Capital. Say what you like about the Minister, those scales never lie.

speaker: Gym attendant
before: Towels are ten gold now. Clench taxes sweat.
after: Towels are ten gold now, because Clench taxes sweat.

speaker: (narration)
before: "You're a hero! Take this. I borrowed it from the gym.
after: "You're a hero! Take this, I borrowed it from the gym.

speaker: (narration)
before: It's not mine. It's yours now. That's how borrowing works, I think."
after: It's not mine, so now it's yours. I think that's how borrowing works."

speaker: (narration)
before: You jump into the Colossal Hamster Wheel and run. And run. The grid hums, the lights across the Gainlands brighten, and somewhere a portal ripper rolls up her sleeves.
after: You jump into the Colossal Hamster Wheel and run until your legs burn. The grid hums, lights brighten across the Gainlands, and somewhere a portal ripper rolls up her sleeves.

speaker: (narration)
before: The wheel is already spinning happily. Let it coast. You deserve a snack.
after: The wheel's still spinning happily on its own. Let it coast; you've earned a snack.

speaker: (narration)
before: You taste a legendary chocolate-peanut-butter shake. Even your muscles want the recipe - big recovery!
after: A legendary chocolate-peanut-butter shake. Even your muscles want the recipe. Big recovery!

speaker: (narration)
before: You hit a double biceps. The mirror gasps. You gasp. +1 HP.
after: You hit a double biceps, and you and the mirror gasp at the same moment. +1 HP.

speaker: (narration)
before: Your pump has peaked; come back after your next visit. Even your reflection needs a cooldown.
after: Your pump has peaked for this visit; come back next time. Even your reflection needs a cooldown.

speaker: (narration)
before: You flex, the mirror flexes back, nothing to heal. Looking great regardless.
after: You flex, the mirror flexes back, and there's nothing left to heal. You look great regardless.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Lights flicker while the regime pipes every watt to the House of Gains. Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill for us - a little resistance.
after: The lights keep flickering because the regime pipes every watt up to the House of Gains. Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill and we'll keep a little for ourselves. Call it quiet resistance.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station for crew morale. Quiet gains - the revolution comes with a straw.
after: Then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. It's for crew morale. Mostly mine.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill, then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. Quiet gains - tell me when you're done.
after: Run the Colossal Hamster Wheel up the hill, then buy a shake at the protein stand in the Swole Station. Come and find me when you're done.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The Swole Station's lights are back on. Grid's humming. I'd make a speech, but all my energy went into the lights. Take your reward.
after: The Swole Station's lights are back on and the grid's humming. I'd make a speech, but all my energy went into the lights. Here, take your reward.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: The grid's running smooth, and some of it's even staying here. I'd hug you, but I'm a foreman. We nod. ...That was a big nod.
after: The grid's running smooth, and some of the power's even staying here for once. I'd hug you, but I'm a foreman, so I'll nod. ...That was a big nod, for me.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Which brings me to rule one. Gary's under a barbell again. Go and spot him; follow the groaning. Then check your form at a Flex Mirror. The regime can't confiscate a reflection. They tried.
after: Which brings me back to rule one. Gary's stuck under a barbell again - follow the groaning and give him a spot. Then check your form at a Flex Mirror. The regime tried confiscating reflections once. It didn't take.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Do both and I'll have Shredna rip you a portal to Calf Cove. Nobody's been out there in months. The calves are... unreal.
after: Do both and I'll have Shredna rip you a portal out to Calf Cove. Nobody's been out there in months, and the calves... well, you'll see.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: You spotted Gary AND checked your form? Beautiful. Here, a Pre-Workout Jitters. On the house.
after: You spotted Gary and checked your form? Beautiful. Here, have a Pre-Workout Jitters, on the house.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Calf Cove is yours. Mind the edge. Always mind the edge. I didn't, once, back in... never mind.
after: Calf Cove's yours now. Mind the edge out there - always mind the edge. I didn't, once, back in the spring of... never mind.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep eating my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM!
after: Regime brutes, golems and sprites keep EATING my deliveries! Beat any three roaming enemies in the Gainlands in card duels! THOSE SHAKES HAD MY NAME ON THEM! I WRITE IT ON EVERY LID!

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: THREE DOWN! Deliveries back on schedule! Here's a Leg Day for your trouble. Do NOT skip it. That's not a joke. That's the card.
after: THREE DOWN! Deliveries are BACK ON SCHEDULE! Here, take a Leg Day for your trouble, and do NOT skip it, champ! I mean that as a coach AND as a card dealer!

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Every machine hums at exactly the right wattage. The lift hums. The gate hums.
after: Every machine settles at exactly the right wattage, and the Lift, the Gate and the Mill all hum together.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: The mill hums. Somewhere, a hamster sighs in relief. A small, heavy parcel drops into the tray.
after: Somewhere a hamster sighs with relief, and a small, heavy parcel drops into the tray.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Just measuring. Lovely broad shoulders round here. Very roomy work, when it comes. It hasn't, lately. Heh.
after: Just measuring, don't mind me. Lovely broad shoulders up here - very roomy work, when it comes. Not that it's come lately. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Appointments. Let's see, you're... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.

speaker: Rip Tearson
before: Shirt number two hundred and twelve. Very proud of it. Notice my form?
after: HNNNGH. Two hundred and twelfth shirt this year. Did you notice my form, buddy?

speaker: (quest giver)
before: You beat Primm. The kingdom's whole again. Which means the gate on the overlook can open. Mount Swolympus.
after: You beat {villain}, and the kingdom's whole again. Which means that gate on the overlook can finally open... Mount Swolympus. I never thought I'd live to see it.

speaker: (quest giver)
before: Only the worthy reach the top. In my experience the worthy bring water. Or a protein shake. Get me one from the stand and the gate's yours.
after: Only the worthy reach the top, mind. In my experience the worthy bring water, or a protein shake. Fetch me one from the stand and the gate's yours.

speaker: (quest giver)
before: A shake from the stand in the Station. Any flavour. Not the illegal one. ...Fine. The illegal one.
after: A shake from the stand in the Station, any flavour. Not the illegal one. ...Oh, go on, then. The illegal one.

speaker: (quest giver)
before: Ahh. Worthy. Definitely worthy. Slightly lumpy.
after: Ahh. Worthy. Very worthy. A bit lumpy, but worthy.

speaker: (quest giver)
before: The gate's open and the ridge is fixed. Mostly. Climb to the top and say hello to the Ancient Spotter. He's held that bar for a thousand years. Ask about his back.
after: The gate's open and the ridge path is mended, mostly. Climb to the top and say hello to the Ancient Spotter - he's held that bar for a thousand years. Ask him about his back.

speaker: (quest giver)
before: The Spotter's waiting at the summit. Don't make him wait another thousand years.
after: The Spotter's waiting at the summit. Don't keep him waiting another thousand years, lad.

speaker: Baron Quadzilla, the Leg Press Lord
before: 'Nobody. Skips. Leg day.' He presses another rep. 'In my cave. Show me yours. No standing ovation required.'
after: 'Nobody. Skips. Leg day.' He presses another rep. 'Not in my cave. Prove it. I won't get up.'

speaker: (narration)
before: The gates swing open on a hall lined with posters of Chancellor Clench. There are no weights anywhere. Not a dumbbell.
after: The gates swing open on a hall papered with posters of Chancellor Clench, and there isn't a single weight anywhere in it, not even a dumbbell.

speaker: (narration)
before: Not a kettlebell. Not a single decorative plate.
after: Every rack along the walls stands empty, right down to the little pegs where the decorative plates used to hang.

speaker: (narration)
before: Somewhere beneath your feet, something is not quite silent. It is breathing. Slowly. On purpose.
after: Somewhere far beneath your feet, something is breathing, slow and even, as if it has been counting every breath for a very long time.

speaker: (narration)
before: Iron-less steel, floodlights, and a banner reading MANDATORY CARDIO. Nobody has ever left through here.
after: Bare steel and floodlights under a banner reading MANDATORY CARDIO. Iron is banned here, and nobody has ever left through these gates.

speaker: (narration)
before: An enforcer searches your bag for weights while a clerk clicks a stopwatch. Minister Quota wants every search done in thirty seconds. He is at forty.
after: An enforcer searches your bag for weights while a clerk times him with a stopwatch. Minister Quota wants every search done in thirty seconds, and he's already at forty.

speaker: (narration)
before: The prisoners are very quiet. The guards are very loud. Only one of these is a problem.
after: The prisoners keep very quiet and the guards are very loud, and it doesn't take long to work out which of them is afraid.

speaker: (narration)
before: The warden has never once lifted a weight. He has never needed to. He is very, very angry. (Elite)
after: The warden has never lifted a weight in his life, has never needed to, and is furious with everyone who has. (Elite)

speaker: (narration)
before: At the bottom of the prison: one cell, one prisoner, one very long breath.
after: At the very bottom of the prison there is a single cell, and from inside it comes one long, slow breath.

speaker: (narration)
before: The warden drops his keyring. At the end of the corridor, behind a door with no handle, someone is doing a very slow, very controlled push-up.
after: The warden's keyring clatters to the floor. At the end of the corridor, behind a door with no handle, someone is doing a push-up so slow and controlled it seems to take a full minute.

speaker: (narration)
before: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, humming a training-montage tune to itself.
after: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' gear, every strap labelled by weight class. A laminated sign reads LOCKER 13 IS A STATE OF MIND. One door hangs ajar, and something inside is humming a marching tune to itself.

speaker: (narration)
before: It smells of victory, eucalyptus and somebody else's victory. It is also warm. You feel sturdier and very slightly watched.
after: The towel is still warm and smells of eucalyptus and somebody else's victory. You feel sturdier with it round your neck, and very slightly watched.

speaker: (narration)
before: Protein bars, a roll of gold and a note: 'Spotter knows.' Somewhere a whistle blows. You keep the gold and the shame.
after: Inside are protein bars, a roll of gold and a note that says 'Spotter knows.' Somewhere down the hall a whistle blows, and you leave with the gold and a guilty conscience.

speaker: (narration)
before: He miscounts your reps on purpose, to be encouraging. You leave taller, if not stronger, and he presses a Gym Bro's number into your hand.
after: The ghost miscounts your reps on purpose, always upward, to be encouraging. You walk away standing taller, if not stronger, and he presses a Gym Bro's number into your hand.

speaker: (narration)
before: A barricade of stacked weight plates, painted regulation red. Behind it, a ferret in a pinstriped suit is timing a guard's push-ups with a silver stopwatch.
after: Someone has built a barricade out of weight plates painted regulation red. Behind it, a ferret in a pinstriped suit is timing a guard's push-ups with a silver stopwatch.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Forty-one. Forty-two. Stop. Eleven percent slower than yesterday. We will discuss it at your review.
after: Forty-one, forty-two, and stop. Eleven percent slower than yesterday, which we will discuss at your review.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: And you. You walked in at a pace of seven out of ten. Disappointing. But measurable.
after: And you walked in at a pace of seven out of ten. Disappointing, but at least it's measurable.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: Hold still. I'm measuring you. Grip: low. Stride: uneven. Resolve... unusually high. That is an inefficiency. Let's remove it.
after: Hold still while I measure you. Grip, low. Stride, uneven. Resolve... unusually high, and that is an inefficiency I intend to remove.

speaker: Vivienne Quota, Minister of Efficiency
before: I will note it. I note everything. The Chancellor will not enjoy this figure.
after: I'll note it, the way I note everything. The Chancellor is not going to enjoy this figure.

speaker: (narration)
before: You face Chancellor Clench's personal guard. Their uniforms are pressed; their technique could use ironing out. (Elite)
after: You face Chancellor Clench's personal guard, whose uniforms are pressed to perfection and whose technique is mostly shouting. (Elite)

speaker: (narration)
before: Trophies of every leader the regime ever overthrew. There is an empty one for Grandmaster Flex.
after: The regime keeps a trophy for every leader it ever overthrew, and one pedestal stands empty, waiting for Grandmaster Flex.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: Careful, son. The guards time their rounds by their squats.
after: Quietly, son. The guards time their rounds by counting their squats, and they lose count.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: Their squats are not regular, so neither are the rounds. Listen for the knees on the stairs.
after: So the rounds come whenever they come. Listen for knees cracking on the stairs, and you'll hear them in good time.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You're Grandmaster Flex? You're... smaller than the posters.
after: You're Grandmaster Flex? Everyone up there talks about you as if you were twice this size.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: Ten years in the dark does that. They took the plates, the protein, the pump. I had nothing.
after: Ten years in the dark will do that. They took my plates, my protein, every bar I ever lifted, and left me with nothing at all.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: So I had everything. My breath. My body. My mind.
after: And nothing, it turns out, is a fine place to start. I still had my breath, my body and my mind, so I trained them every day.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: Come, son. We will climb out together. And I would like a word with Clench. He was the best student I ever had.
after: Come, son, we'll climb out together. I'd like a word with Clench on the way. He was the best student I ever had. He still is.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: "Breathe in. Hold. Breathe out," says Grandmaster Flex.
after: "Breathe in slowly and hold it. Now let it all go," says Grandmaster Flex, breathing along with you.

speaker: Trophy Hall Honor Guard
before: This trophy is reserved. For the Chancellor. For anyone but you.
after: Reserves, off your pedestal! This trophy belongs to the Chancellor, not to some stranger off the wheels!

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: Chancellor Clench stands before an enormous bench press, the only weight left in the whole House of Gains. It is his.
after: Chancellor Clench stands in front of an enormous bench press, the only weight left in the whole House of Gains, and he guards it like a throne.

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: "Master." The word sticks in his throat. "I was your best, you know. Your star pupil."
after: "Master." The word sticks in his throat. "I was your best, you know - your star pupil."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: "You said I would go further than you ever did. Then you said strength lived in the heart and the head. I knew better."
after: "You told me I'd go further than you ever did. Then you started on about strength living in the heart and the head, and I knew better."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: "I took your iron, your protein, your followers. You have come back with nothing, Master."
after: "I took your iron, your protein and your followers, and you've climbed back up here with nothing, Master."

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: "Look how far I went, Master. What do you think you can do?"
after: "Look how far I went, Master. What exactly do you think you can do about it now?"

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: Strength is control. Control is paperwork. Paperwork is HEAVY. Two more plates!
after: Control is strength, paperwork is control, and do you know how HEAVY paperwork gets? Two more plates!

speaker: (narration)
before: The regime's throne room is a gym with a single throne-shaped bench press. It is the only barbell in the House.
after: The regime's throne room is a gym with one throne-shaped bench press in it, the only barbell left in the House.

speaker: (narration)
before: "Nobody goes down," he says. "Unless."
after: "Nobody goes down," he says. Then, after a long and meaningful pause: "Unless..."

speaker: (narration)
before: You win the wrestle. He wins the first three rounds of it. The way down is open, and so is your lip.
after: You win the wrestle, though he wins the first three rounds of it. The way down is open, and so is your lip.

speaker: (narration)
before: He will guard it with his life until you leave. Then it is yours again.
after: He'll guard it with his life until you leave the House, and then it's yours again.

speaker: (narration)
before: You see no bar or bench, only stone worn smooth by ten years of training. Your chest tightens at the sight of the cell; you do not know why.
after: There's no bar or bench in the cell, only stone worn smooth by ten years of training. Something about the bare walls tightens your chest, and you couldn't say why.

speaker: (narration)
before: The lock gives. Grandmaster Flex rises, slowly, unsteadily, and bows. He is so thin you could count his ribs.
after: The lock gives. Grandmaster Flex rises slowly, a little unsteady on his feet, and bows to you. He is so thin you could count his ribs.

speaker: (narration)
before: You read the plate on the empty pedestal: GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING). It has been dusted. Recently.
after: The plate on the empty pedestal reads GRANDMASTER FLEX (PENDING), and someone has dusted it very recently.

speaker: (narration)
before: Medals jingle. Grandmaster Flex winces. "They are not ours to take.
