after: The medals jingle as you scoop them up, and Grandmaster Flex winces. "They are not ours to take, son."

speaker: (narration)
before: Still. The regime owes this house a debt, and gold settles debts." You feel a little guilty, and a little richer.
after: "Still, the regime owes this house a great deal, and gold settles debts." You feel a little guilty, and a little richer.

speaker: (narration)
before: Some things are not for taking. Grandmaster Flex nods once, slowly, in approval.
after: You leave the hall exactly as you found it, and Grandmaster Flex gives you one slow nod of approval.

speaker: Chancellor Clench
before: You bring that... that stick of a man into my house? Look at him, Master. Ten years on bread and water.
after: You brought that... that stick of a man into MY house? Look at you, Master. Ten years on bread and water, and you still won't stay down.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: Hold my coat.
after: Stand back a little, son. It has been a long time, and I would like some room.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: You only ever took the weight. I taught you the heart, and you stopped listening before I got to the mind.
after: You only ever wanted the weight, my boy. I was teaching you the heart, and you stopped listening before I ever got to the mind.

speaker: Chancellor Clench
before: ...What. How. Where were you HIDING all of that?
after: ...How? Ten years in a hole with nothing - where were you HIDING all of that?

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: True strength is not the ability to lift heavy things. It comes from the heart, and from the mind.
after: Strength was never about how heavy a thing is, Clench. It lives in the heart and the mind, and nobody can lock those in a cell.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex
before: The heavy things were only ever practice. Now, my boy. Shall we?
after: The heavy things were only ever practice, my boy. Now, shall we?

speaker: Chancellor Clench, Iron Regent
before: Chancellor Clench stands before an enormous bench press, the only weight left in the whole House of Gains. It is his.
after: Chancellor Clench stands in front of an enormous bench press, the only weight left in the whole House of Gains, and he guards it like a throne.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: Flex does not gloat. He kneels beside his fallen pupil and offers a hand. "You hated yourself for needing the iron, my boy.
after: Flex doesn't gloat. He kneels beside his fallen pupil and offers him a hand. "You hated yourself for needing the iron, my boy.

speaker: (narration)
before: You watch Grandmaster Flex enter the throne room in his prison rags. No one speaks.
after: Grandmaster Flex walks into the throne room in his prison rags, and the whole hall falls silent.

speaker: (narration)
before: You hear him breathe in, slow and even. Ten years without iron have left him thin.
after: He breathes in, slow and even. Ten years without iron have worn him thin as wire, but he stands perfectly straight.

speaker: (narration)
before: Before you, the ruler of the House of Gains takes one step back.
after: Across the room, the ruler of the House of Gains takes one step back.

speaker: Gym attendant
before: The weights are back! I cried. Then I did a set. Then I cried again.
after: The weights are back! I cried, then I did a set, and then I cried all over again.

speaker: (narration)
before: Ask a Beefcake. They have loads. And now they keep it.
after: Ask any Beefcake. They have loads of it, and now they get to keep some.

speaker: (narration)
before: Back under the old management. The old management is still jacked.
after: Back under the old management. The old management can still bench a hay cart.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: YOU DID IT. Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch. Best day since... since the last best day. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.
after: You did it! Flex is out, Clench is down, and I got to watch the whole thing. Best day since... oh, since the last best day, whenever that was. I'm spotting you from now on, like it or not.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: The weights are back in the gym. There's Gary, lifting. With a spotter. Beautiful. Before you go... that boy I told you about, the old king's son, at the Festival.
after: Weights back in the gym, and there's Gary, lifting with a proper spotter. Beautiful. Before you go... that boy I told you about, the old king's son, at the Festival...

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: When you lifted that last regime brute, you made the same face he did. Exactly the same face.
after: When you heaved that last regime brute off his feet, you made the same face he made on my dumbbell. The very same face. Funny, the things you remember.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Free, strong and spotted. Thank you, friend. I climbed Swolympus once, you know. These ten years were steeper.
after: Free, strong and properly spotted, all of us. Thank you, friend. I climbed Swolympus once, you know, and these ten years were steeper.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: That gate up on the overlook? Sealed. Opens when the kingdom is whole again. Not a day before. I asked it nicely.
after: That gate up on the overlook is still sealed. It opens when the kingdom is whole again, and not a day before. I asked it nicely. Twice.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: Foreman Gus. Still on the wheels. Listen to that.
after: Foreman Gus, still on the wheels. But listen to them now - not a single whistle.

speaker: Foreman Gus
before: I might cry into the wheel for energy. Voluntarily, for once.
after: I might even take a day off. No idea how it's done, but I hear you start by sitting down.

speaker: Coach Brutus Benchley
before: CARDS ON SHELVES, IRON ON RACKS! I can finally shout about the floorboard, and I'VE FORGOTTEN HOW!
after: CARDS ON SHELVES, IRON ON RACKS! And I don't have to whisper about the floorboard any more, which is good, because I WAS NEVER ANY GOOD AT IT!

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: Welcome, friend. Grandmaster Flex. Ten years in the dark, and the first thing I wanted was a window. The second was a stretch.
after: Welcome, friend. Grandmaster Flex, at your service. After ten years in the dark, the first thing I wanted was a window, and the second was a good long stretch.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: They took my plates, my protein, my pre-workout. So I breathed. Breathe in. Hold. ...That is what I did for ten years.
after: They took my plates, my protein, everything I had ever lifted. So I breathed: in, hold, and out again. That is what I did for ten years, and it was enough.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: I counted my own heartbeats until they became songs. They thought they were breaking me. They were teaching me.
after: I counted my own heartbeats until they turned into songs. They thought they were breaking me down there, son, but they were teaching me.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: Clench is learning to lift from zero. The strongest take the longest. Yesterday he spotted Gary without being asked. The gym is open to everyone now; come whenever you like.
after: Clench is learning to lift from zero, and the strongest always take the longest. Yesterday he spotted Gary without being asked. The gym is open to everyone now, so come whenever you like.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: Quota's gone. Left for the Capital before the dust settled. She always did leave early.
after: Quota's gone, off to the Capital before the dust had even settled. She always did like to leave early.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: We'll keep the schedule. It will make good kindling. Breathe, son. Nobody here is on the clock any more.
after: We'll keep her schedule, since it will make good kindling. And breathe, son - nobody here is on the clock any more.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: She's back. The real Grand Chef. She tasted my soup and said 'more salt' and I have never been so happy.
after: She's back - the real Grand Chef. She tasted my soup, frowned and said 'more salt', and I have never been so happy in my life.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The pantry door stays wide open, and people come in for biscuits. At last, a proper open-door pastry.
after: The pantry door stays wide open now, and people wander in for biscuits all day long. I keep a tin by the hinge for them.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: A friendly duel? For old times' sake. Loser washes the ladle. It is a very big ladle.
after: Fancy a friendly duel, for old times' sake? Loser washes the ladle, and I should warn you, it's a very big ladle.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: An enormous pantry door blocks the lane. Locked. The keyhole is the size of a dinner plate.
after: An enormous pantry door blocks the lane, locked tight, with a keyhole the size of a dinner plate.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: Chef Fennel Gravois hands over a key the size of a ladle. It turns with a satisfying clunk.
after: Chef Fennel Gravois hands over a key the size of a ladle, and it turns in the lock with a satisfying clunk.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The great pantry door swings open. Somewhere beyond, something smells incredible. Underneath it, faintly, something smells of hot iron.
after: The great pantry door swings open on a smell of roasting meat and fresh bread, and underneath it, faintly, the smell of hot iron.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: TASTE IT. TASTE IT! The Special Sauce is in everything. My soup. My tea. My SOUL.
after: TASTE IT! The Special Sauce is in everything now - my soup, my tea, my very SOUL - and isn't it WONDERFUL?

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The pantry is closed by order of the Grand Chef. The key stays on my apron. For the war effort!
after: The pantry is closed by order of the Grand Chef, and the key stays on my apron. It's all for the war effort!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: You want in? Beat me first. Yes, Chef! No, YOU, Chef!
after: You want the key? You'll have to beat me for it! Yes, Chef! No - YOU, Chef!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois
before: TASTE IT. It is for the war effort. The BISCUIT is for the war effort.
after: TASTE IT! Even the BISCUIT is for the war effort!

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The simmer let go. The sauce let go. Plain bread. No sauce. I could weep. I am weeping.
after: The sauce has let go of me. Is that plain bread, with no sauce on it at all? I could weep. In fact, I am weeping.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own sauces. The real one ALWAYS tasted. Same face. Ask yourself who was wearing the apron.
after: The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own sauces years ago, and the Chef I trained under ALWAYS tasted. Same face, same apron... so who has been wearing it?

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The Test Kitchen is at the far end of the Buffet, and it was never making casserole. Take a biscuit. Take two. Heroes need carbs.
after: Whatever's wrong here starts in the Test Kitchen, at the far end of the Buffet, and it was never making casserole. Take a biscuit for the road. Take two.

speaker: Chef Fennel Gravois, Keeper of the Pantry Key
before: The pantry door stays shut until you learn to cook. Consider this a closed-course meal.
after: The pantry door stays shut until you've learned to cook. Come back when you're properly seasoned!

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: The great pantry door is locked and the chef with the key is extremely seasoned. Win the key and find out what the Grand Chef is really cooking.
after: The great pantry door is locked, and Chef Fennel Gravois won't give up the key. Win it, and find out what's really cooking in the Grand Chef's kitchens.

speaker: (narration)
before: Your HP is already full. A chef refills your plate anyway. Here, being full is treated as a misunderstanding.
after: Your HP is already full, but a chef refills your plate anyway. Around here, being full is treated as a misunderstanding.

speaker: Basil
before: "You fainted into the gravy, so we fished you out. There's a fishing fee... sorry, sorry, I don't set the catch of the day.
after: "You fainted into the gravy, so we fished you out. There's a, um, fishing fee... sorry. Sorry! I don't set the prices, I just hold the ladle.

speaker: Basil
before: Don't tell the taste testers. If anyone asks, say 'Yes, Chef.' It works for everything."
after: Don't tell the taste testers you fainted. If anyone asks you anything, just say 'Yes, Chef.' It works for everything."

speaker: (narration)
before: The fountain's tank is dry for now. It refills on your next visit. Soup takes time.
after: The fountain's tank is dry for now. Soup takes time, and it will be full again on your next visit.

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: Real saffron. It grows in the Candy Field. Ask a sous-chef if you are lost."
after: Real saffron, mind you, which grows in the Candy Field. Ask a sous-chef if you lose your way."

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: That is Basil's request. Speak to Basil in the Grand Pantry. Yes, Chef!"
after: It is Basil's request, so speak to Basil in the Grand Pantry. Yes, Chef!"

speaker: (narration)
before: Hop on when it docks. Ride. Hop off on the other side.
after: Hop on when it docks and hop off on the other side.

speaker: (narration)
before: Step on at one side. Step off at the other. Patience is a garnish.
after: Step on at one side and off at the other. Patience is a garnish.

speaker: (narration)
before: (There is no change. It is gravy. Everything is gravy.)
after: (There is no change. Everything here is gravy.)

speaker: (narration)
before: Sharp cheese ahead. Do not lean on or lick the walls; we cannot keep putting this delicately.
after: Sharp cheese ahead. Please do not lean on the walls, and please, please do not lick them.

speaker: (narration)
before: Read the recipe card. Vibes are not one of the four ingredients.
after: Read the recipe card. Guessing is not one of the four ingredients.

speaker: (narration)
before: Pure momentum with a side of sauce. A failed prototype that escaped. Nobody knows what it is running from. It is probably the cannon.
after: A failed prototype meatball, all momentum and sauce, that escaped the Test Kitchen and hasn't stopped rolling since. Whatever it's running from, it's probably the cannon.

speaker: Basil
before: Psst. Basil, line cook. Ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it: chefs cook, golems guard. Lately the golems have been... practising.
after: Psst. I'm Basil, line cook - ladle in one hand, nerves in the other. We Gourmands feed the kingdom and protect it: the chefs cook and the golems guard. Lately, though, the golems have been... practising.

speaker: Basil
before: Ten years ago {villain}'s people came to the Buffet, and the Grand Chef... changed. Chef ALWAYS tastes, and this Chef doesn't. She just smiles at the soup.
after: Ten years ago {villain}'s people came to the Buffet, and after that the Grand Chef... changed. Chef ALWAYS tastes, and this Chef never does. She just stands there smiling at the soup.

speaker: Basil
before: She put the Special Sauce in every pot. Our rules: nobody leaves hungry, nobody double-dips, and we say "Yes, Chef." Quietly. Nobody asks about the Test Kitchen. I'm not asking.
after: Then she put the Special Sauce in every pot. The old rules still hold - nobody leaves hungry, nobody double-dips, and we say "Yes, Chef." Quietly. And nobody asks about the Test Kitchen. I'm not asking.

speaker: Basil
before: You came back... good, good. A Gourmand never stops stirring, so technically this panic is a cooking method.
after: You came back! Good, good. I've been stirring the same pot for an hour, just to give my hands something to do. A Gourmand never stops stirring.

speaker: Basil
before: Chef laughed for a week. Last month I mentioned that cake to her, and she didn't remember it. Chef remembers every cake she's ever baked.
after: Chef laughed about it for a week. Last month I mentioned that cake to her, and she didn't remember it at all - and Chef remembers every cake she's ever baked.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: We're always out of something. Honey, basil, ghost pepper... half our deliveries go to the Test Kitchen, and nothing comes back. I once fetched a whole pig. Wrong pig. It's still angry.
after: We're always out of something - honey, basil, ghost pepper. Half our deliveries go to the Test Kitchen and nothing comes back. I once fetched them a whole pig. Wrong pig, and he's still cross about it.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Madame Mirepoix. Dessert dealer and card shark of the Grand Pantry. Tonight's tasting menu: three cards, lightly foiled, served with disdain.
after: Madame Mirepoix, darling: dessert dealer and card shark of the Grand Pantry. Tonight's tasting menu is three cards, lightly foiled, served with a little disdain.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: Gourmand-issue, inspected by the Test Kitchen as of this year. They stamped my decorative cake. Right on the rosette. I have not forgiven them.
after: Every card is Gourmand-issue and, as of this year, inspected by the Test Kitchen. They stamped my decorative cake, darling, right on the rosette, and I have not forgiven them.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: You can fetch? Wonderful! We need three ingredients, quick. Our stolen deliveries are scattered all over the Buffet: truffle by the broccoli, salt by the river, honey up the Butte.
after: You can fetch? Oh, wonderful. Our deliveries keep getting stolen and dropped all over the Buffet: there's truffle by the broccoli, salt by the river and honey up the Butte.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Pick up any three and come back. I'll make it worth your while. I'm begging with my whole apron.
after: Bring me any three and I'll make it worth your while. I'm begging with my whole apron here.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Three whole ingredients! The Pantry is saved! For today!
after: Three whole ingredients! The Pantry is saved - for today, anyway, which is the only day I'm worried about.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: Here, a little something. It's a card. It's soup. It's soup you can play.
after: Here, take this for your trouble. It's a card, and somehow it's also a soup. Soup you can play, if you can believe it.

speaker: Sous-Chef Tarragon
before: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. I'm not complaining. I'm fetching. They look similar from a distance.
after: The pantry's stocked until tomorrow, when we do it all again. I'm not complaining, I'm fetching. From a distance they look very similar.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: I am going to cry. Discreetly. Here is your reward, you scrappy little thing. Thank you.
after: And so am I, discreetly. Here is your reward, you scrappy little thing, and thank you.

speaker: Basil
before: Um. A word? Quietly? Old Meatloaf, our oldest golem, has stopped working. The Test Kitchen tried to strip him for parts. We got him back in two pieces. He hasn't spoken since Tuesday.
after: Um, could I have a word? Quietly? Old Meatloaf, our oldest golem, has stopped working. The Test Kitchen tried to strip him for parts, and we only got him back in two pieces. He hasn't spoken since Tuesday.

speaker: Basil
before: He's walking! He's sizzling! Old Meatloaf is back on duty! I'm not crying. I'm standing near onions.
after: He's walking, and he's sizzling! Old Meatloaf is back on duty! I'm not crying, I'm just standing near some onions.

speaker: Basil
before: Old Meatloaf is the best golem in the kingdom. Don't tell the others. They know.
after: Old Meatloaf is the best golem in the kingdom. Don't tell the others - they already know, and they're very gracious about it.

speaker: Old Meatloaf and the gate golems
before: He says it to you. You are not a chef. He does not mind.
after: He says it to you, though you are not a chef. He doesn't mind.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: I have never found a recipe for the Special Sauce. I looked. I even licked the index.
after: I have never found a recipe for the Special Sauce, and believe me, I looked. I even licked the index.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: One. A pinch of knowledge, barely seasoned. Here is a small token. It is a thimble of encouragement.
after: One. A pinch of knowledge, barely seasoned, so here is a small token: a thimble of encouragement.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Two. Half-baked. A fine place to start. Half-baked things can still be rescued.
after: Two. Half-baked, which is a fine place to start; half-baked things can always be rescued.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Three! Nearly perfect. Perfect would make me suspicious. Take your reward and a warm roll.
after: Three! Nearly perfect, and perfect would only make me suspicious. Take your reward and a warm roll.

speaker: Professor Pate
before: Not a pass. Wrong, but deliciously wrong. Walk the Endless Buffet, read the signs, and come back. There is no limit on attempts.
after: Not a pass, I'm afraid - wrong, but deliciously wrong. Walk the Endless Buffet, read the signs and come back; there's no limit on attempts.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Seven seasons on tape, and people STILL do my WHOOSH! Please rewind; the dramatic entrance is at the beginning.
after: Seven seasons on the air, and people STILL do my WHOOSH in the street! I'd do it for you now, but I save it for the cameras.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: My Turbo Tots toys were recalled. Not for safety: for spinning too well. Tonight's audience is ten sprouts and a very patient cloche. Let's COOK!
after: My Turbo Tots toys were recalled for spinning too well, and tonight's audience is ten sprouts and a very patient cloche. But the show goes on! Let's COOK!

speaker: (minigame host)
before: Back for another shift, champ? The cameras are always rolling. They are not. They ran out of film in two-thousand-three. Smile anyway.
after: Back for another shift, champ? Smile for the cameras! They ran out of film years ago, but a professional smiles anyway.

speaker: (minigame host)
before: Remember: the ticket is your friend. The ticket does not judge. The ticket is judging, but kindly.
after: Remember, the ticket is your friend. It's judging you, of course, but kindly.

speaker: Chef Flambe Fontaine
before: Your very first shift on the show! Here is your bonus, free, no obligation. It is a scroll.
after: Your very first shift on the show! Here's your bonus, free and with no obligation: a scroll!

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A single sad bubble rises. It pops. That was all it had to say.
after: A single sad bubble rises and pops. That was all it had to say.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Just measuring. Mind you, the Chef's soups add years to people. Bad for business. Good for everybody else. Heh.
after: Just measuring. Mind you, the Chef's soups add years to people, which is bad for business and good for everybody else. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Appointments. Let's see now... you're not down for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.

speaker: Colonel Casserole
before: Halt, traveller. This gate opens for a duel of honour. Lids up. Yes, Chef.
after: Halt, traveller! This gate opens only for a duel of honour, so lids up. Yes, Chef.

speaker: Madame Mirepoix
before: This deck is underdressed, darling. A little butter. A little foil. Voila.
after: This deck is underdressed, darling. A little butter, a little foil, and voila.

speaker: The Grand Chef (formerly Grand Chef Escoffina)
before: Have you eaten? Sit. Eat. Then save the kingdom. In that order.
after: Have you eaten? Sit. Eat. The kingdom can wait until you've had your soup.

speaker: The Grand Chef (formerly Grand Chef Escoffina)
before: A full table is a safe table. Pull up a chair. That is an order.
after: A full table is a safe table. Pull up a chair, dear - that's an order.

speaker: The Doppelganger (later named Escoffina)
before: I tasted my soup today. As me. Too salty. It was mine.
after: I tasted my own soup today, as me. Too salty, but it was mine.

speaker: The Doppelganger (later named Escoffina)
before: Third-class apprentice. Many dishes. I am trying. The dishes are also trying.
after: I am a third-class apprentice now, with many dishes. I am trying. So are the dishes.

speaker: Basil
before: Over here. Quietly. Have you ever eaten somewhere with no menu? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.
after: Over here, quietly. Have you ever eaten somewhere with no menu at all? ...I'm brave. I'm brave.

speaker: Basil
before: The card is in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. Golden. You'll know it. Chef always said gold means sit down.
after: The card's in one of the hidden stashes around the Buffet. It's golden, so you'll know it when you see it. Chef always said gold means sit down.

speaker: Basil
before: That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited. I think. It feels a lot like the other thing.
after: That's it! One seat, three courses, survival optional. I'm excited, I think - it feels a lot like being terrified.

speaker: (narration)
before: You pass incoming ingredient crates and outgoing unlabelled ones. Research appears to be a one-way conversation.
after: You pass crates of ingredients going in and unlabelled crates coming out, and nothing in between that looks like a meal.

speaker: (narration)
before: Frozen failures line the walls. Some of them are still moving. One of the freezers is humming louder than the rest.
after: Frozen failures line the walls, and some of them are still moving. One freezer hums louder than the rest, as if something inside wants to be heard.

speaker: (narration)
before: A hot meal, an honest one. The only unmodified food in the building. Restore HP.
after: A hot, honest meal: the only unmodified food in the building. Restore HP.

speaker: (narration)
before: The unfinished war machine looms. It is enormous, held together by gravy and willpower.
after: The unfinished war machine looms over you, enormous, and held together by gravy and willpower.

speaker: (narration)
before: The cook behind the counter whispers: "The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own soup ten years ago. Nobody noticed. Everybody noticed. Nobody said."
after: The cook behind the counter leans in and whispers: "The Grand Chef stopped tasting her own soup ten years ago. Every one of us noticed, and not one of us said a word."

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Inspection! ATTEN-TION! Who put a dent in my souffle cannon? Battle stations! This is not a drill, it is a souffle!
after: ATTEN-TION! Inspection! Who put a dent in my souffle cannon? Battle stations, all of you! This is not a drill, it is a souffle, and it will rise on schedule!

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: And what is THIS? A civilian. In my bay. Unsupervised. With flavour on his breath.
after: And what is THIS? A civilian, unsupervised, in my bay, with flavour on his breath. Disgraceful.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense. Taste is a weakness, son. Paste is a strategy.
after: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense, and you will stand up straight when you hear it. Taste is a weakness, son. Paste is a strategy.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Whisk formation! Field-test the prototype on the intruder. I have a ration meeting.
after: Whisk formation! Field-test the prototype on the intruder while I attend a ration meeting. I want a full report, and I want it bland.

speaker: (narration)
before: He salutes the machine. The machine salutes back with a ladle. The Colonel marches out before it has finished preheating.
after: He salutes the machine, the machine salutes back with a ladle, and the Colonel marches out before it has finished preheating.

speaker: (narration)
before: It is delicious. It is probably cursed. You feel strong and slightly sticky, and your units will not stop smelling of gravy.
after: It is delicious and almost certainly cursed. You feel strong and slightly sticky, and your units will not stop smelling of gravy.

speaker: (narration)
before: Some of the pantry is still clean. The jars are labelled DO NOT OPEN, WE MEAN IT. You do not open them. You sell them.
after: A few shelves are still clean, stacked with jars labelled DO NOT OPEN, WE MEAN IT. You respect their wishes and sell them unopened.

speaker: (narration)
before: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every note signed by the Grand Chef is in perfect copperplate, without one gravy stain. Real chefs' notes are mostly gravy stain.
after: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every note signed by the Grand Chef is in perfect copperplate without a single gravy stain, and a real chef's notes are mostly gravy stain.

speaker: (narration)
before: The chef who wrote these has never held a ladle. The impostor is exposed, and so is how little they have been cooking.
after: Laid beside the old recipe cards, it is plain: whoever signed these memos has never held a ladle. The person giving orders in this kitchen is not the cook who used to.

speaker: (narration)
before: Evidence, and a buyer for it. The buyer asks no questions, which is the best kind of buyer.
after: Blueprints like these are evidence, and evidence always has a buyer. The one you find asks no questions, which is the best kind.

speaker: Cannon-Blender Gunner
before: Load the smoothie! Purée setting! FIRE!
after: Load the smoothie, set it to puree, and FIRE!

speaker: The Doppelganger, later Escoffina
before: The Grand Chef turns from the stove. She smiles the smile from every portrait in the Pantry. She has worn it for ten years without a crease.
after: The Grand Chef turns from the stove wearing the smile from every portrait in the Pantry, and in ten years it has never once creased.

speaker: The Doppelganger, later Escoffina
before: "Ah. A taste tester. Welcome to the future of dining. The future is efficient. The future does not need to be tasted."
after: "Ah, a taste tester. Welcome to the future of dining, which is efficient, and which does not need to be tasted."

speaker: The Doppelganger
before: Welcome to the Test Kitchen. Everything here is delicious. I have been told.
after: Welcome to the Test Kitchen. Everything here is delicious, or so I have been told.

speaker: The Doppelganger
before: Delicious. Delicious. I have been told that is the word. ...Why will it not stay on?
after: Delicious... delicious. I was told that is the word. ...Why will this face not stay on?

speaker: The Doppelganger
before: You never taste your own soup, do you? ...Neither do I. I cannot.
after: They always asked whether I tasted the soup. ...I never did. I never could.

speaker: The Doppelganger, later Escoffina
before: The Grand Chef's private kitchen. Her apron is spotless. Her chin is a little off.
after: The Grand Chef's private kitchen. Her apron is spotless, and something about her chin is a little off.

speaker: (narration)
before: A sous-chef is hiding behind the sacks of flour. "She does not taste the soup," he whispers. "She never tastes the soup.
after: A sous-chef is crouched behind the sacks of flour, shaking. "She doesn't taste the soup," he whispers. "Not once, not in ten years.

speaker: (narration)
before: He eats like a man who has not eaten in a week. "Thank you," he says. "Be careful.
after: He eats like a man who hasn't had a proper meal in a week, and when he's finished he grips your hand. "Thank you. Please be careful.

speaker: (narration)
before: The real Chef is down there somewhere. I know she is." You feel better for it.
after: The real Chef is down there somewhere. I know she is." You leave feeling better for having fed him.

speaker: The Doppelganger
before: They never looked at their Chef. They looked at the food.
after: They never looked at their Chef, only at the food.

speaker: The Doppelganger
before: "Delicious." That is the word I was given for it. I say it often. I do not know what it means.
after: "Delicious" is the word I was given for it. I say it often, and I have never known what it means.

speaker: The Doppelganger
before: I have no name or face of my own. I cannot even taste what I make.
after: I have no face of my own and no name, and I cannot even taste what I make. I do not know what is left of me.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: How will they know it's you? After ten years?
after: After ten years, how will they know it's really you?

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: Not with a speech. Not with papers. With dinner.
after: Not with a speech, and not with papers. With dinner.

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: Come here, you. No face, no name. What you are called does not matter. What you do is what matters.
after: Come here, you. No face and no name, and I don't care a crumb about either. What you're called doesn't matter half as much as what you do.

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: You wore my face for ten years and never once learned to taste. Today you start. Let me give you something to start with.
after: You wore my face for ten years and never once learned to taste. Today you start, and I'll give you something to start with.

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: So take my old name. Escoffina. I was always prouder of the work than of the title.
after: Take my old name, then: Escoffina. I was always prouder of the work than of the title, and the name could do with someone starting fresh.

speaker: Escoffina
before: ...Escoffina. I will try to cook honestly. I will try to be someone worth the name.
after: ...Escoffina. I will try to cook honestly, and to become someone worth the name.

speaker: (UI)
before: Leaving the Endless Buffet ends this visit. Town heals you fully. The golems are back to guarding plates, not people. The buffet is still endless.
after: Leaving the Endless Buffet ends this visit. Town heals you fully. The golems guard plates again instead of people, and the buffet is as endless as ever.

speaker: (narration)
before: Nobody leaves hungry. Innovation Season is over. Dinner is back.
after: Nobody leaves hungry. Innovation Season is over, and dinner is back.

speaker: (narration)
before: The taste testers are free. They like food again. Please give them seconds.
after: Our taste testers are free and enjoying food again. Please give them seconds.

speaker: (narration)
before: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet; we just mopped. Free samples by the door. Take two. Nobody is checking.
after: To {town}, through the great pantry door. Wipe your feet, as we have just mopped, and take two free samples on your way out. Nobody is checking.

speaker: (narration)
before: The repurposed cannon now fires bread at pigeons. This is what we meant by a feeding programme.
after: The old cannon has been refitted to fire bread rolls for the pigeons, who have never been happier.

speaker: Basil
before: The real Chef is back in her own kitchen, tasting her own soup. We all cried. Say it with me: Yes, Chef. Louder. YES, CHEF! ...Oh, that felt good. We mean it this time.
after: The real Chef is back in her own kitchen, tasting her own soup, and we all cried into our aprons. Yes, Chef. YES, CHEF! ...Sorry. I whispered it for ten years, and it feels so good to mean it.

speaker: Basil
before: The Special Sauce is down the drain and the golems guard plates again. Yes, Chef - finally an order I can stomach!

before: A small grey machine offers you a ticket. The display above says NOW SERVING 3. Your number is 4,000,213. A polite ghost behind you coughs, then apologises for coughing.

speaker: (narration)
before: You wait. You wait some more. You feel seen, and slightly worse. A vending machine dispenses one sad cookie.

speaker: (narration)
before: Nobody dares object. Yet. Number 4,000,213 is quietly becoming a legend.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: A very comfortable waiting room. The magazines are 600 years old. Restore HP.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: Every important document in the Hall is stamped, signed and witnessed here. The transfer of authority was, too. The notary is still finding blue-green feathers.
after: Every important document in the Hall is stamped, signed and witnessed here, the transfer of authority included. The notary is still finding blue-green feathers.

speaker: (narration)
before: Row after row of chairs. Can your deck outwait the line?
after: Row after row of chairs stretches into the distance. Can your deck outwait the line?

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: The clock is lying. The clock was told to.
after: The clock is lying, and from the look of it, somebody ordered it to.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: It is flawless. Submitted, reviewed, approved, notarized, filed.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Someone should look into it, dear. This form does not tell us what happened to the boy."
after: Someone should look into it, dear, because this form doesn't tell us what happened to the boy."

speaker: Notary Wraith
before: Signed. Witnessed. Notarized. In triplicate. One copy is for you. You may not keep it.
after: Signed, witnessed and notarized in triplicate. One copy is for you, but you may not keep it.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Two aisles over, Agnes is filling in a form with a very stubby pencil. "Form 27-C. Third attempt. It needs a 27-B, which needs a 27-C.
after: Two aisles over, Agnes is filling in a form with a very stubby pencil. "Form 27-C, third attempt. It needs a 27-B, which needs a 27-C.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: They keep stamping it DENIED. Irregular, apparently. Do not mind me, dear. I have filed worse and kept the receipts."
after: They keep stamping it DENIED and writing Irregular in the margin. Don't mind me, dear. I've filed worse and kept the receipts."

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: Every form here has a twin. Every twin has a twin. The clerks are undead and, understandably, a bit short.
after: Every form here has a twin, and every twin has a twin of its own. The clerks are undead and, understandably, a bit short.

speaker: (narration)
before: It works! Mostly. Something in the ceiling disapproves, loudly, with a stapler.
after: It works, mostly. Something in the ceiling disapproves loudly, with a stapler.

speaker: (narration)
before: Nothing is left of Number 4,000,213. You feel lighter, and slightly nonexistent. The machine files you under 'Resolved.'
after: Nothing is left of Number 4,000,213. You feel lighter and slightly nonexistent as the machine files you under 'Resolved.'

speaker: (narration)
before: You pull out half of a lost appeal. It is, technically, a weapon. The machine takes a bite of you in exchange.
after: You pull out half of a lost appeal, which is technically a weapon, and the machine takes a bite of you in exchange.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No, looks up from an infinite pile of paperwork. His face is as smooth as a blank form. His stamp is the size of a tombstone.
after: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No, looks up from an endless pile of paperwork, his face as smooth as a blank form and his stamp the size of a tombstone.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: The answer is no. The question is irrelevant. Please state your case anyway.
after: The answer is no. The question is irrelevant, but you may state your case anyway.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: The answer is no. The question is irrelevant. Please state your case anyway.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: You wait. And wait. A clerk takes pity, and the polite ghost ahead of you shares a biscuit and apologises that it is stale.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: The Expedite Fee is an official fee, with an official receipt. A tiny clerk stamps your ticket and a door opens. You feel oddly refreshed.
after: The Expedite Fee is an official fee with an official receipt. A tiny clerk stamps your ticket, a door opens, and you feel oddly refreshed.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: You cut in line. Forty thousand undead clerks turn and glare. You are processed immediately, and a little roughly.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: She does not look the other way. She looks at the gold. The gold is accepted.

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: Please do not worry. Blood is optional. The signature is not."
after: Please don't worry, the blood is optional. The signature is not."

speaker: D.N.A. staff
before: You argue. A tiny stamp appears from nowhere and hits you. It hurts a little.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: The authorization was valid. It was always valid. But the office is vacant, and policy is policy."
after: The authorization was valid, and it was always valid. But the office is now vacant, and policy is policy."

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
before: The CE-No has been removed from office. By policy, the vacancy passes to the senior-most applicant on file. One moment. I will look it up.
after: The CE-No has been removed from office, and by policy the vacancy passes to the senior-most applicant on file. One moment while I look it up.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
before: ...It is a ghost. It is, for the record, you, Ms. Overdue.
after: ...The senior-most applicant is a ghost. It is, for the record, you, Ms. Overdue.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
before: The procedure is clear. The office passes to you, and I am afraid you cannot appeal it. I would have to deny it.
after: The procedure is clear: the office passes to you. You cannot appeal it, Ms. Overdue. I would only have to deny it, and I find I do not want to.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: ...Then I will stay, Mortimer. Not for you. I will stay until nobody waits as long as I did.
after: ...Then I'll stay, Mortimer, though not for you. I'll stay until nobody has to wait as long as I did.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Even the dead deserve humanity. Our job is to help the lost souls. We have an obligation to help.
after: Everyone in that queue was somebody, and the dead deserve to be treated as people. Helping the lost is the whole job. It always was.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Following orders be damned. We treat everyone with respect.
after: No order outranks that, Mortimer, not his and not yours. From today we treat everyone with respect.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby
before: ...That is not in the handbook.
after: ...That is not in the handbook. I find myself wondering why it never was.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Then we write a new one. Take a number, Mortimer. You are right behind Gerald.
after: Then we'll write a new one. Take a number and wait with the others, Mortimer. You're right behind Gerald, and he'll show you how it's done.

speaker: Kyle
before: the queue moved. like, actually moved. agnes called my number at 3am. i was afk. she called it again. nobody's ever called me twice.
after: the queue moved. it actually moved. agnes called my number at 3am and i was away from my desk, so she called it again. nobody's ever called me twice.

speaker: Kyle
before: anyway. wanna play? one more round before i pass on. jk. unless?
after: wanna play one more round before i pass on? kidding. probably.

speaker: Director Ectomund
before: Back again. The ethics questions have been returned to the building. Not yet to the exam. One reform at a time.
after: Back again, I see. The ethics questions have been returned to the building, though not yet to the exam. One reform at a time.

speaker: Director Ectomund
before: Statistically, you will still fail a question. Statistically, I will still enjoy it. Some things are not corruption. They are personality.
after: Statistically, you will still fail a question, and statistically I will still enjoy it. That is not corruption. That is personality.

speaker: (UI)
before: Leaving the D.N.A. ends this visit. Town heals you fully. You no longer need an exit permit. Nobody does. We are still a little scared of the pen.
after: Leaving the D.N.A. ends this visit. Town heals you fully, and you no longer need an exit permit. Nobody does, though we're all still a little scared of the pen.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Head of the whole Department, and still on the front desk. They gave me a big office, dear. Nobody waits in a big office. They wait here.
after: I'm head of the whole Department now, and I'm still on the front desk. They gave me a big office, dear, but nobody waits in a big office. They wait here.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Mortimer is in the Waiting Room, number 4,000,214. He is learning to wait. It is going about as well as you would expect.
after: Mortimer's in the Waiting Room as number 4,000,214, learning to wait. It's going about as well as you'd expect.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: The authorization is still valid. But there is a rule above it now: help people.
after: The authorization is still valid, dear, but there's a rule above it now: everyone who comes through that door is treated as a person.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Prudence is my deputy. She is much nicer than she used to be, and so, I hear, am I.
after: Prudence is my deputy. She's much nicer than she used to be, and so, I'm told, am I.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Oh! It's you! Gerald, barista, and as of this morning, Number 4,000,212: CALLED. I didn't know what to do with my hands. So I made coffee.
after: Oh, it's you! Gerald, barista, and as of this morning Number 4,000,212: CALLED. I didn't know what to do with my hands, so I made coffee.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Cream? None. Sugar? None. Hope? Back in stock. I am trying not to use it all at once.
after: No cream and no sugar, I'm afraid. None at all. But hope's back in stock, and I'm trying not to use it all at once.

speaker: Gerald, Number 4,000,212
before: Mortimer is Number 4,000,214 now. You were 213, in between us. Don't mention it to him. He goes very quiet.
after: Mortimer's Number 4,000,214 now, and you were 213, right between us. Don't mention it to him, though. He goes very quiet.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Requisitions. Clerk Ledgerbone. The stamp has stopped haunting. It got its raise.
after: Clerk Ledgerbone, Requisitions. The stamp has stopped haunting the place now that it got its raise.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: It doesn't know what to do with itself. Neither do I. Cards, in triplicate, as always.
after: It doesn't know what to do with itself, and neither do I. Cards, in triplicate, as always.

speaker: Clerk Ledgerbone
before: Practising. Just stood here for a minute. Nothing was filed. Exhilarating.
after: I've been practising. I just stood here for a whole minute and filed nothing at all. It was exhilarating.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: I only wanted to leave. I will. Soon. But first I'm fixing this place, so nobody else waits as long as I did.
after: I only ever wanted to leave, and I will, soon. But first I'm putting this place right, so nobody else waits as long as I did.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: Even the dead deserve humanity. Our job is to help the lost souls. Following orders be damned: we treat everyone with respect.
after: Everyone in that queue was somebody, dear, and the dead deserve to be treated as people. No order outranks that, not his and not anyone's.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: Mortimer Grimsby. Formerly CE-No. Currently number 4,000,214 in the Waiting Room of Eternity. Gerald was 4,000,212.
after: Mortimer Grimsby, formerly CE-No, currently number 4,000,214 in the Waiting Room of Eternity. Gerald was 4,000,212, and he has been very patient with me.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: You had 4,000,213. You did not wait. I keep thinking about that.
after: You had 4,000,213, and you did not wait. I keep thinking about that.

speaker: Mortimer Grimsby, CE-No
before: I made others wait far longer. It is worse knowing that now.
after: I made others wait far longer than you, and every one of them was a person. It is worse, knowing that now.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Intake's moving again! Agnes waved me straight through. First time in ten years nobody asked me for Form 27-B. Heh.
after: Intake's moving again! Agnes waved me straight through. First time in ten years nobody's asked me for Form 27-B, and my appointment book is filling up nicely.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: Archdruid Compostella is herself again. She hugged me. She smells like rain and a little bit like compost. Perfect.
after: Archdruid Compostella is herself again, and she hugged me! She smells like rain and a little bit like compost, which is exactly how an Archdruid ought to smell.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: Want a practice round? I promise not to thorn at you. Much. The raccoons are judging, so be nice.
after: Fancy a practice round? I'll try very hard not to thorn at you. The raccoons have come to watch, so let's both be on our best behaviour.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: The Rot keeps this path for the Rotheart. Turn back. Turn back. Turn... into compost.
after: ...this path belongs to the Rotheart now... turn back... before the green decides you would make good compost...

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: If you will not leave, the hungry green will keep you. Forever. Very nicely. Like mulch.
after: ...if you won't leave, the green will keep you... it keeps everything now... nothing it holds is ever allowed to go...

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: Oh. Oh no. Did I thorn at you? I'm so sorry. The Rot speaks very softly, right up until it doesn't.
after: Oh no, did I thorn at you? I'm so sorry. The Rot talks very softly in your head, right up until the moment it's doing all the talking.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, at the Rotheart, deep in the Verdant Dump. Everything grew out from her. Me too, the day a very tidy lady with shears came calling.
after: The Rot took Archdruid Compostella first, down at the Rotheart in the deepest part of the Verdant Dump. Everything grew out from there, and it got into me the day a very tidy lady with shears came calling.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: The path is clear. Go gently in there. And if you see a raccoon, say hi. They're very good boys.
after: The path's clear now. Go gently in there, and if you meet a raccoon, say hello for me. They're very good boys, whatever anyone tells you.

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: ...the green is patient... it has all the time in the world... and so does the garbage...
after: ...the green is patient... nothing ends here any more... come back when you're ready to stay...

speaker: Moss Mulligan, the Corrupted Druid
before: ...come back... the green can wait... it has nowhere to leaf...
after: ...come back... the green can wait... it has forgotten how to do anything else...

speaker: (narration)
before: The path to the Rotheart is a tunnel of living roots. The air is warm, wet and humming.
after: The way to the Rotheart runs through a tunnel of living roots, and the air down here is warm, wet and humming.

speaker: (narration)
before: Something very large is breathing, somewhere underneath. It is not you.
after: Somewhere underneath you, something very large is breathing slowly, the way a sleeper does when the dream is a bad one.

speaker: (narration)
before: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post. The mug is mostly apple. A goat watches every bite. HP restored.
after: You eat roast roots and a pie with a crust like a fence post, washed down with a mug that's mostly apple, while a goat watches every bite. HP restored.

speaker: (narration)
before: You are already full of HP. Granny Gristle offers you a third helping anyway. It is a very small turnip.
after: Your HP is already full, but Granny Gristle offers you a third helping anyway: one very small turnip.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: "Fell over in the muck, dearie. We rolled you out. Mucking-out fee is yours. Call it a soil charge. Heh!
after: "Went down in the muck, dearie, so we rolled you out. Mucking-out fee is yours, mind. I call it a soil charge. Heh!

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Haybale was free. Mind you, it is growing. Best get up before you put down roots."
after: The haybale was free, though it's started growing, so best get up before you put down roots."

speaker: (narration)
before: You already took the one lying here. Come back next visit; the Dump restocks itself overnight. It is very good at that.
after: You already took the one lying here. Come back next visit; these days the Dump restocks itself overnight, whether anyone asks it to or not.

speaker: (narration)
before: The bin burps, steams and hands you a warm Compost Cocktail. It smells like a promise. You feel sturdier. (+1 max HP this visit)
after: The bin burps, steams and hands you a warm Compost Cocktail that smells faintly of promise, and you feel sturdier. (+1 max HP this visit)

speaker: (narration)
before: The Compost Bin needs two piles of good junk. You have fewer than two. It waits for you to get your scrap together.
after: The Compost Bin needs two piles of good junk, and you have fewer than two. It sits there, patient and faintly steaming.

speaker: (narration)
before: The bin is full of cocktails for this visit. Come back next visit. It will have fermented.
after: The bin has given all the cocktails it can for this visit. Come back next time, once it has had a chance to ferment.

speaker: (narration)
before: You kneel. A seed in the shrine splits and blooms. A druid voice that sounds like moss says: "Grow."
after: You kneel, and a seed in the shrine splits and blooms. A druid's voice, soft as moss, says: "Grow."

speaker: (narration)
before: The animals are full. One goat is lying on its back. Come back next visit.
after: The animals are full, and one goat is lying on its back to prove it. Come back next visit.

before: You plant a crop and pat the soil. It wriggles a little. Come back in a bit and it will be ready.
after: You plant a crop and pat the soil, which wriggles a little under your hand. Come back in a while and it will be ready.

speaker: (narration)
before: The crop is still growing. A sprout waves at you. You give it space; it seems rather attached to the plot.
after: The crop is still growing. A sprout waves at you, and you leave it to get on with things.

speaker: (narration)
before: That one is already back in the pen. It is sulking. It will get over it.
after: That one is already back in the pen, sulking. It will get over it eventually.

speaker: (narration)
before: The vine bridge sways and creaks cheerfully. It is made of vines, ambition and a lot of compost.
after: The vine bridge sways and creaks cheerfully under you, held together by vines, goodwill and a great deal of compost.

speaker: (narration)
before: It has grown! You try to picture the spot without it. The druids look pleased with themselves.
after: It has grown! Already you can't quite picture the spot without it, and the druids look very pleased with themselves.

speaker: (narration)
before: You cannot dismount out here, the scree will eat your boots. Find a flat spot first.
after: You can't dismount out here; the scree would eat your boots. Find a flat spot first.

speaker: (narration)
before: A barricade of junk. Far too heavy to push on foot. Something fast and stubborn could charge through it.
after: This barricade of junk is far too heavy to push on foot, but something fast and stubborn could charge straight through it.

speaker: (narration)
before: You fall in! Someone fishes you out with a pitchfork. You drip on dry ground. (-1 HP)
after: You fall in! Someone fishes you out with a pitchfork and leaves you dripping on dry ground. (-1 HP)

speaker: Dump workers
before: Compost doesn't sort itself. Well. Lately it tries. That's the problem.
after: Compost doesn't sort itself. Well, lately it tries, and that's the whole problem.

speaker: Dump workers
before: New stairs. Same climb. And the stairs grew two more steps overnight.

speaker: (narration/UI)

after: A sprout mound with a sign: PLANT A MAGIC BEAN HERE. You don't have one, but beans lie around the Dump, one per field each visit.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A sprout mound at the foot of Rust Peak. You plant a Magic Bean and wait. Above, a hubcap spins.
after: A sprout mound at the foot of Rust Peak. You plant a Magic Bean and wait, and somewhere above you a hubcap starts to spin.

speaker: (narration)
before: A sack of fertilizer plus time makes a harvest. Visit-length time. Do not stare at it.

speaker: (narration)

speaker: (narration)
before: A scarecrow druid faces you, a cabbage growing where its heart should be. You see no crows. The garden has bigger problems.
after: A scarecrow druid faces you with a cabbage growing where its heart should be. There isn't a crow in sight; the garden has bigger problems now.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Welcome to the Compost Grange. Brother Bramble, Warden of the Stream. Please close the door behind you. And lock it. And check the window.
after: Welcome to the Compost Grange. I'm Brother Bramble, Warden of the Stream. Would you close the door behind you, and lock it, and maybe check the window? The vines keep trying it.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: We are the Refusemancers: druids of waste removal and agriculture. Our animals turn the kingdom's garbage into fertilizer for its crops. The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. They eat our carrots.
after: We're the Refusemancers, druids of waste removal and agriculture: our animals turn the kingdom's garbage into fertilizer for its crops. The Buffet calls us garbage eaters, and then they eat our carrots.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Our magic runs through nature itself, and {villain} used it against us. Our Archdruid, Compostella, went first. Something got into her roots.
after: Our magic runs through nature itself, and {villain} turned it against us. Our Archdruid, Compostella, went down to tend the deep roots and never came back up, and nothing has been right since.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Now nothing rots, so nothing feeds the soil. Everything is too alive, and the whole Dump is sick with growing. Also, SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.
after: Now nothing rots, so nothing feeds the soil. Everything is too alive and the whole Dump is sick with growing, and on top of all that, SOMEBODY has eaten the compost AGAIN.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Back at the Grange? Sort your boots: compost, metal, glass, paper. Check for tendrils. We already have enough houseplants.
after: Back at the Grange? Do sort your boots at the door - compost, metal, glass, paper - and check them for tendrils. We have quite enough houseplants already.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The Archdruid planted a tree for every royal birthday. There is a row of them past the stream. Eleven trees. Then nothing.
after: The Archdruid planted a tree for every royal birthday, and there's a row of them past the stream. Eleven trees, and then nothing.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: I water the twelfth spot anyway. I couldn't tell you why. It feels as if somebody is still coming.
after: I water the twelfth spot anyway. I couldn't tell you why, except that it feels as if somebody is still coming.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Not long ago, somebody carried a sleeping young man through these woods at night. He glowed, faintly. Four colours.
after: Not long ago, somebody carried a sleeping young man through these woods in the dead of night. He was glowing faintly, in four colours. I've never seen anything like it.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The raccoons saw. Raccoons see everything.
after: The raccoons saw it too. Raccoons see everything; they just won't tell you about it.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Granny Gristle, junk-trader! Born in a haybale, raised in a barn, retired to a shed. This is the shed. It's started growing. It's got a window I never put in.
after: Granny Gristle, junk-trader! Born in a haybale, raised in a barn and retired to a shed, and this is the shed. It's started growing, mind. There's a window in the back I never put in. Heh!

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Everything here's Refusemancer-issue: grown, composted, well rinsed. Found, not stolen, dearie. The raccoon found it. I just held it very tightly.
after: Everything here's Refusemancer-issue: grown, composted and well rinsed. Found, not stolen, dearie. The raccoon found it, and I just held on to it very tightly.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Cards grown strong, rinsed well, faint smell of earth. Hear that hum? Well, I never promised a silent auction. Heh!
after: Cards grown strong and rinsed clean, with a faint smell of earth. Hear them humming? Well, I never promised you a silent auction. Heh!

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: They're looking at me again. I prefer a root vegetable that minds its own business. Heh!
after: The turnips are looking at me again. I like a root vegetable that minds its own business, I do. Heh!

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: Oh good, a pair of legs! Billie Muckfoot, animal handler. Like the goat. I speak fluent goat. It's mostly screaming. Lately it's about the plants: the fields keep trying to eat my herd.
after: Oh good, a pair of legs! I'm Billie Muckfoot, animal handler, and I speak fluent goat, which is mostly screaming. Lately the screaming's about the plants: the fields keep trying to eat my herd.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: Any luck with the herd? Look for the goat first. It'll be eating something it shouldn't. If the thing is eating it back, shout.
after: Any luck with the herd? Look for the goat first; it'll be eating something it shouldn't. If the something is eating it back, shout for me.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: Find each one out in the Dump and walk it back towards the pen before dark. Don't chase. Walk firmly. Make eye contact.
after: Find each one out in the Dump and get it back to the pen before dark. Don't chase them. Walk up firmly and make eye contact.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: Three escapees, out in the fields. The goat is eating something. The pig is in a puddle. The raccoon is writing a strongly worded letter.
after: Three escapees, all out in the fields: the goat's eating something, the pig's found a puddle, and the raccoon is probably writing me a strongly worded letter.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: All three home! The pen's never looked so full. Here's your reward.
after: All three home, and the pen's never looked so full! Here, you've earned this.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: The herd's home and it's plotting. Thanks! Moss Mulligan at the centre bridge will grow you a crossing now. Tell her I sent you.
after: The herd's home and already plotting the next escape. Thank you! Moss Mulligan will grow you a crossing at the centre bridge now. Tell her I sent you.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: Granny Gristle is out of fertilizer and the crops are sulking. Gather three sacks from around the Dump. Hold your nose. Hold the sack.
after: Granny Gristle is out of fertilizer and the crops are sulking. Gather three sacks from around the Dump, and hold your nose while you do.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: I need three sacks from around the Dump. They're lying where the animals left them. Don't ask how. I never have. Heh!
after: I need three sacks from around the Dump, lying wherever the animals left them. Don't ask me how they got bagged up, dearie. I never have. Heh!

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Three whole sacks! The crops are going to sing. Not literally.
after: Three whole sacks! The crops'll be singing by morning, and I mean that more than I'd like to.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Mostly not. Here's your reward. Found, not stolen. Heh!
after: Here's your reward. Found, not stolen, and only a little bit damp. Heh!

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: The fields are fed. Plant your own with a sack of fertilizer and a little patience. Can't sell you patience. Nobody stays to browse it.
after: The fields are fed, dearie. Plant your own with a sack of fertilizer and a little patience. I'd sell you the patience too, but nobody ever stays long enough to buy it. Heh!

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Somebody dumped a dam of junk across the feeder channel on the north bank, and the stream cannot breathe. Borrow a mount from the stables, charge the dam, and my compost boots are yours.
after: Somebody has dumped a dam of junk across the feeder channel on the north bank, and the stream can't breathe. Borrow a mount from the stables and charge it, and my compost boots are yours.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The junk dam on the north bank. Ride the goat from the north stable and charge it. Do not slow down. Dams can smell hesitation.
after: It's the junk dam on the north bank. Take Gideon the goat from the north stable and charge it at full tilt. He's never slowed down for anything, and I'd hate for him to start now.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The stream is flowing! It is practically dancing. Here: compost boots, still warm. They squelch with pride.
after: The stream's flowing again, practically dancing! Here are the compost boots, still warm. They squelch, but it's a proud sort of squelch.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The stream is clear. For now. The kingdom will refill it by Thursday. That is why we are here.
after: The stream's clear, for now. The kingdom will have it full again by the end of the week, but that's what we're here for.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
before: Ah, a visitor. Druid Thistlewick, Keeper of the Dump's Questions. I have sat in this ring of old appliances for forty years.
after: Ah, a visitor. I am Druid Thistlewick, Keeper of the Dump's Questions, and I have sat in this ring of old appliances for forty years.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
before: The dishwasher and I have an understanding. Lately it talks back. Forty years, and NOW it wants to clear the air.
after: The dishwasher and I have an understanding, though lately it has started talking back. Forty years, and NOW it wants to clear the air.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
before: Sort your thoughts like your bins: compost, recycle, regret. Answer well for gold and seeds. Answer poorly for a gentle, rustling sigh.
after: Sort your thoughts as you would your bins: compost, recycling, regret. Answer well and there is gold and seed in it for you; answer poorly and you will receive a gentle, rustling sigh.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
before: Zero. We have found room for growth. Rather a lot of room. No reward this time.
after: Zero. We have found room for growth, rather a lot of it, I'm afraid. No reward this time.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
before: One. A single seed. Plant it, water it, and try again.
after: One. A single seed, but every garden starts with one. Plant it, water it, and try again.

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
before: I voiced Captain Compost Badger and his Sorting Squad back in the nineties! Nobody knew! All that fame went to a badger in a cape!
after: I was the voice of Captain Compost Badger and his Sorting Squad at every harvest puppet show for twenty years! Nobody knew! All that fame went to a badger in a cape!

speaker: (minigame host)
before: Back for another run, champ? The conveyor is hungry. The bins are patient. I have pie.
after: Back for another run, champ? The conveyor's hungry, the bins are ready, and I've got pie for afterwards!

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
before: Your very first run at the fair! Here's your bonus, free, no obligation. It's a salve.
after: Your very first run at the fair! Here's your first-timer's bonus, no strings attached: a jar of compost salve!

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
before: Compost salve! Rub it in! The salve, champ. Not the victory.
after: Rub it in, champ! The salve, I mean, not the victory. Nobody loves a gloater!

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Nothing has died in this valley in ten years. Not a beetle. Not a leaf. Unnatural, that.
after: Nothing's died in this valley in ten years, not so much as a beetle or a leaf. Unnatural, that.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: I've taken up knitting. Heh.
after: Gives a fellow a lot of free time. I've taken up knitting. Heh.

speaker: Recycle Rhonda
before: Reduce! Reuse! Recy-CLUE: that one goes in the green bin!
after: Reduce! Reuse! And rinse your jars, folks - a sticky jar is a sad jar!

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The vines whisper now. It's not right. Also SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.
after: The vines have started whispering. Also, SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.

speaker: Archdruid Compostella
before: Everything grows back, child. Even me. Especially me.
after: Everything goes back to the soil in the end, child. That's what lets it grow.

speaker: Archdruid Compostella
before: About the barn... I will help mend it. The goat may prefer that I begin elsewhere.
after: About the barn, child... I'll help mend it. The goat would rather I started elsewhere.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: SOMEBODY has been eating ALL the compost. Little paw prints. A tiny crown.
after: SOMEBODY has been eating ALL the compost. There are little paw prints everywhere, and next to the bin I found... a tiny crown.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Chase off two of the scavengers in the Dump and the trail will lead you to the alley under the big dumpster. Gently, please. They're only hungry. And GUILTY.
after: Chase off two of the scavengers in the Dump and their trail should lead you to the big dumpster. Gently, please - they're only hungry. And GUILTY.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Two scavengers in the Dump. Fresh paw prints, freshly stolen compost. A trail of evidence with TERRIBLE table manners.
after: Two scavengers out in the Dump, please. Follow the fresh paw prints; it's a trail of evidence with TERRIBLE table manners.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Under the tipped-over dumpster there's a gate made from a bicycle wheel. That's the way to the Trash Panda Throne. Bring a peg for your nose.
after: Under the tipped-over dumpster there's a gate made from an old bicycle wheel, and that's the way to the Trash Panda Throne. Do bring a peg for your nose.

speaker: His Majesty the Raccoon
before: The compost was for the kingdom. We are the kingdom. Checkmate. ...Is it warm in here?
after: We were only testing the compost on the realm's behalf. Very thoroughly. ...Is it warm in here? It is very warm in here.

speaker: (narration)
before: The vines part for you, slowly. They do not seem to be letting you in. They seem to be letting you go deeper.
after: The vines part for you slowly, and it doesn't feel like being let in. It feels like being drawn deeper.

speaker: (narration)
before: The entrance is a cracked archway wrapped in black-green vines. They tighten as you pass.
after: A cracked archway wrapped in black-green vines that tighten a little as you pass beneath them.

speaker: (narration)
before: Normal-looking plants, mostly. A little too green. Every leaf turns, very slightly, to follow you.
after: Ordinary plants at first glance, only a shade too green, and every leaf turns very slightly to follow you.

speaker: (narration)
before: Mushrooms the size of sheds. Some of them are looking at you. Some of them have hats.
after: Mushrooms the size of garden sheds crowd the path, and a few of them tilt their caps to watch you go by.

speaker: (narration)
before: A ring of pale mushrooms murmurs as you pass. They know your name. They are not sure why.
after: A ring of pale mushrooms murmurs as you pass. They seem to know your name, though they can't think how.

speaker: (narration)
before: The vines are choosing who gets through. They are reading your deck very closely.
after: The vines are choosing who gets through, and they're reading your deck very closely before they decide.

speaker: (narration)
before: The mill wheel is gripped by roots as thick as a cart. Someone has been trimming them. Very neatly. Into the shape of a smiling man in a circlet.
after: Roots as thick as a cart grip the mill wheel. Someone has trimmed them, very neatly, into the shape of a smiling man in a circlet.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Mind the topiary, dear. That's His Perfection from the left. The right side is still growing in.
after: Do mind the topiary, dear. That's His Perfection, seen from the left - the right side is still filling in.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper. I outlawed composting. So untidy. All that rot, lying about in heaps, being honest.
after: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper. I'm the one who outlawed composting. All that rot lying about in heaps, being honest with everybody - so untidy.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Nothing rots here any more.
after: Nothing rots down here any more, and the whole place feels wrong for it.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Isn't it lovely? I brought the Archdruid a little seed, a gift. Life that never ends. She was so very sad, and now nothing ever has to go.
after: Isn't it lovely? I brought the Archdruid a little seed as a gift - life that never ends. She was so very sad, and now nothing ever has to go.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Such a pretty weed. Such a shame. Do hold still, dear.
after: Such a pretty little weed, and such a shame. Do hold still, dear, this won't take a moment.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Gentlemen, if you would. He is well over regulation height.
after: Gentlemen, if you would? He's grown well over regulation height.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Well. You've made a dreadful mess of my hedges. I shall send a note.
after: Well. You've made a dreadful mess of my hedges, and I shall be sending a note.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Brother Bramble's notes are pinned to a root: 'NOTHING ROTS. NOTHING FEEDS THE SOIL. THE SOIL IS STARVING.
after: Brother Bramble's notes are pinned to a root in a worried hand: 'Nothing rots, so nothing feeds the soil, and the soil is STARVING.'

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: IT IS ALIVE. IT IS ALL TOO ALIVE. AND WHO IS EATING THE COMPOST?'
after: Underneath, pressed much harder: 'Everything down here is far TOO alive. And WHO has been eating the COMPOST?'

speaker: (narration)
before: The pool is the colour of a bruise and it is sobbing very quietly. Things float in it that used to be useful. A boot, mostly.
after: The pool is the colour of a bruise, and it's sobbing very quietly around a boot that bobs in the middle of it.

speaker: (narration)
before: Somebody will pay for this. Somebody always does. It is usually a hedgehog.
after: Somebody will pay good gold for a bottle of this. Down here, that somebody is usually a hedgehog.

speaker: (narration)
before: You tell it that it is doing great. It sobs harder, then gives you a very old Mulch Mole it was keeping safe, and a bit of its warmth.
after: You tell it that it's doing very well. It sobs harder, then gives you a very old Mulch Mole it was keeping safe, along with a little of its warmth.

speaker: (narration)
before: A tunnel of drifting spores. A well-built deck walks straight through. A loose one starts to sprout.
after: A tunnel of drifting spores. A well-built deck walks straight through, but a loose one starts to sprout.

speaker: (narration)
before: The Refusemancers' seed bank, long since overrun. Some of the seeds are still good. Some of them have opinions.
after: The Refusemancers' seed bank, long since overrun. Some of the seeds are still good, and some of them have opinions.

speaker: (narration)
before: The oldest tree in the Dump, grown into the Rotheart. It does not recognize you. It does not recognize anything. (Elite)
after: The oldest tree in the Dump, grown into the Rotheart. It doesn't recognize you, or anything else, any more. (Elite)

speaker: (narration)
before: You breathe in rain and old compost. Beneath you, a worm moves through the loose soil. You let your shoulders drop.
after: It smells of rain and old compost, and somewhere beneath you a worm is working through the loose soil. Your shoulders drop for the first time in hours.

speaker: (narration)
before: The golem folds into the floor. The tunnel ahead is smoother, warmer, and has a pulse.
after: The golem folds back into the floor, and the tunnel ahead turns smoother and warmer, with a pulse running through it.

speaker: (narration)
before: A tag in very tidy handwriting: PROPERTY OF THE PATH-OLOGISTS. LIFE THAT NEVER DIES.
after: A tag hangs from it in very tidy handwriting: PROPERTY OF THE PATH-OLOGISTS - LIFE THAT NEVER DIES.

speaker: (narration)
before: But the seed itself will not let go of her. And she will not let go of it.
after: But the seed won't let go of her, and she won't let go of it.

speaker: (narration)
before: Thick, pulsing roots run from every wall into the chamber beyond: the Rotheart's lifelines. You could cut them. It will hurt, her more than you.
after: Thick, pulsing roots run from every wall into the chamber beyond: the Rotheart's lifelines. You could cut them, and it would hurt her far more than you.

speaker: (narration)
before: The roots keep pulsing. The Rotheart keeps its strength.
after: The roots keep pulsing, and the Rotheart keeps its strength.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: Her eyes are open. They are not hers.
after: Her eyes are open, but whatever is looking out of them isn't her.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: "I... am... THE... DUMP," she says, in many voices at once, sorrowful and enraged. "I am what you throw away. I am what grows back. I am HUNGRY."
after: "I... am... THE... DUMP," she says in many voices at once, grieving and furious. "I am WHAT YOU THROW AWAY... I am what GROWS BACK... and I am HUNGRY."

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart
before: I am what you throw away. I am what grows back. I am HUNGRY.
after: I AM what you throw away... I AM what grows back... and I am so... HUNGRY...

speaker: (narration)
before: Five cards drift through the spores. If enough of them are infrastructure, they will hold you steady. If not, the spores will sweeten your lungs.
after: Five cards drift through the spores. If enough of them are infrastructure they'll hold you steady; if not, the spores will settle sweetly in your lungs.

speaker: (narration)
before: A ring of pale mushrooms murmurs as you pass. "Stay," they say, in a thousand tiny voices. "Eat.
after: A ring of pale mushrooms murmurs as you pass. "Stay," they say in a thousand tiny voices, "and eat."

speaker: (narration)
before: Listen. Join."
after: "Listen," they add, softer. "Join us."

speaker: (narration)
before: They tell you things. Where the roots run, where the Rot is thin, where the Archdruid used to walk. You hold onto what you can.
after: They tell you where the roots run, where the Rot wears thin and where the Archdruid used to walk, and you hold on to as much as you can.

speaker: (narration)
