before: It helps. It is not entirely your own thought.
after: It helps, though some of what you now know doesn't feel like your own thought.

speaker: (narration)
before: The mushrooms scream, very quietly. You pretend not to hear. A passing trader is delighted, and pays well.
after: The mushrooms scream very quietly as you pick them, and you pretend not to hear. A passing trader is delighted and pays well.

speaker: (narration)
before: The wall ahead pulses with a slow, wet heartbeat. A seam runs down the middle. Behind it, warm light.
after: The wall ahead pulses with a slow, wet heartbeat, and warm light leaks through a seam down its middle.

speaker: (narration)
before: The wall takes your hands, warm and wet. It hurts. Then it does not.
after: The wall takes your hands, warm and wet. It hurts for a moment, and then it doesn't.

speaker: (narration)
before: Roots grow along your arms, and, oddly, you feel better rooted in the world.
after: Fine roots creep along your arms and then let go, and oddly you feel steadier on your feet than you have in days.

speaker: (narration)
before: It bleeds sap and fury. A glittering stone falls out. It is worth a lot of gold, and a bit of your arm.
after: It bleeds sap and fury, and a glittering stone drops out of the cut. It'll fetch good gold, though it costs you a long scrape down one arm.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: You hear the vines settle overhead. For a moment, nothing moves beneath your feet.
after: Overhead the vines settle, and for a moment nothing moves beneath your feet.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: "...What a terrible dream," Compostella whispers. "The seed. It is still in my roots. It will not die, and I cannot make it."
after: "...What a terrible dream," Compostella whispers. "The seed is still in my roots, child. It won't die, and I can't make it."

speaker: Archdruid Compostella
before: It is the seed. {villain}'s gift: life that never dies. When the great tree I grew up beneath fell, I could not bear it.
after: It's the seed, {villain}'s gift - life that never dies. I grew up beneath a great tree, child, and when she fell, I couldn't bear it.

speaker: Archdruid Compostella
before: I planted the seed in her place. It took. It has been growing in my grief for ten years. Nothing here rots, because of me.
after: I planted the seed where she had stood, and it took. It's been feeding on my grief for ten years. Nothing here rots, and that's my doing.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: A seed that never dies isn't a gift. It's a grief that never ends. Let it rot.
after: Something that can never die isn't a gift. It's a grief that never gets to end. Let it rot.

speaker: Archdruid Compostella
before: Everything I ever loved, I gave back to the soil. Except this one. I could not.
after: Everything I ever loved, I gave back to the soil when its time came. Everything except her.

speaker: Archdruid Compostella
before: ...Then we let it die, together. Hold still. Hold me.
after: ...Then we let it die, together. Hold on to me while it goes.

speaker: Archdruid Compostella
before: ...It is rotting. Honest compost, the first in ten years. Oh. I can hear the soil again.
after: ...It's rotting. Honest compost, the first in ten years. Oh, I can hear the soil again.

speaker: Dump workers
before: The river's still lovely. Still a nightmare to climb out of. Some things healing can't fix.
after: River's still lovely, and still a nightmare to climb out of. Healing only goes so far.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Compost sorts itself the normal way again. Slowly. With help. As it should.
after: Compost's rotting down the normal way again - slowly, with help, the way it should.

speaker: Dump workers
before: The raccoon in the crown says thank you. He also wants your lunch. Still no.
after: The raccoon in the crown says thank you. He'd also like your lunch. I've told him no.

speaker: Dump workers
before: New stairs. Same climb. Worth pausing on, now.
after: Same climb as ever, but the view's worth stopping for now.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Every terrace a little greener. Even the top one. Especially the top one.
after: Every terrace is a little greener now, and the top one most of all.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Archdruid's back on her rounds. She waters the weeds too. Says they had a rough decade.
after: Archdruid's back on her rounds. Waters the weeds too - says they've had a hard ten years.

speaker: Dump workers
before: The trees went back to green overnight. Nobody's talking about that either, but happily.
after: Trees went back to their proper green overnight. Folk keep stopping just to look.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Funny thing. The flowers smell like flowers again. I'd forgotten that was a smell.
after: Funny thing - the flowers smell like flowers again. I'd forgotten they had a smell.

speaker: (narration)
before: Nothing goes to waste. The Rot has gone. The doors may be opened again.
after: Nothing goes to waste. The Rot is gone, and the doors may be opened again.

speaker: (narration)
before: - Water things. They like it. They are only plants.
after: - Water the plants. They're only plants again, and they like it.

speaker: (narration)
before: To {town}. Moss Mulligan's thorn wall is mulch, and she says sorry again. Vines are just vines now. Still sort your boots.
after: To {town}. Moss Mulligan's thorn wall is mulch now, and she says sorry again. The vines are just vines, but please still sort your boots.

speaker: (narration)
before: Source of the sickness, now closed for healing. The vines are only vines. Mostly. Visitors welcome.
after: Source of the sickness, now closed for healing. The vines are only vines (mostly), and visitors are welcome.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: I never thought I'd say it: the Dump is healing. The vines are only vines, the mushrooms are only mushrooms, and the Archdruid is herself again. She is mortified.
after: I never thought I'd get to say it, but the Dump is healing. The vines are only vines, the mushrooms are only mushrooms, and the Archdruid is herself again. She's terribly embarrassed.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Breathe in. Go on. You may breathe deeply now. That smell is honest compost.
after: Go on, breathe in. You can breathe deeply down here now, and that smell is HONEST COMPOST. Isn't it wonderful?

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: This morning Compostella walked straight to the row of royal trees and planted a twelfth. She didn't say why.
after: This morning Compostella walked straight to the row of royal trees and planted a twelfth. She didn't say why, and I didn't like to ask.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: She just smiled at you on the way past.
after: She only smiled at you on her way past. I've been wondering about that all morning.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The stream is clean, the fields are calm and the zucchini has gone back to being a zucchini. Thank you. We owe you more than compost.
after: The stream's clean, the fields are calm and the zucchini has gone back to being a zucchini. We owe you a great deal more than compost.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Granny Gristle, junk-trader! The shed is just a shed again. The turnips are only turnips.
after: Granny Gristle, junk-trader, back in business! The shed's just a shed again, dearie, and the turnips are only turnips.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: I had a little cry, then I planted a field. Shop's open, dearie. Welcome back to the sane side of farming. Heh!
after: I had a little cry, then I went and planted a whole field. Shop's open, dearie, and every bit of it was thrown out by somebody who was wrong. Heh!

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: Billie Muckfoot, animal handler! The herd's back, and the goat's eating a sign.
after: Billie Muckfoot, animal handler! The whole herd's home, and the goat's already eating a sign.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: The sign's not eating back. I've never been so happy to see a goat ruin something.
after: And the sign isn't eating him back this time. I've never been so happy to watch a goat ruin something.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: Every animal present and entirely un-mutated. I could cry. I might.
after: Every animal's home and not one of them mutated. I could cry, honestly, and I might.

speaker: Billie Muckfoot
before: Into a bucket. For the plants.
after: Into a bucket, though. The plants could use it.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: Archdruid Compostella. I am told what happened to the barn. I cannot remember doing it. The barn, I gather, remembers me. I will help put it right.
after: Archdruid Compostella, child, and yes, I've been told about the barn. I don't remember doing it, but I gather the barn remembers me, so I'll be helping to put it right.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: Ten years of the Rot in my roots. It spoke so quietly. It said I was needed. It said the whole world was waiting to grow.
after: The Rot sat in my roots for ten years and spoke so quietly. It told me I was needed, and that the whole world was waiting on me to grow.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: It was my own grief, wearing a seed. Thank you for helping me let it rot.
after: It was my own grief all along, dressed up as a seed. Thank you for helping me let it rot.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: The Dump will heal. The goat may take longer to trust me. Plant something, child. Anything. It will be glad of you.
after: The Dump will heal, though the goat may take a little longer to trust me. Plant something, child. Anything at all. It'll be glad of you.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: You are carrying a loss you cannot name yet, child. When you find its name, do not bury it in a jar. Death is not the end of them.
after: You're carrying a loss you can't name yet, child. When you find its name, don't shut it away in a jar the way I did. Death is not the end of them.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: It looks like the Archdruid. It is still growing. Please do not water.
after: It looks like the Archdruid, and it's still growing. Please do not water it.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: It used to be the Rot-Idol. Now it is topiary. Please do not water.
after: This used to be the Rot-Idol. It's only topiary now, but please still do not water it.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The Groundskeeper's gone. Packed her shears and left for the Capital the moment the Archdruid woke.
after: The Groundskeeper's gone. She packed her shears and left for the Capital the very moment the Archdruid woke.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: She left one pair behind, in a compost heap. Granny Gristle is keeping them. 'Found, not stolen,' she says. Twice.
after: She left one pair behind in a compost heap, and Granny Gristle has kept them. 'Found, not stolen,' she told me, twice, before I'd even asked.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Hear that? Things rotting properly again. Lovely sound. Means something's about to grow. Heh.
after: Hear that? Things rotting properly again. Lovely sound, that - it means something's about to grow.

speaker: (UI)
before: The Doppelganger is exposed, the Special Sauce is recalled, and the real Grand Chef is back in her kitchen. The golems guard plates again. Nobody leaves hungry.
after: The Doppelganger is exposed, the Special Sauce is recalled, and the real Grand Chef is back in her own kitchen with the golems guarding plates again. Nobody leaves hungry.

speaker: (UI)
before: The Rotheart is silent. The vines are only vines again. The Archdruid is herself and deeply apologetic about the barn. The land starts, slowly, to heal.
after: The Rotheart has gone silent and the vines are only vines again. The Archdruid is herself once more, deeply apologetic about the barn, and slowly the land begins to heal.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: The intake's open again, did you hear? Busy week! Gerald's number came up. Lovely chap. Brought his own mug.
after: The intake's open again, did you hear? Busy week. Gerald's number finally came up, lovely chap, and he brought his own mug for the journey.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Agnes stayed, of course. Somebody has to fix the forms. I've put her down for later. Much later. Heh.
after: Agnes stayed on, of course. Somebody has to fix the forms, and I've pencilled her in for later. Much later. Heh.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: Freeing a zone loosens something in your head. Whenever it does, go and tell Elder Maren.
after: Every zone you free seems to shake something loose in your memory. Each time it happens, go and tell Elder Maren; she'll want to hear it.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Checked my book. You're not in it. Not for a good long while. Heh.
after: Checked my book. You're not in it, not for a good long while. Heh.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Business has been slow for ten years. Not my fault. Paperwork. Heh.
after: Business has been ever so slow these ten years. Paperwork, not me. Heh.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You're pale. Sit, sit. Something came back to you, didn't it?
after: You've gone pale as flour. Sit down, sit. Something's come back to you, hasn't it?

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Tell me. All of it, however small.
after: Tell me all of it, however small it seems. The small things are usually the ones that matter.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Light. Four colors of it, warm as bathwater, spilling across a ceiling I can't quite see.
after: There's light, four colors of it, warm as bathwater, spilling across a ceiling I can't quite see.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A woman is humming. A tune with no words, rising and falling like breathing.
after: A woman is humming a tune with no words, and it rises and falls like someone breathing in their sleep.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A hand rests on my head. Gentle. Certain. It smells of lavender and woodsmoke.
after: A hand rests on my head, gentle and certain, and it smells of lavender and woodsmoke.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: ...A lullaby. That tune is from the old days. From the court. Few remember it, and fewer hum it.
after: ...A lullaby. That tune is from the old days, from the court, and there are very few left who remember it. Fewer still who'd hum it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Eat some pie. Don't ask me why my eyes are wet.
after: Have some pie. And don't ask me why my eyes are wet, because I won't tell you.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And look at you. With a zone free, the corruption's grip on the land is slipping, and it is slipping off you with it.
after: And look at you. With one zone free, the corruption's grip on the land is slipping, and it's slipping off you along with it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You should be able to carry a second Path now. Go on, try it at the Deck Station.
after: You ought to be able to carry a second Path now. Go to the Deck Station and try building a deck with two; I'd like to hear how it feels.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: One zone free and back for pie already. Fine. One slice per zone, dearie. Those are the rules now.
after: One zone free and you're back for pie already. Fine, but it's one slice per zone from now on, dearie. I've just made that rule.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Three roads still shut. I'd go myself, dearie, but I'd arrive next spring.
after: Three roads are still shut. I'd see to them myself, dearie, but at my pace I'd arrive next spring.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The square sang last night. Badly. Best thing I've heard in ten years. Don't you dare tell them.
after: The square sang last night, and badly. It was the best thing I've heard in ten years, so don't you dare tell them.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: One zone free. Hm. And the old cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started cheering at night. From the cellar. I am choosing not to ask.
after: One zone free. Hm. And the old cottage at the end of Champions' Road has started cheering at night, from somewhere down in the cellar. I've decided not to ask.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: You freed a whole Path. On your own. With a deck you'd known for a week.
after: You freed a whole Path on your own, with a deck you've only had for a week.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Let me see your hands. Steadier. Good. That's the first thing I've been able to tick off in a long time.
after: Let me see your hands. Steadier than they were. Good. That's the first thing I've been able to tick off my list in a long time.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Still a friend. Still all I can give you.
after: A friend. That's still all I can tell you, and I'm sorry it isn't more.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: I'm not staying in town. The old woman with the shell looks at me like I owe her a pie.
after: I'm not coming into town. The old woman with the shell looks at me like I owe her something, and she's probably right.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Keep going. I'll know when the next one falls. The woods go quiet when a Path comes loose.
after: Keep going. I'll know when the next one falls, because the woods go quiet whenever a Path comes loose.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Another one. Don't hide it behind your teacup. Say it.
after: Another one, is it? Don't hide behind your teacup, dearie. Just say it.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: White rooms. White light that never changes with the hour.
after: White rooms, and a white light that never changes, whatever the hour.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: They never use my name. They call me 'the Subject.' They say 'again.'
after: No one there ever uses my name. They call me 'the Subject', and whatever I do, they only say 'again.'

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Glass, and coats, and 'again.' So that is where you have been.
after: Glass, and white coats, and 'again.' So that's where you've been all this time.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You have earned the truth, so here is the first piece of it: I am not only a tortoise who bakes.
after: You've earned some truth from me, so here's the first piece of it: I'm not just an old tortoise who bakes.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: There is a resistance in this kingdom, and I am its contact in {town}. Wren leads it, from a hideout in the Capital.
after: There's a resistance in this kingdom, and I'm its contact here in {town}. A woman called Wren leads it, from a hideout in the Capital.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I wasn't sure of you before. I am sure now. Mostly.
after: I wasn't sure of you before. I am now, near enough, and I don't say that about many people.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Two zones free. The square's louder now. I complain about it every morning and mean none of it.
after: Two zones free, and the square's louder for it. I complain about the noise every morning and don't mean a word of it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Auntie Alembic keeps asking after you. I tell her you're busy. For once it's even true.
after: Auntie Alembic keeps asking after you. I tell her you're busy, and for once it's even true.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Two zones free. Auntie Alembic has opened her shop on the square, the Alchemist's.
after: Two zones free, and Auntie Alembic has opened the Alchemist's on the square. She brews cards from two Paths at once, if you can stand the steam.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: She asks for your leftovers. From her, that is a compliment.
after: She's been asking for your leftovers. From her, that's a compliment.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Two Paths. People in town are singing again. Badly, but they're singing.
after: Two Paths free, and I could hear the town singing from all the way out here. Badly, but singing.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Even when you were someone who couldn't. Ask me something easier.
after: Even when you were somewhere you weren't allowed to leave. Ask me something easier.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You're shaking. Sit. Slowly now.
after: You're shaking. Sit down, slowly now. Here, take my hand.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A throne room at night. Candles guttering, banners with four colors woven as one.
after: A throne room at night, the candles guttering under banners with four colors woven into one.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A man in white and gold kneels before the king. Soft voice. Then he stands.
after: A man in white and gold kneels before the king and speaks in a soft voice. Then he rises, and his soft voice is the last soft thing in the room.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Hands on my shoulders. Two people pushing me behind them, toward the dark.
after: Two pairs of hands are on my shoulders, pushing me behind them, toward the dark.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: I know that man's face. I have always known it. {villain}.
after: I know that man's face, and I think I have always known it. {villain}.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: A man in white and gold, kneeling, and then standing. And a lab with glass on every side.
after: A man in white and gold, kneeling and then standing. And before that, those rooms with glass on every side.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I know that glass, because I helped to blow it. I founded the study of the Paths, long ago, for the best of reasons.
after: I know that glass, because I helped to blow it. Long ago I founded the study of the Paths, and I did it for the best of reasons.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: {villain} took my work and turned it into a cage. My best student kept the lab running for him. And I ran.
after: {villain} took my work and made a cage of it, and my best student kept the lab running for him. And I ran.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I have been hiding here ever since, with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would ask what else they had made.
after: I've been hiding here ever since, with my hands in pie dough, where nobody would think to ask what else those hands had made.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: That is my secret. Now you hold it, the same as I hold yours.
after: That's my secret. Now you're holding it, the same way I've been holding yours.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb. The whole town is holding its breath. I can hold mine for a week. They cannot.
after: One Path left under {villain}'s thumb, and the whole town's holding its breath. I can hold mine for a week, being a tortoise. They can't.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Three zones free, dearie. Finish the fourth before my pie goes stale. That gives you about a week.
after: Three zones free, dearie. Do finish the fourth before this pie goes stale; I'd give it about a week.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You walk like somebody with somewhere to be now. I preferred the damp young man. He visited more.
after: You walk like somebody with somewhere to be these days. I liked the damp young man better. He visited more.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Three zones free. Only one Path left under {villain}'s thumb. I will not say what I'm feeling. I will say it is a lot of feelings.
after: Three zones free. Only one Path is left under {villain}'s thumb now, and I won't tell you what I'm feeling about it, except that it's a great deal.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: Three. I used to think you were someone else. Someone I lost when we were kids. Now I'm starting to think...
after: Three. At first I told myself you just reminded me of someone. Someone I lost when we were kids. Now I'm starting to think...

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: No. Not until I'm certain. Too many people around here say things before they're certain.
after: No, not until I'm certain. Too many people around here say things before they're sure, and I won't be one of them.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You knew me. Before.
after: You knew me before all this.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: There is something in your face today. The look of someone who has been handed a key. Tell me.
after: There's something in your face today, the look of someone who's just been handed a key. Tell me what it opens.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A boy of eleven, in a coat too fine for the cold. Someone calls across a courtyard: '{prince}!'
after: A boy of eleven stands in a coat too fine for the cold. Someone calls across a courtyard: '{prince}!'

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: I turn. A woman's voice. A man's voice. The {royal_house} crest on every door: four signs in a ring.
after: I turn toward a woman's voice, and then a man's, and on every door is the {royal_house} crest: four signs in a ring.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: {prince_full}. The son of the king and queen. Presumed dead.
after: {prince_full}, son of the king and queen. The whole kingdom believes he died ten years ago.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And I knew. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only. I knew the moment you walked out of it, and I was too frightened to say so.
after: I knew, you see. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only, and I knew it the moment you walked out of it. I was too frightened to say so.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Four signs in a ring. The same as on my stick. I have carried it for ten years and told nobody why.
after: Four signs in a ring, the same as the ones carved on my stick. I've carried it for ten years and never told a soul why.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: And my lab, my life's work, was used on that boy. Forgive me, if you ever can.
after: And my lab, my life's work, was used on that boy. On you. Forgive me if you ever can. I'd understand if you couldn't.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: There is nothing to forgive. You gave me a bed and pie when you thought I might be a spy.
after: There's nothing to forgive. You gave me a bed and pie when you still thought I might be a spy.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You have the look of someone who was told something he did not want to hear. {villain}?
after: You've the look of someone who was told something he didn't want to hear. Was it {villain}?

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Sit. Tell me what he said.
after: Sit down and tell me what he said. All of it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: So he knew you from the first. He told you, and you came to me for the rest.
after: So he knew you from the very first. He told you who you are, and you've come to me for the rest of it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I knew too, dearie. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only. I knew, and I was too frightened to say it.
after: I knew too. The Warden opens that tunnel for one family only, and I knew it the moment you came out of it. I was just too frightened to say so.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: So hear it from the one who held your hand at court: you are {prince_full}, and I am so sorry for what was done to you in my name.
after: So hear it from someone who held your hand at court: you are {prince_full}, and I'm so sorry for what was done to you with the things I built.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: All four Paths free, and {villain} still sitting in his castle. Go and knock, dearie. Loudly.
after: All four Paths free, and {villain} still sitting in his castle as if nothing's changed. Go and knock, dearie. Loudly.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The roads are open. Even I use them. I passed a hare this morning. He has asked for a recount.
after: The roads are open, and even I've been using them. I passed a hare this morning; he's asked for a recount.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Eat something first. Then the castle. Nobody topples a tyrant well on an empty stomach.
after: Eat something first, then go to the castle. Nobody ever toppled a tyrant properly on an empty stomach.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: All four Paths are free. {kingdom} is whole again, or nearly. And up in his castle, {villain} is counting what he has left.
after: All four Paths are free, and {kingdom} is whole again, or nearly. Up in his castle, {villain} will be counting what he has left.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Rest. Then we finish this.
after: Get some rest. Then we finish this, together.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: All four. The kingdom is breathing again. Like voices through a wall, except the wall is coming down.
after: All four. Can you hear it? The kingdom's breathing again, like voices through a wall, except now the wall's coming down.

speaker: (narration)
before: Far away in {town}, the Old Well hums like a full kettle. Both streams have answered. Go back to the well.
after: Far away in {town}, the Old Well hums like a full kettle. Both streams have answered, and the well is calling you back.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: A well with opinions. Fine. I'm keeping the bottle.
after: A well with opinions. I'm keeping the bottle anyway.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I always thought the key was lost. It was not, dearie. Somebody hid it in a chest in this very town. Find it, and we will see what the door is for.
after: I always thought the key was lost, but it wasn't, dearie. Somebody hid it in a chest right here in town. Find it, and we'll see what the door is for.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The key is in a hidden chest in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie. This town has never quite managed a straight one.
after: The key's in a hidden chest somewhere in town. Look in the odd corners, dearie; this town has never quite managed a straight one.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: You found it. Look at the bow: four little carvings, in a ring. Hm. Never mind. I am too old for stairs, dearie. You are not.
after: You found it. Look at the bow: four little carvings in a ring. Hm. Never mind that. I'm too old for stairs, dearie, and you're not.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: The iron hatch beside the well. Go on. Whatever is under it belonged to the Old Kingdom, not to me. Mind the stairs.
after: The door's the iron hatch beside the well. Go on down. Whatever's under it belonged to the Old Kingdom, not to me, so mind the stairs.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: A giant chest was too good to be true. Someone is conning travellers with them, and he took your gold. Find the chests, and find him.
after: That giant chest was too good to be true. Someone is conning travellers with chests like it, and he's taken your gold. Find the rest of the chests, and you'll find him.

speaker: (Quest Log)
before: Far away, a great lock ground open. A hidden lever in every Path zone answers a seal somewhere near Crosspath. Find them all.
after: Somewhere far off, a great lock has ground open. Each Path zone hides a lever that answers a seal near Crosspath. Find all four.

speaker: Shiro Swindle
before: You found me! Nobody finds me. Which means this is a trick. Mine.
after: You found me! Nobody finds me, which can only mean this is a trick. Mine, obviously.

speaker: The Warden of the Four Seals
before: One seal. One Path. The hand is real. Show me the rest of it.
after: One seal for one Path, and the hand is real. Show me the rest of it.

speaker: The Warden of the Four Seals
before: The last seal opens. The Paths agreed to bury this. They also agreed you might come.
after: The last seal opens. The four Paths agreed to bury this, and they agreed that one day you might come for it.

speaker: (UI)
before: Find the hideout through the manhole near the gate. Help the Wrinkles, one quest per Path; seal rifts and reach {villain}'s Castle at the north end. Each freed Path mends a broken city service.
after: Find the Wrinkles' hideout: knock at the manhole near the gate. Help them with one quest for each Path, seal the rifts, and reach {villain}'s Castle at the north end. Each Path you free mends a broken city service.

speaker: (narration)
before: Ow! The Capital has hurt you again. (-HP)
after: The Capital catches you hard, the way it catches everyone. (-HP)

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: 'Dragged you in by the collar. Correction fee is yours. Drink. Then we can discuss your habit of arriving unconscious.'
after: 'I dragged you in by the collar, and the correction fee comes out of your purse. Drink. Then we can talk about this habit you have of arriving unconscious.'

speaker: A gate guard
before: 'Falling in the approved queue area: minor offence. Fine payable. Stand up, citizen. I cannot measure you along the ground.'
after: 'Falling down in the approved queue area is a minor offence, and the fine is payable now. Up you get, citizen. I cannot measure you while you are lying along the ground.'

speaker: (narration)
before: You are through the walls. Somewhere a loudspeaker clears its throat. You are now, officially, a Visitor in {capital}, the Capital of {kingdom}.
after: You're through the walls. Somewhere above you a loudspeaker clears its throat, and you are now, officially, a Visitor in {capital}, the Capital of {kingdom}.

speaker: (narration)
before: You crawl out through the old tunnel and push the rubble aside. The Outskirts again, and a long way from anybody's approved queue.
after: You crawl out through the old tunnel and shove the rubble aside, and you're back in the Outskirts, a long way from anybody's approved queue.

speaker: (narration)
before: You push past rubble and a toppled statue. You find stairs and read an old plaque: 'THE OLD JOINT WORKS. BUILT BY ALL FOUR PATHS, TOGETHER.'
after: Past the rubble and a toppled statue, a flight of stairs leads down to an old plaque: 'THE OLD JOINT WORKS. BUILT BY ALL FOUR PATHS, TOGETHER.'

speaker: (narration)
before: The tunnel runs under the wall, under the gate and under every one of {villain}'s checkpoints. You walk under them all. It is the best moment you have had all day.
after: The tunnel runs under the wall, under the gate and under every one of {villain}'s checkpoints, and you walk beneath them all without being measured once. It's the best moment you've had all day.

speaker: (narration)
before: A manhole by the wall, with a scratch on its lid like a tiny wrinkle. You knock three times, for no reason you can name.
after: There's a manhole by the wall with a scratch on its lid, like a tiny wrinkle. You knock three times, for no reason you can name.

speaker: (narration)
before: A pause. Then the lid lifts and a hand beckons. A voice mutters, 'Wrinkle?' You decide that, yes, you are.
after: After a pause the lid lifts and a hand beckons you down. 'Wrinkle?' a voice mutters, and you decide that, yes, you probably are.

speaker: (narration)
before: Already improved. He has a moustache now. He looks, for the first time, like a person.
after: Someone has already improved this one. With the moustache he looks, for the first time, like a person.

speaker: (narration)
before: You post a complaint. 'Noted,' says the box, gently. You wait. That appears to have been the whole service.
after: You post a complaint. 'Noted,' says the box, gently, and after a long wait you understand that this was the whole service.

speaker: (narration)
before: You post a complaint. A klaxon sounds. A Perfection Inspector appears from nowhere, measures your frown, writes you up and walks off.
after: You post a complaint, and a klaxon sounds. A Perfection Inspector appears from nowhere, measures your frown, writes you up and walks off.

speaker: (narration)
before: The box rattles. It is full. It has had enough of your feedback for one visit.
after: The box rattles, full to the slot. It has had quite enough of your feedback for one visit.

speaker: (narration)
before: This one is too big. It runs all the way up into the castle. It will have to close when he does.
after: This one is too big to seal. It runs all the way up into the castle, and it will only close when he does.

speaker: (narration)
before: A banished compost heap, hiding in a cellar where it was not allowed to be. It is warm. It is alive.
after: A banished compost heap is hiding in a cellar where it was never allowed to be, still warm and still very much alive.

speaker: (narration)
before: An old glass jar with one seed in it. The seed is glowing very faintly green. Nobody has planted anything in the Capital for ten years. It has not given up.
after: An old glass jar holds a single seed, glowing very faintly green. Nobody has planted anything in the Capital for ten years, and the seed hasn't given up.

speaker: (narration)
before: The second wheel has been turning since some of its runners were too small to reach the pedals. A foreman's whistle hangs from a hook. You pocket it.
after: The second wheel has been turning since some of its runners were too small to reach the pedals. A foreman's whistle hangs on a hook nearby, and you pocket it.

speaker: (narration)
before: The third wheel's crew are children in school caps. 'It is a school activity,' says a banner. Nobody has rung the bell.
after: The third wheel's crew are children in school caps. 'It is a school activity,' says a banner, but nobody has rung the bell in years.

speaker: (narration)
before: You pull the lever, break the wheel's rhythm and get them off. They are very small and very proud and they will not stop saying 'Rollo sent you?'.
after: You pull the lever and lift them down one by one. They're very small and very proud, and they keep asking, 'Did Rollo send you?'

speaker: (narration)
before: This crew is free. They are lying on the ground, looking at the sky. It is the best they have felt in ten years.
after: This crew is free. They're lying on their backs looking up at the sky, and it's the best they've felt in ten years.

speaker: (narration)
before: The Pell plot is tended and quiet. Fresh flowers. The family comes every morning now.
after: The Pell plot is tended and quiet, with fresh flowers on it. The family comes every morning now.

speaker: (narration)
before: The iron gate is sealed with a notice: 'NO BURIAL WITHOUT A STAMPED PERMIT (FORM 27-B/6, FINAL APPROVAL).' You have no stamp. Widow Pell said something about a stamp, hidden somewhere in Grave Row.
after: The iron gate is sealed with a notice: 'NO BURIAL WITHOUT A STAMPED PERMIT (FORM 27-B/6, FINAL APPROVAL).' Widow Pell said a stamp was hidden in Grave Row, north of the permit office.

speaker: (narration)
before: 'Form 27-C requires Form 27-B.' 'Form 27-B requires Form 27-C.' 'It is a loop,' you say.
after: 'Form 27-C requires Form 27-B,' she says, 'and Form 27-B requires Form 27-C.' You point out, gently, that this is a loop.

speaker: (narration)
before: Every citizen shall run the wheels for six hours a day. The wheels never stop. The lights never go out. Your legs are not your own.
after: Every citizen shall run the wheels for six hours a day, so that the wheels never stop and the lights never go out. Your legs are not your own.

speaker: (narration)
before: Same as yesterday. Same as tomorrow. You may stop consulting the menu.
after: The same as yesterday and the same as tomorrow. You may stop consulting the menu.

speaker: (narration)
before: To the Crease. There is a smell of cooking down there. Real cooking. Nobody mentions it.
after: To the Crease. There's a smell of real cooking coming up this shaft, and nobody ever mentions it.

speaker: (narration)
before: Closed. Forgotten. Not on any map. (Try the south-west corner.)
after: Closed and forgotten, and on nobody's map. (Try the south-west corner.)

speaker: (narration)
before: Founded by people {villain} could not iron out. No dues. No forms. No smiling.
after: Founded by the people {villain} could not iron out. No dues, no forms, and nobody here has to smile.

speaker: Wren
before: Another one through the shafts. Sit. I am Wren. I was Royal Archivist, once. Now I keep the records this city is not supposed to have.
after: Another one through the shafts. Sit down. I'm Wren; I was the Royal Archivist once, and now I keep the records this city isn't supposed to have.

speaker: Wren
before: Maren sent word from {town} that someone might come. This is the Crease. We are the Wrinkles: the people {villain} could not iron out. We have tea and grudges. The tea is better.
after: Maren sent word from {town} that someone might come. This is the Crease, and we're the Wrinkles, the people {villain} couldn't iron out. We have tea and grudges. The tea's better.

speaker: Wren
before: He is in the castle at the north end, and he truly believes he is helping. That is the hard part. Talk to the streets. Each of them holds a piece of him.
after: He's in the castle at the north end, and he truly believes he's helping, which is the hard part. Talk to the people in the streets. Each of them carries a piece of what he did, and I want it all in the record.

speaker: Wren
before: The records say he began well. His first decree put a hot lunch in front of every schoolchild. Remember that. It excuses nothing.
after: The records say he began well. His first decree put a hot lunch in front of every schoolchild, and I want you to remember that. It excuses nothing, but remember it.

speaker: Wren
before: You brought me something from the streets. It goes in the true record, in ink, where he cannot correct it.
after: You brought me something from the streets. It goes in the true record, in ink, where he can't correct it.

speaker: Wren
before: Two pieces of him now. A man who needs to be right. A man who cannot bear to be disagreed with. I can almost see his shape.
after: That's two pieces of him now: a man who needs to be right, and a man who can't bear to be disagreed with. I can almost see his shape.

speaker: Wren
before: Three. He is afraid, you know. Not of you.
after: That's three. He's afraid, you know, and not of you.

speaker: Wren
before: Of everything that will not obey. A small, sad fear, for a man with so much gold.
after: He's afraid of everything that won't obey him. It's a small, sad fear for a man with so much gold.

speaker: Wren
before: All four. I have the whole of him now. He is not a monster.
after: That's all four, and I have the whole of him now. He is not a monster.

speaker: Wren
before: He is a man who made a list of everything he could not control, and made it illegal.
after: He's a man who made a list of everything he couldn't control, and then made it illegal.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: Hesper Dray. Nurse. Sit. Drink.
after: Hesper Dray. I'm the nurse down here, so do as I say: sit, and drink.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: Tea. Strong, bitter, unapproved. Drink while it is still three things the Ministry dislikes.
after: It's tea, strong and bitter and unapproved. Drink it while it's still three things the Ministry dislikes.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: The rifts? His hold is failing. Everything he forced together keeps coming apart, and he keeps stitching.
after: The rifts? That's his hold failing. Everything he forced together keeps coming apart at the seams, and he keeps stitching.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Shh. Keep it down. Old Fern. Composter.
after: Keep your voice down, will you? I'm Old Fern. Composter, which in this city is about the worst thing a person can be.

speaker: Old Fern
before: I turned this city's waste back into soil. Now that's 'untidy', and so am I. Criminally untidy. Worms in my hat to prove it.
after: I spent forty years turning this city's scraps back into soil, and now that's 'untidy'. So am I, apparently. I've got worms in my hat to prove it.

speaker: Old Fern
before: They shoved the rubbish behind the facade and called it 'Behind'. The land's sick. Nothing grows. Help me save what's left.
after: They swept the rubbish behind the facade and pretended it wasn't there. Now the soil's sick, nothing grows in the Reek, and I'm too old to dig alone. Help me save what's left.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Any luck? The heaps are in cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding. They're being rescued.
after: Any luck? The heaps are tucked into cellars and holes all over the Reek. They think they're hiding from the inspectors. Tell them they're coming home.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Oh. A visitor. Forgive me, I've forgotten how this goes. I am Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.
after: Oh, you've come to the door. Forgive me, it's been a long while since anyone did. I'm Widow Pell. My husband died three years ago, in his chair in the front parlour.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: I cannot bury him. Form 27-B needs Form 27-C, and 27-C needs 27-B. He has waited in his chair for three years.
after: And I can't bury him. Form 27-B needs a 27-C, and the 27-C needs a 27-B, so he's still in his chair, waiting, the way he always used to wait for me.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: I talk to him in the parlour. He was always the patient one. I'm not, it turns out. Please, if you can help.
after: I still talk to him in there. He was always the patient one of us, and it turns out I'm not. If you can help at all, please.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: The stamp, remember. Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where nobody official would look: somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads.
after: Someone hid the Stamp of Final Approval where no official would ever look: in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Rollo Spokes... foreman. Beefcake. Learned the wheels... in the Gainlands. Back then, a wheel stopped at night.
after: Name's Rollo Spokes... wheel foreman, Beefcake, out of the Gainlands. Back home... a wheel stopped at night... and so did the man on it.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Now the facade needs light... so we pedal. Free. Forever. We were told... it was cardio. My calves have calves.
after: Here, the facade needs lighting... so we pedal it. No pay, no end. They told us it was cardio... My calves have calves.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: My crews run six hours a day... for ten years. Nobody's told them they can stop. Somebody ought to.
after: My crews have pedalled six hours a day for ten years... and nobody's ever told them they can stop. Somebody ought to... somebody they'll believe.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Three wheels... pull the brakes. And that big cable by the east wall... feeds the facade. Cut it.
after: Three wheels in the Yards... pull each brake and talk to the crew. Then the big cable by the east wall, the one that feeds the facade... cut it.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: The crews won't stop... till somebody says it's all right. You say it.
after: The crews won't get off... till somebody tells them it's all right to. So you tell them... and mean it.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Hands where I can see them. Good. Chef Marlo. Once of the Market of the Four Paths. Now a 'Nutrient Distributor'. Recipes stay in my apron.
after: Hands where I can see them... good, no inspector's gloves. I'm Chef Marlo. I cooked at the Market of the Four Paths, once. Now I'm a 'Nutrient Distributor', and my recipes stay in my apron.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Three recipe cards, hidden in the quarter. And the dispenser: give it a good kick from me. Spoil it. Spoil it badly.
after: Three recipe cards, tucked away around the quarter, and then the dispenser. Spoil it for me, and spoil it badly. I've waited ten years to say that.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are too tall. You are too short. Your shadow is the wrong length.
after: Entry requires the Approved Visitor Standard. You are somehow both too tall and too short, and your shadow is the wrong length.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: However. The Standard has a provision: the Entry Examination. A card battle. Win it, and you are, retroactively, approved.
after: However, the Standard provides for an Entry Examination, conducted as a card battle. Win it, and you are retroactively approved.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: You again. Still too tall. Still smiling at the wrong angle. Ready for the Examination?
after: You again, still too tall and still smiling at the wrong angle. Are you ready for the Examination?

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: I have measured twelve thousand visitors. I approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. The rest, I will not say.
after: I have measured twelve thousand visitors and approved four. Nine thousand were sent home. About the rest, I would rather not say.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Height inspection! Stand against the post. Straighten.
after: Height inspection! Stand against the post, please, and straighten up.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Not that straight. Hm. You are one hair above regulation.
after: Not that straight. Hm... you are one hair above regulation.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: One hair. I will let it go. This time. Do not grow.
after: One hair, I will let go, this time. Please do not grow while you are inside.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Queue management. The approved queue is this queue. You are in it.
after: Queue management! This is the approved queue, and you are already in it.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. You are leaving? You have not arrived. Please arrive first.
after: Exit control. You wish to leave? But you have not finished arriving. Please arrive first.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready. Please have your exit interview permit ready. Please have a reason.
after: Exit control. Please have your exit permit ready, and your exit interview permit, and, if at all possible, a reason.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: Citizen 4471. I smiled incorrectly. Eleven degrees. The approved angle is eight.
after: I am Citizen 4471. I was brought here for smiling incorrectly. Eleven degrees, when the approved angle is eight.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: It was my wife's wedding. I had been crying. They corrected me.
after: It was our wedding day. I had been crying, the happy kind, and they corrected me for that too.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: I do not smile any more. Not at all. It is a strange thing, to forget how a face works.
after: I do not smile at all any more. It is a strange thing, to forget how your own face works.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Please. A burial permit is all we want: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval.
after: All we want is a burial permit: Form 27-B/6, stamped Final Approval, and then he can finally rest.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Find it, bring it to our family plot at the north end of Grave Row, and let him rest.
after: Somebody hid the Stamp of Final Approval in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. Find it, take it to our family plot at the north end of the Row, and let him rest.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: The stamp is somewhere in Grave Row, among papers nobody reads. Then the plot, at the north end of the Row. Please.
after: The stamp's in Grave Row, north of the permit office, among papers nobody reads. Then bring it to our plot at the north end of the Row. Please.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Here. This was his. He'd want a young person to have it.
after: Here, this was his. He'd want it to go to someone young, who'll use it.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: And something about the man in the castle. He schedules grief. Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.
after: There's something you should know about the man in the castle. He schedules grief: Thursdays, 3:00 to 3:05. Anyone who cries outside those hours is corrected.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Thank you, a hundred times. We're at the plot every morning. What I told you is in your journal: he cannot stand a sadness he did not schedule.
after: Thank you, a hundred times over. I sit with him at the plot every morning now. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he can't bear a sadness he didn't schedule.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull their brake levers... take the foreman's whistle... tell them it's all right.
after: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... three crews nobody ever told to stop. Pull each brake lever... and tell them it's all right, in plain words.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: They won't believe you. Say it anyway. And cut the big cable by the east wall. The facade's lights have lived on my crews' legs for ten years.
after: They won't believe you at first... say it anyway. Then cut the big cable by the east wall. Those facade lights have run on my crews' legs... for ten years.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews. Cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop.
after: Three wheels in the Transit Yards... free the crews, then cut the big cable by the east wall. Keep telling them they can stop... it takes a few goes.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Heard the lights flicker from here. Heard the crews sit down. The whole yard... quiet.
after: I heard the lights flicker from here... then I heard the crews sit down. The whole yard's gone quiet.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: And something about him. He made lateness illegal. A man who cannot wait for anyone.
after: One thing about the man in the castle... he made lateness illegal. That's a man who can't bear to wait... for anyone.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: Wheels are slow. Crews are resting. What I said is in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement, and disagreement is the one thing he won't forgive.
after: The wheels are slowing... and the crews are resting. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: to him, lateness is disagreement... and that's the one thing he won't forgive.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: And the paste dispenser by the east wall: spoil it. Give it a very bad day.
after: And the paste dispenser here in the quarter: spoil it for me. Put something in it that tastes of something.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. 'Some' of this, 'a bit' of that. Always a good recipe.
after: Three recipe cards in the Hungry Quarter, and the dispenser to spoil. You'll know my cards: 'some' of this, 'a bit' of that. That's how a good recipe reads.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Look at the stains. Look at the spelling. And that smell from the dispenser: cabbage. Real cabbage.
after: Look at the stains on them, look at the spelling! And that smell from the dispenser... cabbage. Real cabbage.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: I am crying. Let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.
after: I'm crying, and you'll let me. Here: my real recipe, the one I never dared write down until today.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: And something about him. He cannot taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.
after: And one thing about the man in the castle: he can't taste. Not food, not wine, not salt. He never could.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: I'm cooking again. Real food, real mess. What I told you is in your journal: he made everyone eat what he could not taste.
after: I'm cooking again, real food with a real mess. Remember what I told you, it's in your journal: he made everyone eat what he couldn't taste.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive.
after: Three compost heaps are hiding in the Reek, in cellars and yards and under floors, where they were told to wait. Rescue them. They're alive, whatever the inspectors say.

speaker: Old Fern
before: And there's an old seed in a jar somewhere nearby. Plant it in the Sick Patch, in the Reek. Nobody's planted a thing here in ten years.
after: And there's a jar of old seed somewhere in the Reek. Plant it in the Sick Patch. Nobody's planted a thing in this city for ten years.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Three compost heaps and one jarred seed in the Reek. Rescue the heaps. Plant the seed in the Sick Patch. Give it a chance.
after: Three heaps to rescue in the Reek, and the seed for the Sick Patch. Find the jar first, then give the seed its chance. It's waited long enough.

speaker: Old Fern
before: It took? It TOOK. A flower. In this city.
after: It took? It TOOK! A flower, in this city, after all this time.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Here. Take it. And something about him: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.
after: Here, take this. And one thing about the man in the castle: he's afraid of anything that grows without asking him first.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Weeds. Moss. Children. Anything that surprises him. I think that's the whole of him.
after: Weeds, moss, children. Anything that might surprise him. I reckon that's the whole of him.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Patch is blooming. Heaps are steaming. What I said is in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.
after: The patch is blooming and the heaps are steaming, untidy as you like. Remember what I said, it's in your journal: he's afraid of anything that grows on its own.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Good day! The weather is approved! The lawn is regulation!
after: Good day! The weather has been approved, and the lawn is exactly regulation!

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Good day! It is a very good day. It is the same day as yesterday.
after: Good day! It is a very good day, exactly the same as yesterday.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I have a permit for four more words. I wish it existed.
after: The bread is lovely. The bread is... (a fixed smile) I am only permitted to call it lovely. I would like, very much, to see some.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I had a name before. I think it started with a B. I am allowed to forget it. I am doing very well at it.
after: I had a name before. I think it started with a B. We are allowed to forget them, and I am doing very well at it.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different. I do not remember why. It sounds very tiring.
after: Isn't it lovely to be exactly the same? I used to be different, I think, though I cannot remember why. It sounds very tiring.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Seventy percent, minimum! I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.
after: Seventy percent cheerfulness is the minimum, and today I am at seventy-one! It is a good day.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody visits. Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile in case they do.
after: The Showcase receives visitors from all over! (a pause) Nobody has visited in six years. We still smile, in case they do.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Do you hear the loudspeaker? It plays the same thing every day. It has said my name once.
after: Do you hear the loudspeaker? It says the same things every day, but once, years ago, it said my name.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I tried to be spontaneous once. On a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.
after: I tried to be spontaneous once, on a Tuesday. I said 'hello' to a bird.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: Approved Hat Size: 1. I wear the one. It is a good hat. I do not know whose it is.
after: There is one Approved Hat Size, and this is the hat. It is a good hat, although I do not know whose it was.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: He is not here. He has never been here. The portraits are here.
after: He is never here, you know. He has never once come down. Only the portraits come.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: You try the front door. It does not open. It is not a door.
after: You try the front door, but it does not open, because it is not a door.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: It is a very well-painted rectangle on a wall. Somebody has painted a tiny brass knocker. You knock on it.
after: It is a very well-painted rectangle on the wall. Somebody has even painted a tiny brass knocker, so you knock.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: You try the door. It does not open. You peek through the window: it is a painting of a window, and beyond it a painting of a living room with a painting of a family.
after: The door will not open. Through the window you see a painting of a window, and beyond it a painted living room where a painted family sits.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: They are smiling. They have been smiling for six years.
after: They are all smiling, and they have been smiling for six years.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The door has no handle. The house has no inside. Behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.
after: The door has no handle, and the house has no inside. In the gap behind the facade there is just room for a ladder and a young woman painting the same window for the thousandth time.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: She looks at you. She looks away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.
after: She looks at you, then away. She has the face of someone who has meant to write home for years.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: You try the door. It is open! It is a closet.
after: You try the door, and to your surprise it opens. It is a closet.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: You can go in. You probably should not. Yet.
after: You could go in now. It would be wiser to wait until the city is back on its feet.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: The dispenser is spoiled. Lovely. But the paste comes from somewhere.
after: The dispenser's spoiled, and lovely it is too. But the paste has to come from somewhere, doesn't it?

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: The shuttered stall at the south-west corner hums at night. Stalls are not supposed to hum. Open its ration hatch and look. Gently.
after: The shuttered stall at the quarter's south-west corner hums at night, and stalls don't hum. Open its ration hatch and have a look down. Gently.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: The south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch. Whatever is down there, it will be very, very grey.
after: It's the south-west stall, the one with its shutter down. Open the ration hatch, go down, and shut off whatever you find. I'd bet it's very, very grey.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: I have kept one real onion in my apron for ten years. Tonight, I chop it. You may want to stand back. I will be weeping, and not only from the onion.
after: I've kept one real onion in my apron for ten years, and tonight I'm chopping it. You may want to stand back. I'll be weeping, and not only from the onion.

speaker: (narration)
before: By the last energy wheel, a ferret in pinstripes is timing Rollo's crews. The crews are lying in the sun. She is still timing them.
after: By the last energy wheel, a ferret in pinstripes stands over Rollo's crews with a stopwatch. They are lying in the sun, and she is still timing them.

speaker: (narration)
before: Beside the Sick Patch, a hare in groundskeeper green is measuring Old Fern's seedling with a ruler. It is an inch over regulation. She has written that down.
after: Beside the Sick Patch, a hare in groundskeeper green is measuring Old Fern's seedling with a ruler. It is an inch over regulation, and she has written that down.

speaker: Hortensia Clipwell, Royal Groundskeeper
before: Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now. The lawns, the hedges. They grow in whatever direction they like.
after: Out of regulation. Everything is out of regulation now, the lawns and the hedges both. They grow in whatever direction they please.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump. Sorting peel from shell, all day. Messy. You'll hate it. Good.
after: Granny Gristle needs hands on the compost rows down in the Dump, sorting peel from shell all day long. It's messy work, and you'll hate it. Good.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Just measuring. Lot of very tidy people in this city. Tidy is easy to measure.
after: Just measuring. There's a lot of very tidy people in this city, and tidy is easy to measure.

speaker: Kestrel
before: Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Going into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow the chalk, not the guards. The guards are worse at drawing.
after: Name's Kestrel. I scout for the Wrinkles. Heading into the city? There's an older way in than the gate. Follow my chalk, not the guards; they're worse at drawing.

speaker: Kestrel
before: There's an older way into the city. Nobody remembers it. That's the point.
after: There's an older way into the city that nobody remembers. That's the whole point of it.

speaker: Kestrel
before: Get inside and find the Crease: the manhole near the gate. Knock three times. Not two. Two is rude. Then ask Wren about the tunnels.
after: Get inside, then find the manhole near the gate and knock three times. Not two; two is rude. Wren's down in the Crease. Ask her about the tunnels.

speaker: Kestrel
before: You found them. Told you I'd be here. Didn't say where. That's the fun part. Here, you've earned this.
after: So you found the Crease. Told you I'd be around; I just never said where. Here, you've earned this.

speaker: Kestrel
before: You climb up past the walls. Nobody is watching this way in. Nobody remembers it. That is the point.
after: You climb up inside the walls. Nobody is watching this way in, because nobody remembers it is here.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: A queue of grey citizens, a grey ladle, a supervisor timing every scoop.
after: Grey citizens queue for grey paste while a supervisor times every scoop of the ladle.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Beefcake bore, Gourmand vents, Necrocrat signs, Refusemancer drains. The junction crew lifts the scrap. Every Garbage becomes muscle.
after: A Beefcake bore, Gourmand vents, Necrocrat signs and Refusemancer drains all meet here, and the junction crew turns every scrap of Garbage into muscle.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Vats the size of houses. Something in the third one is humming the national anthem.
after: The vats are the size of houses, and something in the third one is humming the national anthem.

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Behind a ration hatch: a real kitchen, a locked pantry and a badger in medals.
after: Behind the ration hatch is a real kitchen, with a locked pantry and a badger in medals standing guard over it.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: 'HALT. These tunnels do not exist. You are standing in nothing. I cannot allow you to have found it.'
after: 'HALT. These tunnels do not exist, so you are standing in nothing, and I cannot allow you to have found it.'

speaker: (narration)
before: At the end of the Vat Floor, behind a door with a hatch for rations, is a kitchen. A real one. Copper pans, a cold stove, and a badger in a medal-covered chef's coat guarding a locked pantry.
after: At the end of the Vat Floor, behind a door with a ration hatch, is a real kitchen: copper pans, a cold stove, and a badger in a medal-covered chef's coat guarding a locked pantry.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: ATTENTION! This is a restricted pantry! Those recipes are confiscated for the war effort!
after: ATTENTION! You are standing in a restricted pantry, soldier! Every recipe on those shelves has been confiscated for the war effort!

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: What war? The war on FLAVOUR, son. Every citizen fed the same, at the same time, from the same tap. Perfect discipline.
after: Which war? The war on FLAVOUR, son! Every citizen fed the same ration, at the same minute, from the same tap, and not one complaint about the seasoning.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Marlo says you can't taste it either.
after: Marlo says you can't taste it either. Is that why everyone else has to eat it?

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Taste is a weakness. Whisk formation! Golems, to the vats! Nobody touches my pantry!
after: Taste is a weakness, soldier, and I have none! Golems, whisk formation, to the vats! Nobody touches my pantry!
