speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Battle rations! Taste is a weakness. Paste is a strategy!
after: Battle rations, issue! Taste is a weakness, and paste is a strategy!

id: data/encounters/encounter_scripts.json::Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense/1/line::0
speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: Battle stations! This is not a drill, it is a soufflé!
after: Battle stations! This is not a drill, soldier, it is a souffle! Vats, FIRE!

speaker: Enforcer Captain Spotless
before: A SMUDGE. Is TREASON. ...It's on me, isn't it.
after: A SMUDGE is TREASON! ...It's on me, isn't it.

speaker: (narration)
before: The pantry door swings open. Shelves of confiscated jars: pickles, jams, a wheel of cheese with a ration number on it. Somewhere a vat coughs and stops.
after: The pantry door swings open on shelves of confiscated jars: pickles, jams, and a wheel of cheese with a ration number stamped on it. Out on the floor, a vat coughs and stops.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: I invented the paste because nobody could get it wrong. You can't burn paste. You can't oversalt it.
after: I invented the paste because nobody could get it wrong, soldier. You can't burn it, you can't oversalt it, and you can't spoil a regiment's dinner with it.

speaker: Colonel Cornelius Crumb, Director of Culinary Defense
before: You can't... taste it. I never could, you know. Not since the war that wasn't.
after: And you can't... taste it. I haven't tasted anything in years, you know. I thought if nobody could, nobody would notice that I couldn't.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: Then you'll learn. The Grand Chef is taking students. She starts everyone the same way: first, water.
after: Then you'll learn again. The Grand Chef is taking students, and she starts every one of them the same way: first, water.

speaker: (narration)
before: The great doors swing open, silent and perfectly balanced. Beyond them, a long hall, a red carpet and a smell of floor wax and lemons. Somewhere, a very long way away, someone is humming.
after: The great doors swing open, silent and perfectly balanced, onto a long hall and a red carpet that smells of floor wax and lemons. Somewhere a very long way off, someone is humming.

speaker: (narration)
before: 'Welcome,' says a quiet, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet. Please wipe your opinions. You are expected.'
after: 'Welcome,' says a quiet, polite voice from nowhere. 'Please wipe your feet, and your opinions, on the mat provided. You are expected.'

speaker: (narration)
before: 'THE SEED: Nature is untidy. Nature is inefficient. Nature disagrees with itself.
after: 'THE SEED: Nature is untidy, inefficient and forever disagreeing with itself.

speaker: (narration)
before: A seed, properly corrupted, can be made to agree with me. Plant in the Archdruid. Observe.
after: A seed, properly corrupted, can be made to agree with me. Plant it in the Archdruid, and observe.

speaker: (narration)
before: NOTE: it will spread. What grows will be orderly. I believe she will thank me.'
after: NOTE: it will spread, and what grows will be orderly. I believe she will thank me.'

speaker: (narration)
before: Guards in polished armour pour from the gatehouse. Not toward you. Toward her.
after: Guards in polished armour pour from the gatehouse, and they are not coming for you. They are coming for her.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Miss {rescuer_full}, I presume. Former junior Path-ologist. Absent without leave. Removed one item of laboratory property, which has been walking about ever since.
after: Miss {rescuer_full}, I presume! Former junior Path-ologist, absent without leave, who removed one item of laboratory property that has been walking about ever since.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Don't fret, Miss Vey. Your father is very understanding about these things. Take her home, gentlemen. The long way.
after: Don't fret, Miss Vey, your father is ever so understanding about these things. Take her home, gentlemen, and do take the long way.

speaker: (narration)
before: They are through a side door before you reach it. The door has no handle on this side. Of course it doesn't.
after: They are through a side door before you can reach it, and on this side the door has no handle at all.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: {rescuer}. Her name is {rescuer}. I never even asked.
after: {rescuer}. Her name is {rescuer}, and all that way I never once asked her.

speaker: (narration)
before: Solid gold, ten metres tall, polished until you can see your own worried face in them. They open before you touch them. That is the worst part.
after: Solid gold, ten metres tall, and polished until you can see your own worried face in them. They swing open before you touch them, which is somehow the worst part.

speaker: (narration)
before: Thousands of portraits of one man, in order. Each is a little taller, a little straighter, a little more perfect than the last. A story event.
after: Thousands of portraits of one man, hung in order, each a little taller, straighter and more perfect than the last. A story event.

speaker: (narration)
before: A knight made entirely of mirror plates, each of them showing only one face. It moves exactly like you. Then it stops doing that. (A battle.)
after: A knight made entirely of mirror plates, every one showing the same smiling face. It moves exactly like you, right up until it doesn't. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
before: A clerk at a tall desk, stamping everything that moves. Quite fast. Quite sad. His eyes never leave the paper. (A battle.)
after: A clerk at a tall desk stamps everything that moves, quickly and rather sadly. His eyes never leave the paper. (A battle.)

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: The head of the Ministry of Correction: white gloves, kind eyes, a ruler. She is very, very gentle. That is what makes it frightening. (Elite)
after: The head of the Ministry of Correction, with white gloves, kind eyes and a ruler. She is very, very gentle, and that is what makes her frightening. (Elite)

speaker: (narration)
before: A narrow back corridor where the castle's servants work, silent and very fast, in matching grey. They do not smile. They have stopped. (A battle.)
after: A narrow back corridor where the castle's servants work in matching grey, silent and very fast. They do not smile any more; they have stopped trying. (A battle.)

speaker: (narration)
before: The old portraits lean against the wall, face to the plaster. Behind the last one: a small bag someone left. 'In case anyone comes looking for the real one,' says a note. You take it and go back.
after: The old portraits lean against the wall, faces to the plaster. Behind the last one someone has left a small bag and a note: 'In case anyone comes looking for the real one.' You take it and go back.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: 'I never once asked what was wrong with them. Please. The door on the left. Go and look.'
after: 'I never once asked what was wrong with them. Please, take the door on the left and go and look at them.'

speaker: (narration)
before: You take the form. It can be revoked, you suspect, on a technicality. You go back.
after: You take the form. Somewhere in all this paper there must be a technicality, and you suspect someone will find it.

speaker: (narration)
before: You leave the seed where it fell. Out of its dome it looks smaller. Most things here do. You go back.
after: You leave the seed where it fell. Out of its dome it looks smaller, as most things here do once you get close, and you go back.

speaker: (narration)
before: The smile never changes. Neither, you realise, does anything else here. It is strangely restful.
after: The smile never changes, and neither, you realise, does anything else in this place. It is strangely restful, and that frightens you more than the guards do.

speaker: (narration)
before: Heavier than it looks, worth more than it should be, and covered in your fingerprints in a building that remembers fingerprints.
after: It is heavier than it looks and worth more than it should be, and now it is covered in your fingerprints, in a building that remembers fingerprints.

speaker: (narration)
before: There is always one more than there should be. You wave. He waves second. You are, for a moment, a little less afraid of him.
after: There is always one more reflection than there should be. You wave, he waves a moment too late, and for a moment you are a little less afraid of him.

speaker: (narration)
before: The sign is older than the rest of the castle. It is painted by hand. Under it, in different ink, someone has written: 'He meant well.'
after: The sign is older than the rest of the castle and painted by hand. Beneath it, in different ink, someone has written: 'He meant well.'

speaker: (narration)
before: A lectern in the middle of a round room, a book open on it, a pen beside the book. The ink on the last page is still wet. He wrote this today.
after: A lectern stands in the middle of a round room, with a book open on it and a pen beside the book. The ink on the last page is still wet; he wrote this today.

speaker: (narration)
before: A quiet reading room, a lamp, a chair. Someone used to read here. Rest and restore HP.
after: A quiet reading room with one lamp and one chair. Someone used to read here every night. Rest and restore HP.

speaker: (narration)
before: A single long shelf where the reforms are filed in order. Each is a little bigger than the last. A deck challenge: can your deck keep its footing?
after: A single long shelf where the reforms are filed in order, each a little bigger than the last. A deck challenge: can your deck keep its footing?

speaker: (narration)
before: A tall brass automaton that files, stamps and shelves. It has been told the archive is complete. It is very sure. (Elite)
after: A tall brass automaton that files, stamps and shelves. It has been told the archive is complete, and it is very sure of that. (Elite)

speaker: (narration)
before: A single book on a stand, still open. The last page is still wet. A story event: the moment you see him as he sees himself.
after: A single book lies open on a stand, its last page still wet. A story event: the moment you see him as he sees himself.

speaker: (narration)
before: You sit in the old reading chair. It is worn exactly where one person sat, every night, for years. Someone made the lampshade by hand. It is a little crooked.
after: You sit in the old reading chair, which is worn exactly where one person sat every night for years. Someone made the lampshade by hand, and it is a little crooked.

speaker: (narration)
before: Plans for wells. Plans for a school lunch. Plans for a bridge that was actually built.
after: There are plans for wells, plans for a hot school lunch, and plans for a bridge that was actually built.

speaker: (narration)
before: They are good. They are so good. You roll up the best and take it, with something in your throat.
after: They are good. They are so good, and something catches in your throat as you roll up the best of them and take it.

speaker: Royal Staircase Guard
before: No one climbs. The stair has been polished. By seventeen people.
after: No one climbs this stair. It has been polished by seventeen people, and I will not have it scuffed.

speaker: (narration)
before: Roads, rivers, four districts, a hundred thousand tiny houses. Every one of them is exactly where he wants it.
after: Roads, rivers, four districts and a hundred thousand tiny houses, and every one of them is exactly where he wants it.

speaker: Primm (standardization)
before: Do hold still. You are very slightly out of alignment. There. Better.
after: Do hold still. You are a fraction of a degree out of alignment, and I find I cannot leave it. There, that is better.

speaker: Primm (unraveling)
before: I only wanted it to be nice. For everyone. For their own good.
after: I only wanted it to be nice, for everyone. It was for their own good. Why won't anyone let it be for their own good?

speaker: (narration)
before: Each one is a little straighter, a little taller. By the last he is eleven feet tall, with no wrinkles and a smile that does not move. Under each: 'IMPROVED.'
after: Each one is a little straighter and a little taller, until by the last he is eleven feet tall, with no wrinkles and a smile that does not move. Under every one: 'IMPROVED.'

speaker: (narration)
before: In the ninth he looks so tired, and so sincere. You will not forget it. You see through the frame.
after: In the ninth he looks so tired, and so sincere, that you know you will not forget it. After that, none of the frames can fool you.

speaker: (narration)
before: You look at your feet. The carpet is red, and a little worn in the middle. That, at least, is honest. You feel a little steadier.
after: You look down at your feet. The red carpet is worn a little in the middle, which is the one honest thing in the room, and you feel steadier for it.

speaker: (narration)
before: The frame comes off with a squeal. Somewhere an alarm goes off, very politely: 'Please do not remove the improvements.' A hand-sized portrait falls and cuts your hand. The frame is worth a lot.
after: The frame comes off with a squeal, and an alarm goes off somewhere, very politely: 'Please do not remove the improvements.' A small portrait falls and cuts your hand, but the frame is worth a lot.

speaker: (narration)
before: Your face. Tired, dusty, crooked, entirely your own. It is the most welcome thing in the castle.
after: It is your face, tired and dusty and a little crooked, and entirely your own. It is the most welcome thing you have seen in this castle.

speaker: (narration)
before: A long white ward. Fifty beds. In each, a citizen in a grey gown with a small, fixed smile, looking at nothing.
after: A long white ward holds fifty beds, and in each lies a citizen in a grey gown with a small, fixed smile, looking at nothing.

speaker: (narration)
before: You sit by the bed and listen, for as long as it takes. It takes a long time. They tell you their names.
after: You sit by the beds and listen for as long as it takes, which is a long time, and one by one they tell you their names.

speaker: (narration)
before: You carry him out through a window. He is heavier than you expected. It costs you a little. It costs him far more.
after: You carry him out through a window. He is heavier than you expected, and it costs you something, though it has cost him far more.

speaker: (narration)
before: The first page is enough. Somebody will pay for this book. Somebody, one day, will read it aloud.
after: The first page is enough. Somebody will pay well for this book, and somebody, one day, will read it aloud.

speaker: (narration)
before: You sit on step two hundred and fifty, and look up at the very large clock. It has no hands. It has only a plate that says 'ON TIME'.
after: You sit on step two hundred and fifty and look up at the very large clock. It has no hands, only a brass plate that says 'ON TIME'.

speaker: (narration)
before: I have drawn up plans for six new ones. The Council has approved them. I did not sleep. It was wonderful.'
after: I have drawn up plans for six new ones, and the Council has approved every one. I did not sleep at all. It was wonderful.'

speaker: (narration)
before: It goes on. They are good. They are so good.
after: It goes on like that for years, and they are good. They are so good.

speaker: (narration)
before: He is not lying. That is the worst of it. You understand him a little, and you understand exactly what you will have to do.
after: He is not lying, and that is the worst of it. You understand him a little now, and you understand exactly what you will have to do.

speaker: Primm
before: Ah. A visitor. Do come in.
after: Ah, a visitor. Do come in; I so rarely receive anyone who has not been summoned.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Sorry. That's forest mud. I've walked a long way, and everyone I met on the way here was afraid of you.
after: Sorry, that's forest mud. I've walked a long way to get here, and everyone I met on the road was afraid of you.

speaker: Primm
before: Afraid? Of what? Of order?
after: Afraid? Of order, perhaps, or of comfort, or of the dreadful burden of being safe?

speaker: Primm
before: Of comfort? Of being safe? I have given them roofs, and hats, and rules.
after: I have given them roofs, and hats, and rules, and I have given each of them exactly the same amount of each, which is more than anyone before me ever managed.

speaker: Primm
before: Every one of them has a number. Nobody is ever overlooked. Do you know how few kingdoms can say that?
after: Every one of them has a number, so that nobody is ever overlooked. Do you know how few kingdoms can say that? I do. I counted.

speaker: Primm
before: Every unit, equal, in every way. Why must some of them be five? Why must anything be five?
after: Every unit was to be equal, in every way. Why must some of them be five? Why must anything ever be five?

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You took ten years from me. Whatever you took, it was not the part that matters, and strength is not control.
after: You took ten years from me, and whatever you took, it was not the part that matters. Strength is what you do with what's left, and strength is not control.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You took ten years from me. I don't know everything you took. I know it wasn't the part that matters.
after: You took ten years from me. I don't know everything you took, but I know it wasn't the part that matters.

speaker: Primm
before: Then they must be made the same. For their own good. Do you not see?
after: Then they must be made the same, for their own good. I had rather hoped that you, of all people, would see that.

speaker: Primm
before: You are not listening. Nobody ever listens. (a breath) Very well. If you will not follow my rules, I shall use yours.
after: You are not listening; nobody ever listens. (a breath) Very well. If you will not follow my rules, I shall simply have to use yours.

speaker: Primm
before: Your cards. Your plays. Your own deck, in my hands.
after: Your cards, your plays, your very own deck, held in my hands and played rather more tidily than you ever played it.

speaker: Primm
before: And you still beat me. How?
after: And still you beat me. I should very much like to know how.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You copied my cards. What I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.
after: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: And nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
after: And nobody files me under 'subject' ever again. No order you could write outranks treating people with respect.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You copied my cards. What I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.
after: You copied my cards, but what I do with them is mine. A name is a blank page until you sign it.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I'm not your subject. You don't get to decide who I am.
after: Copying a face never made anyone a cook. You don't get to decide who I am.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Nobody files me under 'subject' again. No order outranks treating people with respect.
after: Nobody files me under 'subject' ever again. No order you could write outranks treating people with respect.

speaker: Primm
before: That is not true. I made the wells. I made the roads.
after: That is simply not true. I made the wells, and I made the roads.

speaker: Primm
before: NO. No, no, no. The rules are PERFECT.
after: No. No, no, no. The rules are perfect. I checked every one of them myself, twice.

speaker: Primm
before: The rules ARE perfect. If the rules are not perfect then I have been... then I have been...
after: The rules are perfect. They have to be, because if they aren't, then I have been... then all this time I have been...

speaker: Primm
before: Everything is coming apart. Why is everything coming apart? I only wanted it to be nice!
after: Everything is coming apart, and I don't understand why. I only wanted it to be nice.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: 'The heart and the mind, son. You brought both. We are with you.' (Grandmaster Flex's Heart: Beefcake units get +1 power, and you gain 2 max HP.)
after: 'Strength is the heart and the mind, son, and you brought both. We're with you.' (Grandmaster Flex's Heart: Beefcake units get +1 power, and you gain 2 max HP.)

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: The Grand Chef, in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? No. Of course you have not.'
after: The Grand Chef, in a clean apron, ladle in hand. 'Have you eaten? No, of course you haven't. Here. Eat first, fight after.'

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: 'Ten years of sauce that tasted of nothing. Let us feed this kingdom something real.' (The Grand Chef's Feast: Gourmand units get +1 defense, life gain is stronger, and you gain 2 max HP.)
after: 'Ten years of sauce that tasted of nothing. Let's feed this kingdom something real again.' (The Grand Chef's Feast: Gourmand units get +1 defense, life gain is stronger, and you gain 2 max HP.)

speaker: (narration/UI)
before: Nobody stands beside you. The Paths are not free yet: their leaders are still behind wheels, behind sauce and behind paperwork. You step into the chamber alone.
after: Nobody stands beside you. The Paths are not free yet, and their leaders are still held behind wheels and sauce and paperwork and thorns, so you step into the chamber alone.

speaker: (narration)
before: The model lies in pieces. A hundred thousand tiny houses on the floor, all in the wrong places, and somehow they look better.
after: The model lies in pieces, a hundred thousand tiny houses scattered across the floor in all the wrong places, and somehow they look better.

speaker: Primm
before: ...It is over. The rules were not enough.
after: ...So it is over. I wrote such good rules, and they were not enough.

speaker: Primm
before: I did it for them. I did it for the people. You do see that?
after: I did it for them, for the people. You do see that, don't you?

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm not burying that in a jar. I'm letting it go.
after: You took my mother and father, and I can't even remember their faces. I'm not going to keep that under glass the way you keep everything. I'm letting it go.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: You took my mother and father. I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting it go anyway. Watch.
after: You took my mother and father, and I can't even remember their faces. I'm letting it go anyway. Watch me.

speaker: Primm
before: It was the mirrors. Wasn't it. I wanted a world where nothing could surprise me.
after: It was the mirrors, wasn't it? I wanted a world where nothing could ever surprise me.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: I'm not going to correct you. That was your way. Start smaller. Say sorry to one person.
after: I'm not going to correct you; that was always your way. Start smaller than that. Say sorry to one person.

speaker: (narration)
before: No crown. No perfect smile. Only a tired man kneeling above a very small kingdom.
after: There is no crown and no perfect smile, only a tired man kneeling above a very small kingdom.

speaker: (narration)
before: Somebody downstairs will pay for them. Nobody upstairs will miss them. That is the whole plan.
after: Somebody downstairs will pay for them and nobody upstairs will miss them, which is as much of a plan as you need.

speaker: (narration)
before: It is perfect. It is horrifying. Your face stays like that for a while, and the guards leave you alone.
after: The smile comes out perfect, which is horrifying, and your face stays like that for a while. The guards leave you alone.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Where is the Lab?
after: Where is this Lab? Where did you take her?

speaker: (narration)
before: He withdraws, bravely, at a run. You fold the memo into your pocket. Beneath the forest. Her father.
after: He withdraws, bravely, at a run. You fold the memo into your pocket, and two phrases go with it: beneath the forest, and her father.

speaker: (UI)
before: Leaving the Capital ends this visit. Town heals you fully. Nobody will ask for your exit permit. Nobody has a permit machine. The road is just a road.
after: Leaving the Capital ends this visit, and Town heals you fully. Nobody will ask for an exit permit on the way out; the road is just a road again.

speaker: (narration)
before: The doors of {villain}'s Castle stand open. The gold is flaking. A pigeon has built a nest in the crown above the lintel and nobody has asked it for a permit.
after: The doors of {villain}'s Castle stand open, and the gold is flaking off them. A pigeon has built a nest in the crown above the lintel, and nobody has asked it for a permit.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: You wake up on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray is writing on a clipboard. It says 'NOTES', and then, in small letters, 'finally'.
after: You wake on a cot in the Crease. Nurse Hesper Dray looks up from her clipboard as if she has been expecting you for some time.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: 'Fell over. We rolled you in. The fee is still yours. The tea is not free just because the kingdom is.'
after: 'You fell over, so we rolled you in. The fee's still yours, mind. The tea isn't free just because the kingdom is.'

speaker: (narration)
before: Now: some houses. A very tidy lawn. A lot of citizens who would like to go home.
after: Now: some houses, a very tidy lawn and a lot of citizens who would like to go home.

speaker: (narration)
before: The tears are sealed. The pigeons have moved in. The pigeons are staying.
after: The tears are sealed. The pigeons have moved in, and they are staying.

speaker: Wren
before: You did it. Sit. I am Wren: Royal Archivist, and for ten years the only honest record in this city.
after: You did it. Sit down a moment. I'm Wren, Royal Archivist, and for ten years I kept the only honest record in this city.

speaker: Wren
before: The Crease is just a cellar now. We are keeping it anyway, for the stories.
after: The Crease is just a cellar now, but we're keeping it. Too many true things were written down there to let it go.

speaker: Wren
before: The kingdom is mending, one argument at a time. It is dreadfully inefficient. I have never been happier. Take your time.
after: The kingdom is mending one argument at a time, and it's dreadfully inefficient. I've never been happier. Take your time.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Old Fern. Composter. Allowed to say it out loud now.
after: Old Fern, composter, and I'm allowed to say so out loud now.

speaker: Old Fern
before: The patch came in, the heaps are steaming and nobody's hit me in a week. Untidy and proud.
after: The patch came in, the heaps are steaming, and nobody's thumped me for it in a week. I'm untidy, and I'm proud of it.

speaker: Old Fern
before: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry. Won't. Waste of good water. Come back any time.
after: Smell that? Honest compost. I could cry, but it'd be a waste of good water. Come back any time.

speaker: Widow Pell
before: Widow Pell. My husband is at rest. I visit him every morning.
after: I'm Widow Pell. My husband is finally at rest, and I visit him every morning, the way I always meant to.

speaker: Rollo Spokes
before: We're lifting again. Real things. On purpose. Come and watch the crews. Bring a snack.
after: We're lifting again, real things and on purpose this time. Come and watch the crews, and bring a snack.

speaker: Chef Marlo
before: And chaotic. There is flour on the ceiling. I have never been so happy to have a mess.
after: And chaotic, I'll grant you. There's flour on the ceiling, and I've never been so happy to see a mess.

speaker: Captain Spotless
before: I do not measure anyone any more. I just stand here. Yesterday a man walked by at exactly the approved height, and I wept.
after: I don't measure anyone any more; I simply stand here. Yesterday a man walked by at exactly the approved height, and I wept, and I could not tell you why.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: I smile now, when I want. It comes out crooked. My wife says it is the best thing she has ever seen.
after: I smile now, when I want to. It comes out crooked, and my wife says it's the best thing she's ever seen.

speaker: Citizen 4471, later Aldous
before: Aldous. Crooked. I'm practising.
after: It's Aldous. Still crooked, but I'm practising.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I do not know the hat size and I do not care! It is wonderful to be alive.
after: I don't know the approved hat size and I don't care! It's wonderful to be alive.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I blinked just now. Twice. Nobody came.
after: I blinked twice just now, and nobody came to write it down.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The bakery is painted on. There is going to be a real one, as soon as someone learns to bake. I have a recipe. The recipe is: try.
after: The bakery's only painted on, but there's going to be a real one as soon as someone learns to bake. I have a recipe. It says: try.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: My name is Berta. I had forgotten. It was on the tip of my tongue for ten years.
after: My name is Berta! I'd forgotten it. It was on the tip of my tongue for ten years.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: My house is different from my neighbour's now. He has painted his purple. I am furious. I am so happy to be furious.
after: My house is different from my neighbour's now, because he's painted his purple. I'm furious about it, and I'm so happy to be furious.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I go behind the house and look at the wall, still. It is a good wall. It is just a wall.
after: I still go round the back and look at the wall sometimes. It's a good wall, and it's only a wall.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I smiled at a funeral yesterday. Nobody corrected me. It was a good funeral.
after: I smiled at a funeral yesterday, and nobody corrected me. It was a good funeral.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I will not smile at all today if I do not want to. I am enjoying it.
after: I'm not going to smile at all today unless I want to, and I'm enjoying it enormously.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The hedge is round. The hedge wanted to be round. I asked it. I did not have to submit a form.
after: The hedge is round because it wanted to be round. I asked it myself, and I didn't have to submit a form.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The loudspeaker is silent. I stood under it for an hour. I said my name aloud, myself.
after: The loudspeaker's gone quiet. I stood under it for an hour and said my own name out loud, just because I could.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I do not know what to do on a Thursday, now it is all of them.
after: Now that every day is Spontaneity Thursday, I don't know what to do with any of them.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: My daughter came home. With the little green hat. I have never seen a hat I loved more.
after: My daughter came home in her little green hat. I've never loved a hat more in my life.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I am not going to be polite today. I am going to be honest. Your hat is awful. I love it.
after: I'm not going to be polite today, I'm going to be honest: your hat is awful, and I love it.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I opened the door at the back. It was raining. I stood in it for an hour.
after: I opened the back door and it was raining, so I stood out in it for an hour.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The Showcase is not the best of all places. It is a place. It is mine. It is a good place.
after: The Showcase isn't the best of all places any more. It's just a place, and it's mine, and it's a good one.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I am going to go somewhere else. Just to see. Then I will come back, if I want.
after: I'm going to go somewhere else, just to see what it's like. Then I'll come back, if I want to.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: He was not kind. He was afraid. I think both can be true.
after: He wasn't kind, he was afraid, and for ten years none of us could tell the difference.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: I am not sure I forgive him. I am not sure I need to.
after: I'm not sure I forgive him, and I'm not sure I need to.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: He is gone. I looked away. I looked away for a whole minute. It was a very long minute.
after: He's gone, so I looked away from his portrait for a whole minute. It was a very long minute.

speaker: A Perfectly Happy Citizen
before: The closet is a closet. The sign says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, YOU DO NOT HAVE TO SMILE.
after: The closet is just a closet now. A sign inside says: IF YOU ARE READING THIS, YOU DO NOT HAVE TO SMILE.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. (a cough) The weather is no longer approved. It is just weather. It seems to be managing.
after: Attention, citizens. (a cough) The weather is no longer approved; it is just weather, and it seems to be managing on its own.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. The exits are open. The entrances are open.
after: Attention, citizens. The exits are open, and so, it turns out, are the entrances.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. All is not well. It will be.
after: Attention, citizens. All is not well yet, but it will be.

speaker: Percival Plume, Deputy Minister of Good News
before: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real. Please thank anyone who exists.
after: Attention, citizens. The Wrinkles were real all along, and they kept the true record. Please thank them.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Queue management. There is no queue any more. I am standing here out of habit.
after: Queue management. There's no queue any more, so I'm only standing here out of habit.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Nobody has told me where else to stand. I thought I might go for a walk. If that is... No. I am not asking. I am telling you. I think.
after: Nobody's told me where else to stand, so I thought I might go for a walk. If that's... no. I'm not asking permission, I'm telling you. I think.

speaker: Capital guards and clerks
before: Exit control. You may leave whenever you like. I am just standing here. It is a very open exit.
after: Exit control. You may leave whenever you like; I'm only standing here. It's a very open exit.

speaker: Nurse Hesper Dray
before: Still unapproved. Nothing's approved any more. Best thing that ever happened to my tea.
after: My tea's still unapproved, but then nothing's approved any more. Best thing that ever happened to it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Sit down, dearie. Word came from the Capital this morning, by way of a pigeon who was very rude about it.
after: Sit down, dearie. Word came from the Capital this morning, and you won't like it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Plume's men took a girl at the castle gate. The one who carried you out of the woods. {rescuer_full}.
after: Plume's men took a girl at the castle gate, the one who carried you out of the woods. {rescuer_full}, they called her.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I knew that face the day you walked in here. Her father worked in my laboratory, once. I never trusted her for a minute.
after: I knew whose girl she was the day she brought you to my door. Her father worked in my laboratory once, and I never trusted her for a minute because of it.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: I have been wrong about people before. Once. In 1987. It seems I've gone and done it twice.
after: I've been wrong about people before. Once, in 1987. It seems I've gone and done it twice.

speaker: Elder Maren
before: Back where she came from, I expect. Somewhere with glass walls and no windows. That's a door I can't open. Not yet.
after: Back where she came from, I expect: somewhere with glass walls and no windows. That's a door I can't open for you. Not yet.

speaker: Wren
before: We saw them take her at the gate. Four guards and a peacock with a speaking trumpet. We couldn't get close.
after: We saw them take her at the gate: four guards and a peacock with a speaking trumpet. We couldn't get anywhere near her.

speaker: Wren
before: Her name goes in the true record. Whatever else happens.
after: Her name goes in the true record, whatever else happens.

speaker: (narration)
before: The scale model cracks in half. Then the table cracks. Then, with the sound of a very large drawer being pulled from a very large cabinet, the castle walls begin to come down.
after: The scale model cracks in half, and then the table under it, and then, with the sound of a very large drawer being pulled from a very large cabinet, the castle walls begin to come down.

speaker: (narration)
before: Shopfronts topple. Hedges wilt into their own shapes. The loudspeakers cough once and go quiet.
after: Shopfronts topple, hedges slump back into their own shapes, and the loudspeakers cough once and go quiet.

speaker: (narration)
before: Behind the facade: houses, lawns and people, all of them a bit crooked. A child paints the new sign at the gate: PATHORDIA.
after: Behind the facade are houses, lawns and people, all of them a little crooked. At the gate, a child paints the new sign: PATHORDIA.

speaker: (narration)
before: The Beefcakes are late. The Necrocrats have brought a form. The Gourmands are overdressed. The Refusemancers smell, faintly, of compost.
after: The Beefcakes are late, the Necrocrats have brought a form, the Gourmands are overdressed, and the Refusemancers smell faintly of compost.

speaker: (narration)
before: The point was never to be the same. The point was the argument. Different Paths, working together.
after: The point was never to be the same; the point was the argument. Different Paths, working together.

speaker: (narration)
before: You are back in {pathordia}. It is mostly the same streets, but it sounds quite different: people are shouting at each other cheerfully, in every direction.
after: You are back in {pathordia}. The streets are mostly the same, but they sound quite different now: people are shouting at each other cheerfully, in every direction.

speaker: Grandmaster Flex, the Unbroken
before: Rollo's crews are lying in the sun. I told them rest is a rep. They believed me. Heart and mind, son. You used both.
after: Rollo's crews are lying in the sun, because I told them rest is a rep and they believed me. You used heart and mind both, son. That's the whole lift.

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: The sauce is gone from every stove in the kingdom. Real onions again. I have not wept so much since I was a girl.
after: The sauce is gone from every stove in the kingdom, and I'm cooking with real onions again. I haven't cried this much since I was a girl.

speaker: The Grand Chef
before: You did something worth signing, you know. Now sit. Eat. Eat a mess.
after: Sit. Eat. You did something worth putting your name to, and you look as if you haven't had a proper meal since.

speaker: Agnes Overdue
before: I think I am going to cry. I have wanted to for a very long time.
after: I think I'm going to cry, dear. I've wanted to for a very long time.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: Look at this crack in the marble. Something is growing out of it.
after: Look at this crack in the marble, child. Something's growing out of it.

speaker: Compostella, the Rotheart, and Archdruid Compostella
before: I am going to let it. It has earned the right. So have you, child.
after: I'm going to let it. It's earned the right, and so have you.

speaker: Primm
before: Your power has kept this kingdom lit for ten years. I have only been looking after it. Surely you can see that.
after: Your power has kept this kingdom lit for ten years, and I have only ever looked after it. Surely you can see that.

speaker: (narration)
before: The castle does not fall. It opens. Where the Model Room floor was, a stair of four colours winds down into the old heart of the Capital.
after: The castle does not fall; it opens. Where the Model Room floor was, a stair of four colours winds down into the old heart of the Capital.

speaker: (narration)
before: Cracked streets. Real faces. A boy he kept in a cell.
after: Cracked streets, real faces, and a boy he kept in a cell.

speaker: (narration)
before: Slowly, he understands how much he broke. The wells were good. The schools were good. He made one choice for everyone, and nobody will trust him with another.
after: Slowly, he understands how much he broke. The wells were good, and so were the schools, but he made one choice for everyone, and nobody will trust him with another.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Ah. You did it, then. The castle.
after: Ah. You did it, then, the castle and all.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Then I've two graves to finish properly, up in the city. Grave Row. Come by when you're ready. No rush. There never is, with me.
after: Then I've two graves to finish properly, up in Grave Row in the city. Come by when you're ready. No rush; there never is, with me.

speaker: Old Hob the Gravedigger (secretly Death)
before: Appointments. Let's see. You... hm. Not for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.
after: Appointments. Let's see now... you're not down for a good long while. Ha! Lovely.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Eight years. Gate stayed open. Every night. In case.
after: Eight years. Kept the gate open every night, in case.

speaker: Isla Brannoch
before: You're the one who knocked the castle over? Dad says thank you. That's what the 'Hm' meant. Thank you from me, too.
after: You're the one who knocked the castle over? That 'Hm' was Dad saying thank you. Thank you from me, too.

speaker: (narration)
before: Half the city has come. Nobody was told to. Wren holds the true record. Maren holds a pie she has forgotten about.
after: Half the city has come, and nobody told them to. Wren holds the true record; Maren holds a pie she has forgotten she is carrying.

speaker: Gatekeeper Brannoch
before: Notebook's full of her name. Started a new one. First page says yours. Spelled right, this time.
after: Notebook's full of her name, so I've started a new one. First page says yours. Spelled it right, this time.

speaker: (narration)
before: In the Capital's square, the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands. Nobody trips. Several people cry.
after: In the Capital's square the leaders of the four Paths clasp hands, and several people in the crowd begin to cry.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Only the worthy reach the top. Also bring water.
after: Only the worthy reach the top, they say. The worthy also bring water, if they've any sense.

speaker: Old Man Mountain
before: Mount Swolympus is open. Take the trail behind the station. Mind the thin air... never gets enough credit for being there.
after: Mount Swolympus is open at last. Take the trail behind the station, and mind the thin air up top... never gets enough credit, thin air.

speaker: The Ancient Spotter
before: A stone colossus sits at the summit with its hands out, palms up, waiting for a barbell. It has been spotting for a thousand years. It is very, very ready.
after: A stone colossus sits at the summit with its palms turned up, waiting for a barbell. It has been spotting for a thousand years, and it is very, very ready.

speaker: (narration)
before: A gallery of glass above the cells, a kettle, a cracked mug that says WORLD'S OKAYEST PATH-OLOGIST, and a corkboard of notes on one subject. The newest are a count of days.
after: A glass gallery looks down on the cells: a kettle, a cracked mug, and a corkboard of notes about one subject. The newest notes are only a count of days.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: They put me in your cell. My father thinks that's educational. With him it is hard to tell.
after: They put me in your cell. My father calls it educational, and the worst of it is that he means it.

speaker: (narration)
before: The only room in the Lab with a rug. On the desk, a journal in a neat, slanted hand. The last entry is ten years old.
after: This is the only room in the Lab with a rug. On the desk lies a journal in a neat, slanted hand, and its last entry is ten years old.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: He told me the King died of a fever. He told me you were a patient. I brought you soup.
after: He told me the King died of a fever. He told me you were a patient, so I brought you soup.

speaker: (narration)
before: The only room in the Lab with a rug. On the desk, a journal in a neat, slanted hand, and a child's drawing: 'For Papa, from {rescuer}.' The last entry is ten years old.
after: This is the only room in the Lab with a rug. On the desk lies a journal in a neat, slanted hand beside a child's drawing: 'For Papa, from {rescuer}.' The last entry is ten years old.

speaker: The Wanderer
before: Siphon is {rescuer}'s father. He held the door.
after: Siphon is {rescuer}'s father, and he held the door for them.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
before: Subject 1. And my daughter. Both of you home at once. I shall have to rearrange the schedule.
after: Subject 1, and my daughter too! Both of you home at once. I shall have to rearrange the whole schedule.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
before: You have grown. Remarkable. The draining has been very good for your posture.
after: Remarkable. You've grown at least two inches, and the time away has done wonders for your posture. I'll want measurements.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: You held the door, Dad. The night they killed the King and Queen. I read it in your own hand.
after: You held the door, Dad, the night they killed the King and Queen. I read it in your own hand.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: You told me he was a patient. I brought him soup. For years.
after: You told me he was a patient, and I brought him soup for years.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
before: Subject 1. You came back to us. You have grown. Remarkable, after so many cycles.
after: Subject 1, you came back to us! And you've grown. Remarkable, after so many cycles; I'll want measurements.

speaker: Dr. Ambrose Siphon, Chief Path-ologist
before: Assistants come home. Subjects too. Please, sit. This will only drain a little.
after: Assistants always come home, and so do subjects, it seems. Please, sit. This will only drain a little.

speaker: The Rescuer (Elowen)
before: You held the door, Dad. The night they killed the King and Queen. It's in your journal, in your own hand.
after: You held the door, Dad, the night they killed the King and Queen. It's in your journal, in your own hand.

before: I knew whose girl she was the day she brought you to my door. Her father worked in my laboratory once, and I never trusted her for a minute because of it.
after: I knew whose girl she was the day she brought you to my door. Her father worked in my laboratory once, and I held that against her for far too long. I was wrong to.

before: And nobody files me under 'subject' ever again. No order you could write outranks treating people with respect.
after: And nobody files me under 'subject' ever again.

before: One thing about the man in the castle... he made lateness illegal. That's a man who can't bear to wait... for anyone.
after: One more thing about the man in the castle: he made lateness illegal. That's a man who can't bear to wait for anyone.

before: Welcome to the Department of Necrotic Affairs, dear. I'm Agnes Overdue, front desk. I died at this desk in 1987 and I've been employee of the month ever since. Nobody else qualified.
after: Welcome to the Department of Necrotic Affairs, dear. I'm Agnes Overdue, front desk. I died at this desk forty years ago and I've been employee of the month ever since. Nobody else qualified.
